## 4. Determinism test suite

The determinism tests cover generation, kernel correctness and invariance, online serving, multimodal inputs, and LoRA shrink. The shared `utils.py` selects available attention backends and provides device-based skip markers. [tests/v1/determinism/utils.py:24-82]()

### Test coverage

| Test module | What the shown test code checks |
|---|---|
| `test_batch_invariance.py` | Runs a “needle” prompt alone to establish a baseline, then inserts it at a random position in mixed prompt batches and fails if its generated text differs. It parameterizes attention backend and RMSNorm implementation. [tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py:24-45]()[tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py:57-95]()[tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py:99-153]() |
| `test_batch_invariance_vlm.py` | Generates image or video inputs, compares single-request and batched token IDs and selected-token log probabilities, and exercises eager and default execution configurations. [tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance_vlm.py:17-55]()[tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance_vlm.py:58-108]()[tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance_vlm.py:110-138]() |
| `test_nvfp4_batch_invariant.py` | Compares baseline and mixed-batch NVFP4 generation, including token IDs, text, and selected-token log probabilities. [tests/v1/determinism/test_nvfp4_batch_invariant.py:26-44]()[tests/v1/determinism/test_nvfp4_batch_invariant.py:47-104]() |
| `test_lora_shrink_batch_invariant.py` | Checks LoRA shrink against a reference and verifies that a target row’s result is unchanged across several batch sizes. [tests/v1/determinism/test_lora_shrink_batch_invariant.py:27-39]()[tests/v1/determinism/test_lora_shrink_batch_invariant.py:42-99]() |
| `test_rms_norm_batch_invariant.py` | Compares Triton-based batch-invariant RMSNorm and fused add-RMSNorm against PyTorch numerical references across multiple batch sizes and hidden dimensions. [tests/v1/determinism/test_rms_norm_batch_invariant.py:36-76]()[tests/v1/determinism/test_rms_norm_batch_invariant.py:85-171]() |
| `test_matmul_batch_invariant.py` | Validates `matmul_batch_invariant` correctness against `torch.matmul` across 2D/3D/4D/5D shapes and tuned M-buckets. [tests/v1/determinism/test_matmul_batch_invariant.py:28-86]()[tests/v1/determinism/test_matmul_batch_invariant.py:114-136]() |

The needle generation test obtains its random seed and runtime limits from environment variables, including `VLLM_TEST_SEED`, `VLLM_NEEDLE_TRIALS`, and `VLLM_NEEDLE_BATCH_SIZE`; it uses a fixed `SamplingParams` seed for generation. [tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py:57-95]()

### What the tests assert

The tests use different comparison strengths appropriate to the target:

- The needle test compares generated text between the baseline and mixed-batch run. [tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py:110-153]()
- The VLM test compares token IDs and uses `torch.equal` for selected-token log-probability tensors. [tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance_vlm.py:58-89]()
- The online test checks token equality and compares each per-step log probability, reporting a bitwise mismatch if values differ. [tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py:178-190]()
- The LoRA shrink test compares the output of a specific row across different batch sizes using `torch.testing.assert_close`. [tests/v1/determinism/test_lora_shrink_batch_invariant.py:78-99]()

### Natural-language-to-code map: end-to-end test paths

**Diagram: User-facing inference scenarios mapped to determinism test entities**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Scenario["CheckDeterministicInference"] --> Offline["LLM.generate"]
    Scenario --> Online["OpenAICompatibleCompletionAPI"]
    Scenario --> Multimodal["ImageOrVideoPrompt"]
    Offline --> NeedleTest["test_v1_generation_is_deterministic_across_batch_sizes_with_needle"]
    Online --> OnlineTest["test_logprobs_bitwise_batch_invariance_bs1_vs_bsN"]
    Multimodal --> VLMTest["test_vlm_batch_invariance_bs1_vs_bsN"]
    NeedleTest --> NeedleOutput["baseline_text compared with needle text"]
    OnlineTest --> OnlineOutput["tokens and per-step logprobs"]
    VLMTest --> VLMOutput["token IDs and selected-token logprobs"]
```

## 5. Operational notes and limitations

Batch invariance is marked beta in the feature documentation. The tested-model list includes dense, MoE, vision-language, and sliding-window-attention examples; the documentation notes that other models may work but are not necessarily explicitly validated. [docs/features/batch_invariance.md:3-5]()[docs/features/batch_invariance.md:122-148]()

For tensor parallelism, observe the documented all-reduce size limitation before relying on batch invariance: a size not divisible by 16 bytes can result in different all-reduce paths as batch size changes. [docs/features/batch_invariance.md:162-163]()

For test diagnosis, the shared test utilities expose `TEST_MODEL` (overridable with `VLLM_TEST_MODEL`) and determine the available backend set from device type and Triton availability. [tests/v1/determinism/utils.py:24-41]()[tests/v1/determinism/utils.py:43-67]()

Sources: `docs/features/batch_invariance.md:3-5`, `docs/features/batch_invariance.md:122-148`, `docs/features/batch_invariance.md:162-163`, `tests/v1/determinism/utils.py:24-67`

## Purpose and Scope

This page gives a high-level view of how vLLM connects a model identifier and its Hugging Face configuration to a model implementation, runtime configuration, and supported task. It also introduces the main model-support areas without detailing their internal mechanisms. For details, see the child pages listed below. [vllm/config/model.py:150-168]() [vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py:46-69]()

**Sources:** [vllm/config/model.py:150-168]() [vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py:46-69]()

## Model Registry Architecture

The model registry maps Hugging Face architecture names to implementation modules and classes. The registry also imports capability queries for tasks and properties such as pooling, multimodal support, pipeline parallelism, and LoRA support [vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py:46-69]() [vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py:73-100]().

`ModelConfig` holds the model identifier, runner and conversion choices, tokenizer settings, and the `model_impl` selection (`auto`, `vllm`, `transformers`, or `terratorch`). Together, model configuration and registry lookup connect the requested model to the appropriate implementation path [vllm/config/model.py:89-109]() [vllm/config/model.py:150-179]().

For details, see [Model Registry and Architecture Detection](#5.1).

Diagram: Architecture Resolution Flow
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "Natural Language Space"
        HFArch[""Hugging Face Architecture String""]
    end
    subgraph "Code Entity Space"
        Registry[""vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py:_TEXT_GENERATION_MODELS""]
        ModelConfig[""vllm/config/model.py:ModelConfig""]
        ImplClass[""Implementation Module and Class""]
    end
    HFArch --> Registry --> ImplClass
    ModelConfig --> Registry
```

## Configuration Loading and Weight Loading

Configuration loading bridges model repository data and vLLM’s internal model settings. `vllm/transformers_utils/config.py` uses Hugging Face configuration utilities and maintains a model-type-to-config-class registry (`_CONFIG_REGISTRY`); it also defines aliases for Hugging Face fields that use different names across architectures [vllm/transformers_utils/config.py:13-50]() [vllm/transformers_utils/config.py:56-90]() [vllm/transformers_utils/config.py:112-167]().

`ModelConfig` incorporates the loaded Hugging Face configuration and related model properties. Architecture-specific conversion and validation connect those properties to the runtime configuration [vllm/config/model.py:31-53]() [vllm/config/model.py:150-168]() [vllm/model_executor/models/config.py:18-25]().

For details, see [Configuration Loading and Weight Loading](#5.2).

## Model Implementation Backends

vLLM supports native implementations and a Transformers modeling backend. The supported-models documentation describes native implementations under `vllm/model_executor/models/` and the Transformers backend as an option for model implementations available through Transformers [docs/models/supported_models.md:8-24]().

The registry supplies architecture-to-implementation mappings, while `ModelConfig.model_impl` represents the implementation choice [vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py:73-100]() [vllm/config/model.py:107-109]() [docs/models/supported_models.md:16-26]().

For details, see [Transformers Modeling Backend](#5.3).

## Purpose and Scope

This page explains how vLLM associates Hugging Face (HF) architecture names with model implementation entries, how model configuration and architecture-specific configuration registries fit into that process, and which capability-query interfaces are exposed by the model registry. The implementation references below are limited to the code excerpts available in the codebase. [vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py:46-69]() [vllm/config/model.py:13-15]()

Sources: [vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py:46-69]() [vllm/config/model.py:13-15]()

---

## Architecture Registry Overview

The model registry is defined in `vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py`. Its `_TEXT_GENERATION_MODELS` mapping uses HF architecture identifiers as keys and pairs each key with a module name and a vLLM implementation class name. For example, `DeepseekV4ForCausalLM` maps to `vllm.models.deepseek_v4` and `DeepseekV4ForCausalLM`; `LlamaForCausalLM` maps to `llama` and `LlamaForCausalLM`. [vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py:73-100]() [vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py:152-155]()

The registry module also imports capability helpers from `interfaces.py` and `interfaces_base.py`. Those imports show the kinds of questions the registry’s surrounding code can ask about a model, including multimodal support, pipeline parallel support, attention type, pooling-model status, and text-generation-model status. [vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py:46-69]()

| Registry Element | What the Available Code Establishes |
|---|---|
| `_TEXT_GENERATION_MODELS` | Maps architecture-name strings to module and class-name pairs. [vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py:73-100]() |
| `supports_multimodal`, `supports_pp`, `is_hybrid`, and related helpers | Imported from `interfaces.py` for model capability checks. [vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py:46-60]() |
| `get_attn_type`, `is_pooling_model`, `is_text_generation_model`, and pooling defaults | Imported from `interfaces_base.py`. [vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py:62-69]() |

**Example Architecture Mappings**

| HF Architecture Identifier | Module Entry | Class Entry |
|---|---|---|
| `LlamaForCausalLM` | `llama` | `LlamaForCausalLM` |
| `DeepseekV4ForCausalLM` | `vllm.models.deepseek_v4` | `DeepseekV4ForCausalLM` |
| `ChatGLMModel` | `chatglm` | `ChatGLMForCausalLM` |

These entries are declared in `_TEXT_GENERATION_MODELS`. [vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py:83-100]() [vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py:152-155]()

## Natural Language Space to Code Entity Space: Registry Lookup

An HF architecture name such as `DeepseekV4ForCausalLM` is the human-readable identifier used as a registry key. The registry associates it with the code-level module and implementation class names `vllm.models.deepseek_v4` and `DeepseekV4ForCausalLM`. Likewise, `LlamaForCausalLM` is associated with `llama` and `LlamaForCausalLM`. [vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py:92-100]() [vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py:152-155]()

The available excerpt shows these mappings declared in `_TEXT_GENERATION_MODELS`; it does not include the lookup function or its call sites. [vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py:73-100]()

**Diagram: HF Identifiers and Registry Symbols**

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph NaturalLanguageSpace
        HFConfigLlama["config_json_architecture_LlamaForCausalLM"]
        HFConfigDS4["config_json_architecture_DeepseekV4ForCausalLM"]
    end
    subgraph CodeEntitySpace
        RegistryFile["vllm_model_executor_models_registry_py"]
        RegistryMap["_TEXT_GENERATION_MODELS"]
        LlamaTuple["llama_LlamaForCausalLM"]
        DS4Tuple["vllm_models_deepseek_v4_DeepseekV4ForCausalLM"]
    end
    HFConfigLlama --> RegistryMap
    HFConfigDS4 --> RegistryMap
    RegistryFile --> RegistryMap
    RegistryMap --> LlamaTuple
    RegistryMap --> DS4Tuple
```

## Configuration Loading and Custom Config Registry

`vllm/transformers_utils/config.py` defines a lazy configuration-class mapping, `_CONFIG_REGISTRY`, keyed by model-type strings. `LazyConfigDict.__getitem__` returns an already stored class directly; when the stored value is a string, it imports `vllm.transformers_utils.configs` and resolves the named class from that module. [vllm/transformers_utils/config.py:112-122]()

The shown registry includes entries such as `deepseek_v32`, `kimi_k3`, `hy_v4`, `step5`, and `deepseek_v41`. These are model-type-to-config-class mappings, separate from the architecture-name-to-model-class mappings in `vllm.model_executor.models.registry`. [vllm/transformers_utils/config.py:122-167]() [vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py:73-100]()

`ModelConfig` imports `MODEL_ARCH_CONFIG_CONVERTORS` and `ModelArchConfigConvertorBase`, establishing a connection to architecture-config conversion. [vllm/config/model.py:47-50]()

| Configuration Symbol | Role Established by the Excerpt |
|---|---|
| `LazyConfigDict` | Resolves string values lazily to classes in `vllm.transformers_utils.configs`. [vllm/transformers_utils/config.py:112-120]() |
| `_CONFIG_REGISTRY` | Maps model-type strings to config class names or classes. [vllm/transformers_utils/config.py:122-167]() |
| `MODEL_ARCH_CONFIG_CONVERTORS` | Imported by `ModelConfig` from `model_arch_config_convertor`. [vllm/config/model.py:47-50]() |
| `ModelConfig` | Declared as the model configuration object. [vllm/config/model.py:150-165]() |

**Diagram: Model Type to Config-Class Registry**

```mermaid
graph LR
    HFModelType["HF_model_type_deepseek_v32"] --> ConfigRegistry["_CONFIG_REGISTRY"]
    ConfigRegistry --> LazyDict["LazyConfigDict___getitem__"]
    LazyDict --> ConfigModule["vllm_transformers_utils_configs"]
    ConfigModule --> ConfigClass["DeepseekV3Config"]
```

Sources: [vllm/transformers_utils/config.py:112-167]() [vllm/config/model.py:47-50]() [vllm/config/model.py:150-165]()

## Architecture Detection and Model Configuration

`ModelConfig` declares model-related fields including `model`, `runner`, `convert`, and `tokenizer_mode`. The `runner` field is described as the model runner type, with `auto` as its default; `convert` describes conversion using adapters, including adapting a text-generation model for pooling tasks. [vllm/config/model.py:150-179]()

The model registry imports both task/model classification helpers (`is_pooling_model`, `is_text_generation_model`) and capability helpers (`supports_multimodal`, `supports_pp`). [vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py:46-69]()

**Diagram: Configuration and Registry Entities**

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User as "User_Model_Path"
    participant ModelConfig as "vllm_config_model_ModelConfig"
    participant HFConfig as "HF_Configuration_Loading"
    participant Registry as "vllm_model_executor_models_registry__TEXT_GENERATION_MODELS"
    participant ImplEntry as "Module_Class_Pair"

    User->>ModelConfig: "Set_model_runner_convert_fields"
    ModelConfig->>HFConfig: "Load_model_configuration"
    HFConfig-->>ModelConfig: "Provide_model_configuration_data"
    ModelConfig->>Registry: "Architecture_resolution_boundary"
    Registry-->>ImplEntry: "Architecture_name_mapping_value"
```

Sources: [vllm/config/model.py:150-179]() [vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py:46-69]() [vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py:73-100]()

## Model Capability Queries and Interfaces

The registry module imports named capability helpers from `vllm.model_executor.models.interfaces` and `interfaces_base`. These helpers form the visible interface for querying model properties. [vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py:46-69]()

| Query Symbol | Meaning Indicated by Its Name |
|---|---|
| `supports_multimodal` | Multimodal support query. [vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py:46-60]() |
| `supports_multimodal_encoder_tp_data` | Multimodal encoder tensor-parallel data support query. [vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py:46-60]() |
| `supports_multimodal_raw_input_only` | Query for multimodal raw-input-only support. [vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py:46-60]() |
| `supports_pp` | Pipeline-parallel support query. [vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py:46-60]() |
| `supports_lora` | LoRA support query. [vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py:46-60]() |
| `is_hybrid`, `is_attention_free`, `has_inner_state` | Model-structure or execution-property queries. [vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py:46-60]() |
| `get_attn_type` | Returns or determines an attention-type classification. [vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py:62-69]() |
| `is_pooling_model`, `is_text_generation_model` | Model/task classification queries. [vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py:62-69]() |
| `get_default_seq_pooling_type`, `get_default_tok_pooling_type`, `get_score_type` | Pooling and score-related query helpers. [vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py:62-69]() |

**Diagram: Capability-Query Names to Code Modules**

```mermaid
graph LR
    ResolvedClass["Resolved_Model_Class"]
    Interfaces["vllm_model_executor_models_interfaces"]
    InterfacesBase["vllm_model_executor_models_interfaces_base"]
    ResolvedClass --> SupportsMultimodal["supports_multimodal"]
    ResolvedClass --> SupportsPP["supports_pp"]
    ResolvedClass --> IsHybrid["is_hybrid"]
    ResolvedClass --> GetAttnType["get_attn_type"]
    ResolvedClass --> IsPooling["is_pooling_model"]
    Interfaces --> SupportsMultimodal
    Interfaces --> SupportsPP
    Interfaces --> IsHybrid
    InterfacesBase --> GetAttnType
    InterfacesBase --> IsPooling
```

Sources: [vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py:46-69]()

## Speculative Model Architecture Checks

`vllm/config/speculative.py` declares literal types for speculative methods and model-type families, including `MTPModelTypes`, `DFlashModelTypes`, `DSparkModelTypes`, and `EagleModelTypes`. These types describe accepted configuration labels. [vllm/config/speculative.py:38-83]() [vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py:73-100]()

The `_validate_qwen3_omni_dspark` function validates a Qwen3-Omni DSpark draft-checkpoint contract. [vllm/config/speculative.py:86-102]() [vllm/config/speculative.py:146-181]()

| Symbol | Purpose Shown in the Excerpt |
|---|---|
| `MTPModelTypes` | Literal set of MTP model-type labels. [vllm/config/speculative.py:38-67]() |
| `DFlashModelTypes` | Literal type containing `dflash`. [vllm/config/speculative.py:68-73]() |
| `DSparkModelTypes` | Literal type containing `dspark`. [vllm/config/speculative.py:68-73]() |
| `_validate_qwen3_omni_dspark` | Validates architecture and configuration requirements for Qwen3-Omni DSpark draft model. [vllm/config/speculative.py:146-181]() |

Sources: [vllm/config/speculative.py:38-102]() [vllm/config/speculative.py:146-181]()

## Test Model Registry and Validation Metadata

`tests/models/registry.py` defines `_HfExamplesInfo`, a frozen dataclass for per-architecture test metadata. Its fields include a default test model, optional extra models, tokenizer settings, speculative-model settings, Transformers version bounds, input requirements, dtype, eager-execution settings, prefix-caching settings, remote-code trust, model-length and batch limits, and revision information. [tests/models/registry.py:16-120]()

The class also defines checks for Transformers-version compatibility and online model availability. [tests/models/registry.py:122-180]() [tests/models/registry.py:182-191]()

Sources: [tests/models/registry.py:16-120]() [tests/models/registry.py:122-191]() [vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py:3-5]()

---

## Summary

- `_TEXT_GENERATION_MODELS` maps architecture-name strings to module and class-name pairs. [vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py:73-100]()
- `_CONFIG_REGISTRY` maps model-type strings to configuration classes, resolving string entries lazily through `vllm.transformers_utils.configs`. [vllm/transformers_utils/config.py:112-167]()
- `ModelConfig` exposes model, runner, conversion, and tokenizer configuration fields. [vllm/config/model.py:47-50]() [vllm/config/model.py:150-179]()
- The registry module imports capability-query helpers for multimodal, parallelism, model-structure, attention, and pooling properties. [vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py:46-69]()
- Speculative configuration includes architecture-specific validation for Qwen3-Omni DSpark. [vllm/config/speculative.py:146-181]()
- The test model registry stores example-model and compatibility metadata. [tests/models/registry.py:16-120]() [vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py:3-5]()

Sources: [vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py:3-5]() [vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py:46-100]() [vllm/transformers_utils/config.py:112-167]() [vllm/config/model.py:47-50]() [vllm/config/model.py:150-179]() [vllm/config/speculative.py:146-181]() [tests/models/registry.py:16-120]()

## Purpose and scope

This page describes the path from model configuration and checkpoint selection to model initialization, weight loading, post-load processing, layerwise reload, and optional IPC weight caching. It focuses on the parser and loader entities that connect model configuration to runtime tensors [vllm/model_executor/model_loader/default_loader.py:55-183]().

Sources: [vllm/model_executor/model_loader/default_loader.py:55-183]()

---

## Configuration Format Support

The loader supports automatic selection between Hugging Face and Mistral weight formats. In `DefaultModelLoader._prepare_weights`, `load_format="auto"` checks for `consolidated*.safetensors` and selects `"mistral"` when those files are found; otherwise it selects `"hf"` [vllm/model_executor/model_loader/default_loader.py:147-183]().

| Format | Role described by the available implementation |
|---|---|
| `auto` | Selects Mistral weight format when `consolidated*.safetensors` files are present; otherwise selects HF format [vllm/model_executor/model_loader/default_loader.py:168-183](). |
| `hf` | A loader format handled by the default loader’s checkpoint preparation and weight iteration paths [vllm/model_executor/model_loader/default_loader.py:147-183](). |
| `mistral` | A loader format selected by the `auto` check for repositories containing consolidated safetensors files [vllm/model_executor/model_loader/default_loader.py:168-183](). |

### Configuration Format Detection Flow

The available loader code establishes automatic **weight-format** detection. The configuration parser classes `HFConfigParser` and `MistralConfigParser` belong to the broader configuration-loading path [vllm/config/load.py:30-60]().

**Diagram: Automatic weight-format selection**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["DefaultModelLoader._prepare_weights"] --> B{"load_format == auto"}
    B -->|"No"| C["Use configured load_format"]
    B -->|"Yes"| D["list_filtered_repo_files"]
    D --> E{"consolidated*.safetensors found"}
    E -->|"Yes"| F["Select mistral"]
    E -->|"No"| G["Select hf"]
```

Sources: [vllm/model_executor/model_loader/default_loader.py:147-183]()

---

## Configuration Parser Architecture

`HFConfigParser` and `MistralConfigParser` are the named parser entities associated with the HF and Mistral configuration formats [vllm/config/load.py:30-60]().

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["HF configuration format"] --> B["HFConfigParser"]
```

## HuggingFace Configuration Loading

`HFConfigParser` is the named parser for Hugging Face configuration [vllm/config/load.py:30-60](). The loader-side connection is visible in `DefaultModelLoader`: the class prepares model weight sources and selects a weight format, while configuration and model construction are handled through the model configuration and initialization interfaces [vllm/model_executor/model_loader/default_loader.py:55-58](), [vllm/model_executor/model_loader/utils.py:73-103]().

Sources: [vllm/config/load.py:30-60](), [vllm/model_executor/model_loader/default_loader.py:55-58](), [vllm/model_executor/model_loader/utils.py:73-103]()

---

## Mistral Configuration Loading

`MistralConfigParser` is the named parser associated with Mistral-native configuration [vllm/config/load.py:30-60](). The available loader implementation confirms a related checkpoint convention: when automatic weight-format selection is active, the presence of `consolidated*.safetensors` leads `DefaultModelLoader._prepare_weights` to choose `"mistral"` [vllm/model_executor/model_loader/default_loader.py:168-183]().

Sources: [vllm/config/load.py:30-60](), [vllm/model_executor/model_loader/default_loader.py:168-183]()

---

## Model Architecture Configuration Conversion

Model construction is coordinated by `initialize_model`. It takes a `VllmConfig`, obtains the `ModelConfig` if one was not explicitly supplied, and obtains the model class through `get_model_architecture` if no class was supplied. It then applies expert substitution and configures quantization when a quantization config is present [vllm/model_executor/model_loader/utils.py:73-95]().

For new-style model classes, `initialize_model` enters the current vLLM configuration context and calls the model class with `vllm_config` and `prefix`; it records reload metadata before returning [vllm/model_executor/model_loader/utils.py:96-136]().

**Diagram: Configuration-to-model construction**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["VllmConfig"] --> B["initialize_model"]
    B --> C["ModelConfig"]
    B --> D["get_model_architecture"]
    D --> E["model_class"]
    E --> F{"new-style constructor"}
    F -->|"Yes"| G["model_class(vllm_config, prefix)"]
    F -->|"No"| H["inspect constructor parameters"]
    H --> I["legacy-compatible kwargs"]
    G --> J["record_metadata_for_reloading"]
    I --> J
    J --> K["initialized torch.nn.Module"]
```

Sources: [vllm/model_executor/model_loader/utils.py:73-136](), [vllm/model_executor/models/gpt_oss.py:92-163]()

## Weight Loading Subsystem (`weight_utils.py`)

`weight_utils.py` provides utilities for downloading and initializing model weights, including shared file-lock creation (`get_lock`), atomic file replacement (`atomic_writer`), natural sorting for numbered checkpoint shards (`_natural_sort_key`), and optional ModelScope downloading (`maybe_download_from_modelscope`) [vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_utils.py:1-3](), [vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_utils.py:74-193]().

**Diagram: Checkpoint preparation and utility flow**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["DefaultModelLoader._prepare_weights"] --> B["maybe_download_from_modelscope"]
    B --> C["select local or remote source"]
    C --> D["select load format"]
    D --> E["weight_utils file filters"]
    E --> F["safetensors or PyTorch iterator"]
    G["get_lock"] --> B
    H["atomic_writer"] --> I["atomic file replacement"]
    J["_natural_sort_key"] --> K["ordered shard filenames"]
```

Sources: [vllm/model_executor/model_loader/default_loader.py:25-42](), [vllm/model_executor/model_loader/default_loader.py:147-183](), [vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_utils.py:96-193]()

## Layerwise Weight Reloading

Layerwise reload records model tensor metadata, restores layer tensors to the meta device, and wraps parameter weight loaders so that loading and processing can occur incrementally [vllm/model_executor/model_loader/reload/layerwise.py:44-145]().

**Diagram: Layerwise reload workflow**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["initialize_model"] --> B["record_metadata_for_reloading"]
    B --> C["capture_layer_to_meta"]
    C --> D["initialize_layerwise_reload"]
    D --> E["restore_layer_on_meta"]
    D --> F["initialize_online_processing"]
    F --> G["make_online_process_loader"]
    G --> H["track loaded elements"]
    H --> I{"layer ready"}
    I -->|"No"| H
    I -->|"Yes"| J["materialize layer"]
    J --> K["load and process weights"]
    K --> L["copy processed values to retained storage"]
```

Sources: [vllm/model_executor/model_loader/utils.py:96-103](), [vllm/model_executor/model_loader/reload/layerwise.py:44-145](), [vllm/model_executor/model_loader/reload/meta.py:41-61](), [vllm/model_executor/model_loader/reload/meta.py:120-153]()

## Weight Cache Daemon and IPC Loading

The weight-cache daemon keeps post-quantized, tensor-parallel-sharded model weights in GPU memory and serves CUDA IPC handles over Unix domain sockets [vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_cache/daemon.py:3-25](). `IpcModelLoader` initializes a model on the meta device and replaces its parameters and buffers with daemon-provided tensors [vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_cache/ipc_loader.py:68-92]().

**Diagram: Daemon preload and engine mapping**

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant D as "weight_cache.daemon"
    participant L as "DefaultModelLoader"
    participant E as "IpcModelLoader"
    participant P as "weight_cache.protocol"
    D->>L: "load checkpoint and initialize weights"
    D->>D: "process_weights_after_loading"
    D->>P: "publish socket and TensorEntry handles"
    E->>P: "connect using get_socket_path"
    E->>P: "request cached tensors"
    P-->>E: "CUDA IPC handles and alias metadata"
    E->>E: "map tensors or clone in copy mode"
    Note over E: "Fallback can use disk loading when enabled"
```

Sources: [vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_cache/daemon.py:89-169](), [vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_cache/ipc_loader.py:68-92](), [vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_cache/protocol.py:72-151]()

---

## Quantized Checkpoint Handling

Weight loading and quantization processing are separate stages. `process_weights_after_loading` reties embeddings when appropriate, traverses model modules, and invokes quantization-related handling [vllm/model_executor/model_loader/utils.py:139-167]().

Sources: [vllm/model_executor/model_loader/utils.py:139-167](), [vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_cache/protocol.py:92-114](), [vllm/model_executor/models/gpt_oss.py:44-49](), [vllm/model_executor/models/gpt_oss.py:85-89]()

## Purpose and Scope

Section 5.3 describes the Transformers modeling backend: a wrapper around Hugging Face models that vLLM can use when the model does not have a dedicated native vLLM implementation. The backend is composed from task-specific mixins for causal generation, MoE, multimodal inputs, embeddings, and sequence classification. It also adapts model layers and attention interfaces for vLLM execution, and applies structural fusers where supported [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/base.py:17-18]().

Sources: [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/base.py:17-18]()

---

## Activation and Backend Resolution

The backend’s model classes are defined in `vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/__init__.py` [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/__init__.py:1-197](). That file supplies distinct classes for text-only causal models, MoE causal models, multimodal causal models, embedding models, and sequence-classification models [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/__init__.py:128-185]().

## Class Hierarchy and Mixins

`Base` is an `nn.Module` implementing `VllmModel` and several vLLM capability interfaces: quantization, LoRA, pipeline parallelism, and Eagle/Eagle3 support [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/base.py:109-117](). Its constructor stores configuration objects from `VllmConfig`, retrieves the HF configuration and text configuration, and obtains tensor- and pipeline-parallel groups [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/base.py:122-139](). It also initializes bookkeeping for weight loading, fusers, attention fusers, and auxiliary hidden states [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/base.py:140-163]().

Task behavior is composed through mixins. `CausalMixin` adds the language-model head and logits path [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/causal.py:38-66](); the module also defines MoE, multimodal, embedding, and sequence-classification compositions [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/__init__.py:128-185](). Multimodal model classes are registered with `MULTIMODAL_REGISTRY` using `MultiModalProcessor`, `MultiModalProcessingInfo`, and `MultiModalDummyInputsBuilder` [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/__init__.py:144-148]().

**Diagram: Backend class relationships**


## The Fusers System

A fuser describes a detected transformation and how to apply it [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/fusers/base.py:27-34](). `BaseFuser.match` analyzes a traced module graph and may return a fuser; `validate` checks whether the transformation applies to a particular module and configuration; and `fuse` performs the transformation [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/fusers/base.py:40-59](). `RewriteFuser` updates a module’s attributes and binds a rewritten forward method [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/fusers/base.py:90-125](). `StackedFuser` specializes this approach to merge sibling projections and exposes mapping information for checkpoint weights and packed-module configuration [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/fusers/base.py:129-171]().

The base backend keeps fuser bookkeeping in `self.fusers` and tracks attention fusers by layer index in `self.attention_fusers` [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/base.py:148-154]().

The fuser implementations illustrate two kinds of structural optimization:
- `QKVFuser` matches three same-input linear projections, identifies their Q/K/V roles, validates compatible dimensions, and rewrites the forward to use a merged projection and split its output [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/fusers/qkv.py:37-98](), [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/fusers/qkv.py:100-162]().
- `RMSNormFuser` recognizes RMSNorm-shaped computation, including a native `rms_norm` operation and explicit mean-square/reciprocal-square-root forms [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/fusers/rms_norm.py:143-182]().

**Diagram: Fuser lifecycle and code entities**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Module["HfModuleClass"] --> Trace["TorchFxGraph"]
    Trace --> Match["BaseFuser.match"]
    Match --> QKV["QKVFuser"]
    Match --> RMS["RMSNormFuser"]
    QKV --> Validate["BaseFuser.validate"]
    RMS --> Validate
    Validate --> Fuse["BaseFuser.fuse"]
    Fuse --> Rewrite["RewriteFuser.update_attrs"]
    Rewrite --> Forward["RewriteFuser.fused_forward"]
    Fuse --> WeightMaps["StackedFuser.orig_to_new_stacked"]
    Fuse --> PackedMap["StackedFuser.packed_modules_mapping"]
    BaseBookkeeping["Base.fusers and Base.attention_fusers"] --> Fuse
```

Sources: [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/fusers/base.py:27-71](), [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/fusers/base.py:90-126](), [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/fusers/qkv.py:37-98](), [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/fusers/qkv.py:100-162](), [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/fusers/rms_norm.py:143-182](), [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/base.py:148-154]()

### QKV Projection Fusion

`QKVFuser.match` searches the traced graph for exactly three linear calls that share an input placeholder [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/fusers/qkv.py:52-68](). Where projection widths differ, it identifies the uniquely larger projection as Q and the equal-width pair as K and V [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/fusers/qkv.py:72-80](). It also checks whether a returned output projection is compatible [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/fusers/qkv.py:89-97]().

Before rewriting, `QKVFuser.update_forward` checks that the three projection calls use the same input and that another linear does not consume that same input [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/fusers/qkv.py:110-131](). It then inserts a merged call in a block that dominates the three projection calls and compiles the rewritten forward [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/fusers/qkv.py:133-150](). `validate` checks input sizes, bias compatibility, K/V width equality, and divisibility of Q and K widths by the attention head size [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/fusers/qkv.py:152-165]().

Sources: [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/fusers/qkv.py:51-165](), [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/fusers/base.py:126-171]()

### RMSNorm Fusion

`RMSNormFuser.match` uses FX graph structure rather than relying only on the source class name [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/fusers/rms_norm.py:144-182](). The matcher handles a native `rms_norm` operation and begins matching an explicit RMSNorm pattern based on squared input, mean, epsilon addition, and inverse square root [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/fusers/rms_norm.py:168-182]().

`TPAwareNormMixin` handles a tensor-parallel-sharded input when the normalization weight describes a wider dimension: it gathers the input, normalizes the reconstructed tensor, splits the result, and returns the slice for the current TP rank [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/fusers/rms_norm.py:107-140]().

Sources: [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/fusers/rms_norm.py:107-182]()

---

## `Base` Class Internals

`Base.__init__` initializes the backend from a `VllmConfig`, stores model, cache, compilation, device, parallelism, and quantization configuration, and obtains the TP and PP groups [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/base.py:122-139](). It initializes fuser and weight-loading state, rejects unsupported MXFP4 quantization names, patches the HF configuration, and decorates the model for `torch.compile` [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/base.py:140-174](). Model construction begins inside a context that marks model components and initializes without allocating normal device buffers [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/base.py:175-180]().

Utility functions support adapting HF modules to vLLM layers [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/utils.py:17-40](). `replace_linear_class` maps a selected parallel style to `ColumnParallelLinear`, `RowParallelLinear`, or `ReplicatedLinear`, forwarding dimensions, bias presence, quantization configuration, and prefix [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/utils.py:109-147](). `replace_conv_class` replaces supported zero-padding `Conv2d` and `Conv3d` modules with vLLM convolution layers and leaves unsupported cases unchanged [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/utils.py:150-188]().

**Diagram: Configuration and layer-adaptation path**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Config["VllmConfig"] --> BaseInit["Base.__init__"]
    BaseInit --> ModelConfig["ModelConfig"]
    BaseInit --> TextConfig["TextConfig"]
    BaseInit --> Groups["GetPpGroupAndGetTpGroup"]
    BaseInit --> Quant["QuantConfig"]
    Module["HfLinear"] --> ReplaceLinear["replace_linear_class"]
    ReplaceLinear --> Column["ColumnParallelLinear"]
    ReplaceLinear --> Row["RowParallelLinear"]
    ReplaceLinear --> Replicated["ReplicatedLinear"]
    Conv["HfConv2dOrConv3d"] --> ReplaceConv["replace_conv_class"]
    ReplaceConv --> ConvLayer["Conv2dLayerOrConv3dLayer"]
```

Sources: [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/base.py:122-180](), [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/utils.py:109-188]()

## Causal Language Modeling Sub-backend

`CausalMixin` combines `VllmModelForTextGeneration` with `Base` [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/causal.py:38-43](). It constructs `ParallelLMHead` on the last pipeline-parallel rank, optionally ties it to a `VocabParallelEmbedding`, and creates a `LogitsProcessor` using the text configuration’s vocabulary size, logit scale, and optional final-logit soft cap [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/causal.py:45-64](). Other PP ranks use `PPMissingLayer` for the LM head [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/causal.py:65-66]().

`CausalMixin.load_weights` wraps `Base.load_weights` to handle an `lm_head.bias` checkpoint entry: on the last PP rank it registers the bias under the configured load device and invokes the bias weight loader [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/causal.py:68-85](). `compute_logits` applies the `LogitsProcessor` to the LM head and hidden states [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/causal.py:87-89]().

**Diagram: Causal output path**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Hidden["hidden_states"] --> ComputeLogits["CausalMixin.compute_logits"]
    LMHead["ParallelLMHead"] --> ComputeLogits
    LogitsProcessor["LogitsProcessor"] --> ComputeLogits
    ComputeLogits --> Logits["logits"]
    PPGroup["pp_group.is_last_rank"] --> LMHead
    PPGroup --> Missing["PPMissingLayer"]
```

Sources: [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/causal.py:38-89]()

---

## Attention Integration

The Transformers package registers `vllm_attention_forward` and `vllm_mla_attention_forward` in Transformers’ `ALL_ATTENTION_FUNCTIONS` registry under the names `"vllm"` and `"vllm_mla"` [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/__init__.py:125-126](). Both functions retrieve the vLLM attention instance from the module’s `attn` attribute and call `check_sinks` before forwarding [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/__init__.py:67-78](), [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/__init__.py:107-108]().

For standard attention, `vllm_attention_forward` transposes and reshapes query, key, and value tensors for the vLLM attention call [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/__init__.py:79-91](). When the value head dimension is smaller than the query/key head dimension, it pads the value before the call and trims the output afterward [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/__init__.py:87-94](). The MLA wrapper reshapes query, compressed key/value, and positional key tensors and supplies the output shape to the vLLM attention instance [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/__init__.py:107-121]().

The `check_sinks` guard raises an error if the HF attention module supplies `s_aux` but the vLLM attention instance does not report `has_sink` [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/__init__.py:47-64]().

Sources: [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/__init__.py:46-125]()

---

## Mixture of Experts (MoE) Support

The MoE mixin module defines `TransformersMoERunner`, a `MoERunner` subclass registered as the pluggable layer `"transformers_fused_moe"` [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/moe.py:62-65](). Its `forward` accepts the Transformers expert-call signature, converts `topk_ids` and `topk_weights` to the expected dtypes, and invokes the registered `transformers_moe_forward` custom operator [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/moe.py:72-90]().

The custom operator uses the active `ForwardContext` to locate the layer in `no_compile_layers`, stores the routing IDs in that layer’s `TransformersMoEState`, and invokes the runner’s underlying forward path [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/moe.py:100-110](). The fake implementation returns an empty tensor shaped like the hidden states [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/moe.py:113-119]().

Routing can use IDs already computed by the HF block (`_hf_topk_router_precomputed`) or call a Transformers gate to obtain weights and IDs (`_hf_topk_router`) [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/moe.py:131-165](). In the precomputed path, if the number of routing IDs differs from the local hidden-state count, the code gathers IDs across the expert-parallel or data-parallel group [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/moe.py:144-153]().

`TransformersRoutedExperts.get_expert_mapping` extends the base expert mapping with both common projection names and Mixtral-style `w1`, `w2`, and `w3` names [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/moe.py:172-185]().

**Diagram: Transformers MoE routing handoff**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    HFExpertsForward["HfExpertsForward"] --> TransformersMoERunner["TransformersMoERunner.forward"]
    TransformersMoERunner --> CustomOp["torch.ops.vllm.transformers_moe_forward"]
    CustomOp --> ForwardContext["get_forward_context"]
    ForwardContext --> Layer["no_compile_layers[layer_name]"]
    Layer --> State["TransformersMoEState.topk_ids"]
    Layer --> RunnerForward["_forward_super"]
    State --> PrecomputedRouter["_hf_topk_router_precomputed"]
    Gate["_hf_topk_router"] --> RouterResult["topk_weights and topk_ids"]
    PrecomputedRouter --> RouterResult
    RouterResult --> RoutedExperts["TransformersRoutedExperts"]
```

Sources: [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/moe.py:54-185]()

---

## Multimodal Sub-backend

`MultiModalMixin` is the Transformers backend mixin for multimodal models [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/multimodal.py:17-56](). Concrete multimodal classes are registered with `MULTIMODAL_REGISTRY` using `MultiModalProcessor`, `MultiModalProcessingInfo`, and `MultiModalDummyInputsBuilder` [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/__init__.py:144-148]().

`MultiModalProcessingInfo` detects whether the HF processor exposes audio, image, or video processing [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/multimodal.py:96-160](). Video support additionally checks the Transformers version and whether the processor can count video tokens [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/multimodal.py:113-134](). For audio, it obtains the target sampling rate from the processor when available and otherwise uses 16 kHz [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/multimodal.py:162-166](); `get_data_parser` constructs a `MultiModalDataParser` with the applicable sampling rate, video metadata setting, and expected hidden size [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/multimodal.py:168-173]().

**Diagram: Multimodal capability detection and parser setup**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    HFProcessor["get_hf_processor"] --> AudioCheck["_get_audio_processor"]
    HFProcessor --> ImageCheck["_is_image_model"]
    HFProcessor --> VideoCheck["_is_video_model"]
    AudioCheck --> Modalities["_get_supported_modalities"]
    ImageCheck --> Modalities
    VideoCheck --> Modalities
    Modalities --> Parser["get_data_parser"]
    Parser --> DataParser["MultiModalDataParser"]
    AudioCheck --> SamplingRate["_get_audio_sampling_rate"]
    SamplingRate --> Parser
    VideoCheck --> VideoMetadata["_video_needs_metadata"]
    VideoMetadata --> Parser
```

Sources: [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/multimodal.py:96-173]()

---

## Pooling and Sequence-Classification Sub-backends

The Transformers package defines embedding and sequence-classification model classes by composing `EmbeddingMixin` or `SequenceClassificationMixin` with other backend mixins [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/__init__.py:35-38](), [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/__init__.py:161-193](). These compositions support standard, MoE, and multimodal architectures [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/__init__.py:161-193]().

Sources: [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/__init__.py:35-38](), [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/__init__.py:161-193]()

## Backend Tests

The backend tests verify that selected models are using the Transformers backend and compare greedy-generation log probabilities against a reference runner [tests/models/transformers/test_backend.py:72-121](). The test helper also checks expected counts of fused linear modules and vLLM `Attention` instances [tests/models/transformers/test_backend.py:96-106](). Test cases cover causal models, custom-code models, and MoE models [tests/models/transformers/test_backend.py:124-148]().

Additional tests exercise hybrid attention, attention sinks, and MLA [tests/models/transformers/test_backend.py:150-205](). Fuser unit tests provide coverage for linear pattern matching and RMSNorm pattern matching [tests/models/transformers/fusers/test_linear.py:1-30](), [tests/models/transformers/fusers/test_rms_norm.py:1-15]().

Sources: [tests/models/transformers/test_backend.py:59-205](), [tests/models/transformers/fusers/test_linear.py:1-30](), [tests/models/transformers/fusers/test_rms_norm.py:1-15]()

---

## Summary

The Transformers backend integrates Hugging Face models into vLLM via a shared `Base` class and task-specific mixins [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/base.py:109-117](), [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/__init__.py:128-185](). Causal models supply parallel LM heads and logit processors [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/causal.py:38-66](); MoE models bridge routing into vLLM's MoE runner via custom operators [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/moe.py:54-111](); and multimodal models detect modalities and configure custom processors [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/multimodal.py:96-173](). The fusers system optimizes execution through QKV projection fusion and RMSNorm replacement [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/fusers/qkv.py:37-162](), [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/fusers/rms_norm.py:107-182]().

Sources: [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/base.py:109-179](), [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/causal.py:38-89](), [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/moe.py:54-165](), [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/multimodal.py:96-173](), [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/__init__.py:46-185](), [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/fusers/base.py:27-126](), [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/fusers/qkv.py:37-162](), [vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/fusers/rms_norm.py:107-182]()

## Purpose and Scope

This page describes the multimodal model interfaces and implementation patterns visible in the supplied code excerpts. It covers the `SupportsMultiModal` interface, selected vision-language and omni implementations, encoder CUDA Graph support, and how these concepts connect to code entities. The requested model-family scope also includes LLaVA, Pixtral, Whisper, Voxtral, and Ultravox; the excerpts supplied here do not include their implementation files, so this page does not infer their internal behavior.

Sources: [vllm/model_executor/models/interfaces.py:152-215]() [vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_vl.py:25-25]() [vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_omni_moe_thinker.py:23-23]()

## Model Architecture and Interfaces

### The `SupportsMultiModal` Interface

`SupportsMultiModal` is a runtime-checkable protocol for multimodal models. It extends `SupportsMultiModalEmbeddings`, whose documented embedding output forms are a list or tuple of 2D tensors, one per multimodal item, or a single 3D tensor with items grouped in the batch dimension. The protocol declares `supports_multimodal` and related capability flags; `supports_multimodal_raw_input_only` is documented as indicating raw-form processing rather than embedding inputs. The helper `_require_is_multimodal` raises an error when its `is_multimodal` argument is absent. [vllm/model_executor/models/interfaces.py:77-84]() [vllm/model_executor/models/interfaces.py:124-136]() [vllm/model_executor/models/interfaces.py:152-215]()

| Interface or type | Role |
|---|---|
| `SupportsMultiModalEmbeddings` | Protocol for models that can merge external multimodal embeddings. [vllm/model_executor/models/interfaces.py:152-175]() |
| `SupportsMultiModal` | Multimodal model protocol, including capability flags. [vllm/model_executor/models/interfaces.py:177-215]() |
| `MultiModalEmbeddings` | Type alias for the supported tensor collection forms. [vllm/model_executor/models/interfaces.py:77-84]() |
| `SupportsEncoderCudaGraph` | Model opt-in protocol identified in the encoder CUDA Graph design. [docs/design/cuda_graphs_multimodal.md:48-55]() |
| `SupportsTranscription` | Interface imported by the Qwen3-Omni-Moe thinker implementation. [vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_omni_moe_thinker.py:93-101]() |

**Interface relationship: protocol names to code entities**

```mermaid

    }

```

## Data Flow: From Input to Embeddings

The model files show a recurring division of responsibilities: multimodal inputs and processing abstractions describe parsed items and prompt updates, while model implementations define modality-specific input schemas and model components. For example, the Qwen3-VL implementation imports `MultiModalDataDict`, `MultiModalFeatureSpec`, `BaseMultiModalProcessor`, and `PromptReplacement`; the Qwen2.5-VL implementation defines image pixel and embedding input schemas. [vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_vl.py:63-102]() [vllm/model_executor/models/qwen2_5_vl.py:168-206]()

## Encoder CUDA Graphs

Encoder CUDA Graph capture is separate from decoder CUDA Graph capture; the design document states that both can be enabled simultaneously. `EncoderCudaGraphManager` manages capture, replay, greedy packing, and data-parallel execution. Models opt in through `SupportsEncoderCudaGraph`, and `EncoderItemSpec` describes an encoder input item and its output token count. [docs/design/cuda_graphs_multimodal.md:1-8]() [docs/design/cuda_graphs_multimodal.md:48-55]()

Capture uses token-budget levels with associated graph and I/O buffers. The design document describes user-specified budgets through `encoder_cudagraph_token_budgets` and separate paths for multi-path encoders. [docs/design/cuda_graphs_multimodal.md:57-78]() The listed supported architectures include Qwen2-VL, Qwen2.5-VL, Qwen3-VL, Gemma4, GLM-4.1V/4.6V-Flash, Kimi-VL, MiniCPM-V variants, and Nemotron-VL. [docs/design/cuda_graphs_multimodal.md:10-33]() [tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_vit_cudagraph.py:192-200]()

Sources: [docs/design/cuda_graphs_multimodal.md:1-8]() [docs/design/cuda_graphs_multimodal.md:48-78]() [docs/design/cuda_graphs_multimodal.md:10-33]() [tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_vit_cudagraph.py:192-200]()

## Key Implementation Details

### Multimodal Embedding Merge

`MultiModalEmbeddings` represents multimodal embedding outputs as a list, tuple, or tensor. The supplied model files import `_merge_multimodal_embeddings`, including Qwen3-VL and Qwen3-Omni-Moe thinker. The helper’s definition and full merge semantics are not included in the supplied excerpts, so this page does not specify its internal scatter or masking behavior. [vllm/model_executor/models/interfaces.py:77-84]() [vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_vl.py:154-160]() [vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_omni_moe_thinker.py:119-124]()

### Qwen3-VL Bilinear Position-Embedding Kernel

The Qwen3-VL file labels a Triton kernel section for fused bilinear position-embedding interpolation and defines `_bilinear_pos_embed_kernel` when Triton is available. The comments describe the kernel as combining interpolation and spatial-merge reorder into one output suitable for addition to patch embeddings. ## Summary

The supplied code establishes `SupportsMultiModal` and `SupportsMultiModalEmbeddings` as protocol-level interfaces, with model-specific input schemas and processors represented in the Qwen-VL, GLM4, Gemma4, and omni implementations. The encoder CUDA Graph design provides a separate capture/replay mechanism for supported encoders. Implementation details for several requested families—including LLaVA, Pixtral, standalone Whisper, Voxtral, and Ultravox—are not present in the supplied excerpts and are intentionally left unspecified. [vllm/model_executor/models/interfaces.py:152-215]() [docs/design/cuda_graphs_multimodal.md:48-55]() [vllm/model_executor/models/qwen2_5_vl.py:168-206]() [vllm/model_executor/models/glm4_1v.py:144-195]() [vllm/model_executor/models/gemma4_mm.py:3-15]()

## Purpose and Scope

This page follows multimodal request data from its public input representation through parsing and model-specific processing, media decoding, and encoder execution. It covers `MultiModalDataDict`, modality item abstractions, the multimodal processor framework, video-loader registration and audio decoding, processor and encoder caching concepts, prompt updates, and chat-message input formats. [docs/features/multimodal_inputs.md:16-22]() [vllm/multimodal/parse.py:22-39]() [vllm/multimodal/processing/processor.py:34-55]()

**Sources:** [docs/features/multimodal_inputs.md:16-22]() [vllm/multimodal/parse.py:22-39]() [vllm/multimodal/processing/processor.py:34-55]()

## Chat Message Multimodal Integration and Parsing

The public input path supports multimodal data in two related forms: a prompt paired with `multi_modal_data`, and chat messages whose content includes text and media items. The offline-input documentation describes `multi_modal_data` as a dictionary following the `MultiModalDataDict` schema. Its chat examples show content parts for image URLs, PIL images, precomputed image embeddings, and text; video can also be represented in chat as a sequence of image-frame content parts. [docs/features/multimodal_inputs.md:16-22]() [docs/features/multimodal_inputs.md:106-152]() [docs/features/multimodal_inputs.md:154-186]()

In the processing layer, `MultiModalDataParser` converts modality data into typed modality-item collections. `ModalityDataItems` provides a common interface for counting and retrieving items, plus separate methods for data passed to a Hugging Face processor and data passed directly to the model. [vllm/multimodal/parse.py:60-112]() [vllm/model_executor/models/voxtral.py:41-45]()

### Supported Content Forms

| Chat or request content | Role in the input |
|---|---|
| `image_url` | Supplies an image by URL. [docs/features/multimodal_inputs.md:126-129]() |
| `image_pil` | Supplies an image as a PIL object. [docs/features/multimodal_inputs.md:130-133]() |
| `image_embeds` | Supplies precomputed image embeddings. [docs/features/multimodal_inputs.md:134-137]() |
| `text` | Supplies ordinary text alongside multimodal content. [docs/features/multimodal_inputs.md:138-141]() |
| Video frames represented as `image_url` items | Represents a video as a sequence of frame images in the documented chat example. [docs/features/multimodal_inputs.md:154-186]() |
| `multi_modal_data` | Carries modality-keyed data alongside a prompt. [docs/features/multimodal_inputs.md:16-22]() |

The supported chat examples and offline prompt form are documented in the multimodal-input guide. [docs/features/multimodal_inputs.md:16-22]() [docs/features/multimodal_inputs.md:106-152]() [docs/features/multimodal_inputs.md:154-186]()

## `MultiModalDataDict` and Multimodal Input Types

`MultiModalDataDict` is the modality-keyed request-data type imported by the parser from `vllm.inputs`. The parser module also defines `ModalityDataItems`, a generic abstraction that stores data and its modality name, exposes `get_count`, `get`, `get_all`, and separates processor input data from model passthrough data. [vllm/multimodal/parse.py:22-39]() [vllm/multimodal/parse.py:60-112]()

`ProcessorBatchItems` is the list-backed implementation: it unwraps `MediaWithBytes` when retrieving an item, but preserves the original wrapper for hashing. Its processor data is returned under a pluralized modality key, while its passthrough data is empty. [vllm/multimodal/parse.py:115-137]()

`EmbeddingItems` accepts either a batched tensor or a list of tensors. It validates that a single embedding has two or three dimensions, and that each embedding in a list is two-dimensional; it can also validate the expected hidden size. [vllm/multimodal/parse.py:139-203]()

| Abstraction | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `MultiModalDataDict` | Modality-keyed input dictionary accepted by the multimodal input schema. [vllm/multimodal/parse.py:22-39]() |
| `ModalityDataItems` | Common indexed interface for parsed items; separates processor data from passthrough data. [vllm/multimodal/parse.py:60-112]() |
| `ProcessorBatchItems` | Represents sequence-backed items and preserves wrapped data for hashing. [vllm/multimodal/parse.py:115-137]() |
| `EmbeddingItems` | Represents embedding tensors and validates embedding dimensionality. [vllm/multimodal/parse.py:139-203]() |

**Sources:** [vllm/multimodal/parse.py:22-39]() [vllm/multimodal/parse.py:60-112]() [vllm/multimodal/parse.py:115-137]() [vllm/multimodal/parse.py:139-203]()

### Modality Item Relationships

**Diagram: Data dictionary and parser abstractions**

```mermaid

        "get_passthrough_data()"
    }

        "list-backed items"

    }

        "tensor or list of tensors"

        "validate hidden size"
    }

    ModalityDataItems <|-- ProcessorBatchItems
    ModalityDataItems <|-- EmbeddingItems
```

**Sources:** [vllm/multimodal/parse.py:22-39]() [vllm/multimodal/parse.py:60-112]() [vllm/multimodal/parse.py:115-137]() [vllm/multimodal/parse.py:139-203]()

## Registry, Processor Factories, and Processing Info

The multimodal processing framework is organized around `BaseMultiModalProcessor`, `BaseProcessingInfo`, processor inputs, and modality-specific parsing. The processor module imports the parsed multimodal item types and defines prompt-update structures used to align processed multimodal content with prompt token positions. [vllm/multimodal/processing/processor.py:34-55]() [vllm/multimodal/processing/processor.py:91-103]() [vllm/multimodal/processing/processor.py:158-228]()

A model-specific processor can provide information about the tokenizer, media processor, and data parser. For example, `VoxtralProcessingInfo` obtains its Mistral tokenizer and feature extractor, creates a `MultiModalDataParser` with the target sample rate and channel count, and declares an audio-item limit. `VoxtralMultiModalProcessor` derives from `BaseMultiModalProcessor` and builds dummy inputs through the processor framework. [vllm/model_executor/models/voxtral.py:83-129]() [vllm/model_executor/models/voxtral.py:132-175]()

`cached_encode` applies an LRU cache to repeated tokenizer calls, keyed by tokenizer, text, and relevant encoding options. [vllm/multimodal/processing/processor.py:58-71]()

### Processor Inputs and Prompt Updates

`PromptIndex` describes how to locate a position in a tokenized or decoded prompt. `PromptIndexTargets` supplies start, prefix, and end targets. `PromptUpdateDetails` carries the full token sequence for an update and can optionally identify which token positions receive embeddings. These structures support matching multimodal placeholders to the prompt representation. [vllm/multimodal/processing/processor.py:74-155]() [vllm/multimodal/processing/processor.py:174-228]()

**Diagram: Processor concepts from request data to model-specific input**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    DataDict["MultiModalDataDict"] --> DataParser["MultiModalDataParser"]
    DataParser --> DataItems["ModalityDataItems"]
    DataItems --> MultiModalProcessor["BaseMultiModalProcessor"]
    ProcessingInfo["BaseProcessingInfo"] --> MultiModalProcessor
    MultiModalProcessor --> Inputs["ProcessorInputs"]
    MultiModalProcessor --> PromptUpdate["PromptUpdate"]
    PromptUpdate --> PromptIdx["PromptIndex"]
    PromptUpdate --> UpdateDetails["PromptUpdateDetails"]
    VoxtralInfo["VoxtralProcessingInfo"] --> VoxtralProc["VoxtralMultiModalProcessor"]
    VoxtralProc --> Inputs
```

**Sources:** [vllm/multimodal/parse.py:60-112]() [vllm/multimodal/processing/processor.py:34-55]() [vllm/multimodal/processing/processor.py:74-155]() [vllm/multimodal/processing/processor.py:174-228]() [vllm/model_executor/models/voxtral.py:83-175]()

### Processor Configuration

`mm_processor_kwargs` supports shared flat options and modality-specific Hugging Face processor scopes: `text_kwargs`, `images_kwargs`, `videos_kwargs`, and `audio_kwargs`. `_merge_mm_processor_kwargs` recursively merges nested mappings; for scoped values, the documented precedence is configured flat, configured scoped, inference flat, then inference scoped. [vllm/config/multimodal.py:30-143]()

**Sources:** [vllm/config/multimodal.py:30-143]()

## Image, Audio, and Video Decoding, and Caching

### Image and Audio Parsing

`vllm.multimodal.parse` imports image normalization and conversion helpers, audio normalization and resampling helpers, and modality-specific item types. The parser therefore forms the boundary between public modality data and the structured inputs used by processors. [vllm/multimodal/parse.py:22-39]()

The supplied audio implementation identifies `soundfile`, PyAV, and torchcodec as available decoding backends, with `"auto"` attempting torchcodec, then soundfile, then PyAV. `load_audio_pyav` opens the audio container, checks for an audio stream, and can reject a file based on duration metadata before decoding. Its decoding loop tracks samples and decoded bytes, with options for duration and byte limits. [vllm/multimodal/media/audio.py:30-76]() [vllm/multimodal/media/audio.py:82-112]() [vllm/multimodal/media/audio.py:113-174]()

### Video Loader Registry and Decoding

`VideoLoaderRegistry` maps loader names to loader classes and can associate video processor class names with backend names. It separately tracks whether a backend requires a GPU. `get_video_loader_backend_for_processor` exposes the processor-to-backend lookup. [vllm/multimodal/video.py:36-98]()

`VideoLoader.load_bytes` is the abstract interface for loading video bytes into decoded frames and metadata. Its return type permits either a host NumPy array or a device tensor, depending on the selected codec. `VideoBackend` is registered as the `"opencv"` loader, and its documented sampling policy is uniform sampling, with the decoder codec selected independently through the `backend` keyword argument. [vllm/multimodal/video.py:131-178]() [vllm/multimodal/video.py:197-210]()

The frame helpers resize frames through OpenCV and can sample a requested number of frames at evenly spaced indices. `VideoLoader.create_hf_metadata` produces metadata fields including total frames, FPS, duration, backend, sampled indices, and whether all frames were selected. [vllm/multimodal/video.py:100-128]() [vllm/multimodal/video.py:180-195]()

### Video Backend Selection

**Diagram: Video processor registration and decoder selection**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    ProcName["video_processor class name"] --> GetBackend["get_video_loader_backend_for_processor()"]
    RegBackend["VideoLoaderRegistry.processor2backend"] --> GetBackend
    RegClass["VideoLoaderRegistry.name2class"] --> LoadBytes["VideoLoader.load_bytes()"]
    VideoBackend["VideoBackend"] --> RegisterOpencv["VIDEO_LOADER_REGISTRY.register(opencv)"]
    LoadBytes --> DecodeVideo["decode_video()"]
    DecodeVideo --> OpencvBackend["opencv"]
    DecodeVideo --> TorchcodecBackend["torchcodec"]
    DecodeVideo --> PynvBackend["pynvvideocodec"]
    DecodeVideo --> DeepstreamBackend["deepstream"]
    LoadBytes --> Metadata["VideoLoader.create_hf_metadata()"]
```

The decoder module and its lazy-import behavior are exercised by tests: selecting a decoder backend imports only that backend module. [tests/multimodal/test_video.py:122-179]()

**Sources:** [vllm/multimodal/video.py:36-98]() [vllm/multimodal/video.py:131-210]() [vllm/multimodal/video.py:180-198]() [tests/multimodal/test_video.py:122-179]()

### Caching and Resource Limits

The parser’s `ProcessorBatchItems.get_item_for_hash` preserves `MediaWithBytes` wrappers when data is used for hashing, retaining access to original bytes where present. [vllm/multimodal/parse.py:115-133]() `cached_encode` separately caches repeated tokenizer encoding calls. [vllm/multimodal/processing/processor.py:58-71]()

Media fetching and decoding are resource-sensitive. The security guidance recommends restricting media URL domains and describes configurable limits for remote download size, aggregate request download size, decoded image pixels, aggregate decoded request bytes, audio file size and duration, audio decode bytes, and embedding densification. [docs/features/multimodal_inputs.md:10-15]()

`EncoderCache` stores multimodal encoder outputs to avoid recomputing embeddings for identical inputs. `MultiModalCache` is a generic LRU cache used for multimodal processor items, which can be configured with a maximum size in gigabytes. [vllm/multimodal/cache/base.py]() Tests verify the size calculation for cached items. [tests/multimodal/test_cache.py:109-132]()

**Sources:** [vllm/multimodal/parse.py:115-133]() [vllm/multimodal/processing/processor.py:58-71]() [docs/features/multimodal_inputs.md:10-15]() [vllm/multimodal/cache/base.py]() [tests/multimodal/test_cache.py:109-132]()

---

## Encoder Runner and Multimodal Execution

`EncoderRunner` is a GPU-side component responsible for coordinating multimodal encoder work. It manages the execution of multimodal encoders, potentially leveraging CUDA graphs for performance optimization. [vllm/v1/worker/gpu/mm/encoder_runner.py:34-60]()

The `prepare_mm_inputs` method filters multimodal features, identifying those that need encoding and those that are already in the model's embedding space (`"prompt_embeds"` modality). Pre-embedded features are directly cached. [vllm/v1/worker/gpu/mm/encoder_runner.py:81-107]()

The `execute_mm_encoder` method groups and batches multimodal inputs by modality to optimize encoding. It attempts to use CUDA graphs if available and supported for the current modality, otherwise it calls `model.embed_multimodal` directly. The outputs are then sanity-checked. [vllm/v1/worker/gpu/mm/encoder_runner.py:150-174]()

`EncoderRunner` also includes functionality for profiling the encoder cache memory. [vllm/v1/worker/gpu/mm/encoder_runner.py:110-149]()

### Encoder Flow: Processor Inputs to Encoder Cache

**Diagram: High-level multimodal encoder path**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Inputs["ProcessorInputs"] --> PrepareInputs["EncoderRunner.prepare_mm_inputs()"]
    PrepareInputs --> Cache["EncoderCache"]
    PrepareInputs --> ExecuteEncoder["EncoderRunner.execute_mm_encoder()"]
    ExecuteEncoder --> Embed["model.embed_multimodal()"]
    Embed --> Cache
    Cache --> Reuse["multimodal feature reuse"]
```

**Sources:** [vllm/multimodal/processing/processor.py:34-55]() [vllm/v1/worker/gpu/mm/encoder_runner.py:34-174]()

---

## Input Management: Placeholder Ranges and Prefix Caching

Prompt processing must associate multimodal content with prompt positions. The processor framework defines `PromptIndex` and prompt-update types for locating and replacing prompt regions; `PromptUpdateDetails` can mark which tokens correspond to embeddings. [vllm/multimodal/processing/processor.py:91-103]() [vllm/multimodal/processing/processor.py:158-228]()

The multimodal input module defines `PlaceholderRange`, which represents a range of tokens in the prompt that corresponds to a multimodal feature. It includes `offset`, `length`, and an optional `is_embed_mask` to indicate which tokens within the range should be replaced by embeddings. [vllm/multimodal/inputs.py:121-206]()

`NewRequestData` in the scheduler output includes `mm_features` which are stripped of covered multimodal data based on `num_computed_tokens` and `uses_mrope`. [vllm/v1/core/sched/output.py:69-73]()

**Sources:** [vllm/multimodal/processing/processor.py:91-103]() [vllm/multimodal/processing/processor.py:158-228]() [vllm/multimodal/inputs.py:121-206]() [vllm/v1/core/sched/output.py:69-73]()

---

## Security Considerations for Media Inputs

Multimodal requests that reference remote media can cause the server to make outbound requests. The security guidance recommends setting `--allowed-media-domains` and considering `VLLM_MEDIA_URL_ALLOW_REDIRECTS=0` to prevent redirects from bypassing domain restrictions. [docs/features/multimodal_inputs.md:10-15]()

The documentation details limits intended to constrain oversized downloads and decoded media allocations, including `VLLM_MAX_MEDIA_DOWNLOAD_SIZE_MB`, `VLLM_MAX_MEDIA_REQUEST_DOWNLOAD_SIZE_MB`, `VLLM_MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS`, `VLLM_MAX_MEDIA_REQUEST_DECODE_BYTES`, `VLLM_MAX_AUDIO_CLIP_FILESIZE_MB`, `VLLM_MAX_AUDIO_DECODE_DURATION_S`, `VLLM_MAX_AUDIO_DECODE_BYTES`, and `VLLM_MAX_EMBED_DECODE_BYTES`. Setting these limits to zero disables the corresponding protection. [docs/features/multimodal_inputs.md:10-15]()

**Sources:** [docs/features/multimodal_inputs.md:10-15]()

---

## Summary

`MultiModalDataDict` is the request-level modality mapping. `MultiModalDataParser` and `ModalityDataItems` provide structured item access and distinguish processor data from model passthrough data. Model-specific processors build on `BaseMultiModalProcessor` and processing-info objects; prompt-update structures connect multimodal features to prompt token positions. Media decoding is backend-specific: audio supports soundfile, PyAV, and torchcodec choices, while video uses a loader registry and selectable decoder backends. Processor encoding and media limits address repeated work and resource use; `EncoderRunner` coordinates multimodal encoder execution and leverages `EncoderCache` for feature reuse. [vllm/multimodal/parse.py:22-39]() [vllm/multimodal/parse.py:60-137]() [vllm/multimodal/processing/processor.py:34-55]() [vllm/multimodal/processing/processor.py:174-228]() [vllm/multimodal/media/audio.py:62-76]() [vllm/multimodal/video.py:36-98]() [vllm/v1/worker/gpu/mm/encoder_runner.py:34-174]()

**Sources:** [vllm/multimodal/parse.py:22-39]() [vllm/multimodal/parse.py:60-137]() [vllm/multimodal/processing/processor.py:34-55]() [vllm/multimodal/processing/processor.py:174-228]() [vllm/multimodal/media/audio.py:62-76]() [vllm/multimodal/video.py:36-98]() [vllm/v1/worker/gpu/mm/encoder_runner.py:34-174]()

## Purpose and Scope

This page documents the vendor- and hardware-specialized model implementation tree in `vllm/models/`, focusing on the architecture and execution patterns of families such as `deepseek_v32`, `deepseek_v4`/`deepseek_v41`, `kimi_k3`, `minimax_m3`, `qwen4_exp`, `glm5next`, `inkling`, `hy_v4`, `dots3_note`, and `step5`. These families incorporate hardware-specific sub-backends (NVIDIA, AMD ROCm, XPU), sparse Multi-Latent Attention (MLA), Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) heads, and custom fused operations.

These implementations compose family-specific layers with shared vLLM execution facilities for attention, MoE routing, quantization, distributed execution, weight loading, and speculative decoding. Hardware-specific modules select optimized kernels and memory layouts while preserving model-family computational contracts. `[vllm/models/deepseek_v4/attention.py:133-143]()`, `[vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/model.py:78-100]`, `[vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/model.py:21-124]`, `[vllm/models/minimax_m3/nvidia/model.py:3-13]()`

Sources: `[vllm/models/deepseek_v4/attention.py:133-143]()`, `[vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/model.py:78-100]()`, `[vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/model.py:21-124]()`, `[vllm/models/minimax_m3/nvidia/model.py:3-13]()`

---

## 1. Directory Structure and Vendor Model Layout

The model implementations follow a family-oriented layout with platform-specific subpackages (e.g., `nvidia`, `amd`, `common`, `specialized_decode`). For instance, DeepSeek V4/V4.1 provide platform-specific implementations for NVIDIA (`DeepseekV4FlashMLAAttention`, `DeepseekV4MegaAttnAttention`) and AMD ROCm, while Kimi K3 implements specialized Gated Delta Attention (`KimiK3DeltaAttention`) and Latent MoE runners. `[vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/model.py:78-95]()`, `[vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/model.py:100-108]`, `[vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/kda.py:105-108]()`

### Family and Backend Map

| Family | Subpackages / Paths | Implementation Themes |
|---|---|---|
| `deepseek_v32` | `deepseek_v32/` | MLA, sparse indexer cache, top-K token selection, MTP integration |
| `deepseek_v4` / `deepseek_v41` | `deepseek_v4/`, `deepseek_v41/` (`nvidia/`, `amd/`, `common/`) | Sparse MLA, FlashMLA, MegaMoE, TRTLLM MXFP4/NVFP4 experts, MTP heads, Engram caches |
| `kimi_k3` | `kimi_k3/` (`nvidia/`, `amd/`, `common/`) | Multimodal Kimi ViT/Proprocessors, Gated Delta Attention (KDA), Latent MoE, low-latency GEMM |
| `minimax_m3` | `minimax_m3/` (`nvidia/`, `amd/`, `common/`) | Sparse prefill/decode attention kernels, indexer score/topk, Gemma-style RMSNorm |
| `qwen4_exp`, `glm5next`, `inkling`, `hy_v4`, `dots3_note`, `step5` | Named in configuration scope | Specialized vendor architectures with custom tensor parallelism and op bindings |

Sources: `[vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/model.py:78-95]()`, `[vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/model.py:100-108]()`, `[vllm/models/minimax_m3/nvidia/model.py:3-13]()`

### Model Implementation Responsibilities

A vendor model module wires together shared linear layers (`ColumnParallelLinear`, `RowParallelLinear`, `MergedColumnParallelLinear`), custom normalization layers (`RMSNorm`), MoE blocks (`FusedMoEFactory`, `DeepGemmMegaMoEExperts`), and specialized attention mechanics.

```mermaid
    DeepseekV4Attn --> DeepseekCompressor["DeepseekCompressor\n[vllm/models/deepseek_v41/compressor.py]"]
```
