## Purpose and scope

This page describes vLLM’s LoRA adapter configuration and runtime management: how the documented serving API exposes dynamic loading and unloading, how `WorkerLoRAManager` [vllm/lora/worker_manager.py:27-32]() and `LoRAModelManager` [vllm/lora/model_manager.py:76-77]() manage adapter lifecycles, how supported model layers are selected and wrapped for LoRA, how Punica kernels and wrappers execute multi-tenant LoRA, and how fused Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) LoRA handles 2D, 3D, and shared adapter layouts. [docs/features/lora.md:105-155](), [vllm/lora/worker_manager.py:27-104](), [vllm/lora/model_manager.py:76-167]()

Sources: [docs/features/lora.md:105-155](), [vllm/lora/worker_manager.py:27-104](), [vllm/lora/model_manager.py:76-167]()

## 1. Overview and core concepts

LoRA enables serving base models with adapter-specific weights on a per-request basis. Model support requires implementing the `SupportsLoRA` interface [docs/features/lora.md:3-5](), while `LoRAConfig` [vllm/config/lora.py:31-32]() specifies configuration constraints including maximum rank, adapter counts, dtypes, target modules, and MoE layouts.

The primary system and code entities involved are:

| Entity | Role & Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `LoRAConfig` | Configures adapter capacity (`max_loras`, `max_cpu_loras`), rank limits (`max_lora_rank`), `target_modules`, and MoE format flags. [vllm/config/lora.py:31-88]() |
| `WorkerLoRAManager` | Manages worker-side LoRA adapter checkpoints, validating metadata via `PEFTHelper` and instantiating `LoRAModelManager`. [vllm/lora/worker_manager.py:27-159]() |
| `LoRAModelManager` | Maintains registered and active adapter caches (`AdapterLRUCache`), tracks supported modules, selects MoE-related layouts, and coordinates the Punica wrapper. [vllm/lora/model_manager.py:65-167]() |
| `LoRAModel` | Represents a parsed adapter checkpoint containing layer weights (`LoRALayerWeights`) and full modules to save. [vllm/lora/lora_model.py:57-88]() |
| Punica Wrappers | Interface abstractions (e.g., `PunicaWrapperBase`, `PunicaWrapperXPU`) managing metadata tensors and kernel dispatch (`bgmv_shrink`, `bgmv_expand`, `fused_moe_lora`). [vllm/lora/punica_wrapper/punica_xpu.py:30-73]() |

Sources: [docs/features/lora.md:3-7](), [vllm/config/lora.py:31-88](), [vllm/lora/worker_manager.py:27-159](), [vllm/lora/model_manager.py:65-167](), [vllm/lora/lora_model.py:57-88](), [vllm/lora/punica_wrapper/punica_xpu.py:30-73]()

### Natural-language concepts mapped to code entities

The following diagram bridges high-level adapter lifecycle operations to concrete classes and methods in the codebase.

**Diagram: Adapter management data flow and code entities**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Client["ClientRequestsLoad"]
    API["vllm/entrypoints/openai/api_server.py"]
    Worker["WorkerLoRAManager"]
    Factory["vllm.lora.model_manager.create_lora_manager"]
    Manager["LoRAModelManager"]
    Load["WorkerLoRAManager._load_adapter"]
    Peft["PEFTHelper.from_local_dir"]
    Model["LoRAModel.from_local_checkpoint"]
    Reg["AdapterLRUCache"]
    
    Client --> API
    API --> Worker
    Worker --> Factory
    Factory --> Manager
    Worker --> Load
    Load --> Peft
    Load --> Model
    Model --> Reg
```

Sources: [vllm/lora/worker_manager.py:86-159](), [vllm/lora/model_manager.py:65-167](), [vllm/lora/lora_model.py:120-174]()

## 2. LoRA request identity and configuration

Requests carry a `LoRARequest` object specifying the adapter name, integer ID, path, and optional layout flags (such as `is_3d_lora_weight`) [tests/lora/test_gptoss_tp.py:89-94](). 

`LoRAConfig` provides configuration attributes validated at initialization [vllm/config/lora.py:119-136]():

| Configuration Field | Description |
|---|---|
| `max_lora_rank` | Maximum supported rank for adapters (e.g., 16, 32, 64). [vllm/config/lora.py:34-35]() |
| `max_loras` | Maximum number of active adapters in a single batch. [vllm/config/lora.py:36-37]() |
| `max_cpu_loras` | Maximum number of adapters cached in CPU memory (must be $\ge$ `max_loras`). [vllm/config/lora.py:43-45]() |
| `lora_dtype` | Data type for LoRA weights (`"auto"` defaults to base model dtype). [vllm/config/lora.py:46-47]() |
| `target_modules` | Optional list of module name suffixes to apply LoRA to. [vllm/config/lora.py:48-51]() |
| `enable_mixed_moe_lora_format` | Forces universal 2D MoE wrapper (`FusedMoEWithLoRA`) for mixed 2D/3D deployments. [vllm/config/lora.py:74-79]() |
| `enable_moe_shared_loras` | Enables shared-outer MoE expert adapter layout. [vllm/config/lora.py:80-86]() |

Sources: [tests/lora/test_gptoss_tp.py:89-94](), [vllm/config/lora.py:34-86](), [vllm/config/lora.py:119-136]()

## 3. `LoRAModelManager` and `WorkerLoRAManager` lifecycle

`WorkerLoRAManager` manages the worker-side state [vllm/lora/worker_manager.py:27-32](). It inspects `VllmConfig` for scheduler limits and vocabulary size, establishes position embedding limits (handling encoder-decoder models like Whisper via `max_target_positions` when applicable), and lazily instantiates the adapter manager via `create_lora_manager` [vllm/lora/worker_manager.py:45-104]().

`LoRAModelManager` identifies supported modules via `get_supported_lora_modules` [vllm/lora/model_manager.py:104-107](), configures `AdapterLRUCache` instances for registered and active adapters [vllm/lora/model_manager.py:114-119](), initializes packed module mappings, and sets up the Punica execution wrapper [vllm/lora/model_manager.py:132-167]().

**Diagram: Initialization lifecycle of worker and model managers**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Cfg["VllmConfig"] --> W[WorkerLoRAManager]
    W --> CF[create_lora_manager]
    CF --> M[LoRAModelManager]
    M --> SM[get_supported_lora_modules]
    M --> PM[process_packed_modules_mapping]
    M --> PW[_init_punica_wrapper]
    M --> CM[_create_lora_modules]
```

Sources: [vllm/lora/worker_manager.py:27-104](), [vllm/lora/model_manager.py:104-167]()

### Adapter checkpoint loading and validation

When loading an adapter via `WorkerLoRAManager._load_adapter` [vllm/lora/worker_manager.py:106-110](), the system:
1. Resolves absolute paths using `get_adapter_absolute_path` [vllm/lora/worker_manager.py:119-119]().
2. Parses PEFT configuration via `PEFTHelper.from_local_dir` and validates it against `LoRAConfig` [vllm/lora/worker_manager.py:121-127]().
3. Loads tensor checkpoints into CPU memory using `LoRAModel.from_local_checkpoint` with appropriate weight mappers (`hf_to_vllm_mapper`), skip prefixes, and MoE expert-parallel specs [vllm/lora/worker_manager.py:129-152]().
4. Validates MoE layout compatibility and classification head weights [vllm/lora/worker_manager.py:154-160]().

Sources: [vllm/lora/worker_manager.py:106-160]()

## 4. Dynamic loading and unloading through the serving API

The vLLM server supports runtime loading and unloading of adapters when `VLLM_ALLOW_RUNTIME_LORA_UPDATING=True` [docs/features/lora.md:105-117]():
- **Load Adapter**: `POST /v1/load_lora_adapter` accepts `lora_name` and `lora_path` in the JSON payload [docs/features/lora.md:129-135]().
- **Unload Adapter**: `POST /v1/unload_lora_adapter` accepts `lora_name` to remove the adapter from memory [docs/features/lora.md:147-155]().

Sources: [docs/features/lora.md:105-155]()

## 5. LoRA layer implementations and routing

The layer builder `from_layer` iterates through `_all_lora_classes` in priority order, invoking `can_replace_layer` on source modules [vllm/lora/utils.py:83-135](). Specific wrappers (such as custom indexers and QKV projections) are checked before generic merged and column-parallel classes [vllm/lora/utils.py:83-106]().

Supported layer wrappers include:
- **Linear layers**: `ColumnParallelLinearWithLoRA`, `MergedColumnParallelLinearWithLoRA`, `RowParallelLinearWithLoRA`, `ReplicatedLinearWithLoRA`, and their fully-sharded S-LoRA variants [vllm/lora/layers/__init__.py:3-32]().
- **Embeddings & Logits**: `VocabParallelEmbeddingWithLoRA`, `LogitsProcessorWithLoRA` [vllm/lora/layers/__init__.py:20-34]().
- **Classification heads**: `ClassificationHeadWithLoRA`, `TokenClassificationHeadWithLoRA` [vllm/lora/layers/classifier.py:4-174]().
- **Mixture of Experts**: `FusedMoEWithLoRA`, `FusedMoE3DWithLoRA` [vllm/lora/layers/fused_moe.py:30-30](), [vllm/lora/layers/__init__.py:26-26]().

Sources: [vllm/lora/utils.py:83-135](), [vllm/lora/layers/__init__.py:3-32](), [vllm/lora/layers/classifier.py:4-174]()

## 6. Punica kernels and wrappers

Punica provides multi-tenant LoRA GEMM execution via custom CUDA/XPU kernels (`bgmv_shrink`, `bgmv_expand`, `bgmv_expand_slice`) [vllm/lora/punica_wrapper/punica_xpu.py:15-15]().

- `PunicaWrapperBase` and platform-specific implementations (e.g., `PunicaWrapperXPU`) maintain token-to-lora mapping indices and kernel metadata (`LoRAKernelMeta`) [vllm/lora/punica_wrapper/punica_xpu.py:30-62]().
- `get_captured_lora_counts` calculates active adapter count boundaries for CUDA graph specialization (powers of two up to `max_loras` plus `max_loras + 1`) [vllm/lora/utils.py:57-71]().
- Fully-sharded S-LoRA layers (`ColumnParallelLinearWithLoRA`) utilize `add_shrink` and `add_expand` combined with `tensor_model_parallel_all_gather` [vllm/lora/layers/column_parallel_linear.py:24-82]().

**Diagram: Punica wrapper and execution flow**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Input["InputTensor x"] --> Shrink["PunicaWrapperXPU.add_shrink"]
    Shrink --> Gather["tensor_model_parallel_all_gather"]
    Gather --> Expand["PunicaWrapperXPU.add_expand"]
    Expand --> Output["FusedOutputTensor"]
```

Sources: [vllm/lora/punica_wrapper/punica_xpu.py:30-195](), [vllm/lora/utils.py:57-71](), [vllm/lora/layers/column_parallel_linear.py:24-82]()

## 7. Fused MoE LoRA and adapter layouts

MoE models are detected via `is_moe_model`, which scans for `MoERunner` modules [vllm/lora/utils.py:109-114](). 

`FusedMoEWithLoRA` wraps MoE runner layers [vllm/lora/layers/fused_moe.py:30-34]():
- Enforces modular kernel requirements and integrates with `MoELoRAContext` [vllm/lora/layers/fused_moe.py:65-88](), [vllm/lora/layers/fused_moe.py:142-159]().
- Supports dual CUDA stream execution for overlapping base GEMM and LoRA computations when `VLLM_LORA_ENABLE_DUAL_STREAM` is active [vllm/lora/layers/fused_moe.py:52-53](), [vllm/lora/layers/fused_moe.py:136-159]().
- Handles 3D-weight MoE checkpoints and universal 2D formats via `enable_mixed_moe_lora_format` and shared-outer expert factor layouts via `enable_moe_shared_loras` [vllm/config/lora.py:74-86](), [vllm/lora/layers/fused_moe.py:57-59]().

Sources: [vllm/lora/utils.py:109-114](), [vllm/config/lora.py:74-86](), [vllm/lora/layers/fused_moe.py:30-159]()

## 8. Tests and validation

Test suites in `tests/lora/` validate adapter loading, MoE format constraints, and tensor conversions:
- `test_reject_fused_moe_lora_before_registration` ensures missing MoE format flags trigger descriptive validation errors before caching [tests/lora/test_lora_manager.py:58-83]().
- `test_from_lora_tensors` verifies safetensors parsing into `LoRAModel` rank, alpha, and device tensors [tests/lora/test_lora_manager.py:118-141]().
- `test_gpt_oss_lora` validates end-to-end generation with LoRA adapters on MoE architectures [tests/lora/test_gptoss_tp.py:129-155]().

Sources: [tests/lora/test_lora_manager.py:58-141](), [tests/lora/test_gptoss_tp.py:129-155]()

## 9. Operational notes

- Runtime adapter updating via API endpoints (`/v1/load_lora_adapter`, `/v1/unload_lora_adapter`) requires setting `VLLM_ALLOW_RUNTIME_LORA_UPDATING=True` and should be restricted to trusted environments [docs/features/lora.md:105-117]().
- `max_cpu_loras` must be greater than or equal to `max_loras`; validation enforces this constraint [vllm/config/lora.py:43-45](), [vllm/config/lora.py:119-127]().
- Unsupported MoE backends (such as MegaMoE) reject LoRA configuration during kernel config verification [vllm/config/lora.py:138-145]().

Sources: [docs/features/lora.md:105-117](), [vllm/config/lora.py:43-45](), [vllm/config/lora.py:119-145]()

## Purpose and scope

Section 6.5 documents the Rust frontend’s HTTP and gRPC serving layers, the crates that make up its request path, and how that path connects to an engine through `EngineCoreClient`. The workspace includes separate crates for serving, chat, text, LLM access, tokenization, parser, engine-core transport, mock-engine support, and metrics [rust/Cargo.toml:1-18]().

Sources: [rust/Cargo.toml:1-18]()

## Layered crate architecture

The Rust workspace separates the frontend into crates with explicit dependencies between the serving and request-processing layers. `vllm-server` builds the serving runtime around `vllm-chat`, `vllm-text`, `vllm-llm`, and `vllm-engine-core-client`; the workspace also includes `vllm-tokenizer`, `vllm-parser`, `vllm-mock-engine`, and `vllm-metrics` [rust/Cargo.toml:1-18]().

The chat crate describes its boundary as messages rendered to prompts, tokenized prompts passed toward the engine, and streamed structured assistant events returned to callers [rust/src/chat/src/lib.rs:4-11](). The server assembles this stack by wrapping an `EngineCoreClient` in `EngineCoreLlm`, then `TextLlm`, then `ChatLlm`, and placing the chat interface in `AppState` [rust/src/server/src/lib.rs:130-163]().

## HTTP and gRPC serving

`vllm-server` declares distinct modules for `routes` and `grpc`, alongside middleware, listeners, shared state, TLS, rendering, and runtime support [rust/src/server/src/lib.rs:4-22](). Its server lifecycle integrates Hyper and Tonic server types [rust/src/server/src/lib.rs:38-50]().

## Request and response flow

At startup, `build_state` loads the model’s chat and text backends, resolves a coordinator mode, connects an `EngineCoreClient`, and constructs the `EngineCoreLlm`, `TextLlm`, and `ChatLlm` layers. It then creates shared `AppState` with served model names and server options [rust/src/server/src/lib.rs:85-171]().

For text generation, `lower_text_request` validates prompt token IDs and creates a `GenerateRequest`. It transfers multimodal features into the engine request, lowers sampling parameters, and carries request metadata such as request ID, priority, cache salt, data-parallel rank, session ID, KV hints, reasoning-parser arguments, LoRA request, and arrival time [rust/src/text/src/lower.rs:66-106]().

**Diagram: Request path from server setup through engine boundary**

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Caller as ""HTTP or gRPC caller""
    participant Server as ""vllm-server""
    participant Chat as ""ChatLlm""
    participant Text as ""TextLlm""
    participant Lower as ""lower_text_request""
    participant Llm as ""EngineCoreLlm""
    participant Client as ""EngineCoreClient""
    participant Engine as ""EngineCore""

    Caller->>Server: ""submit request""
    Server->>Chat: ""ChatRequest""
    Chat->>Text: ""TextRequest""
    Text->>Lower: ""TextRequest and prompt_token_ids""
    Lower-->>Text: ""PreparedTextRequest""
    Text->>Llm: ""GenerateRequest""
    Llm->>Client: ""engine request""
    Client->>Engine: ""transport request""
    Engine-->>Client: ""engine output""
    Client-->>Llm: ""generation output""
    Llm-->>Text: ""text output stream""
    Text-->>Chat: ""chat events""
    Chat-->>Server: ""response stream""
    Server-->>Caller: ""HTTP or gRPC response""
```

## Purpose and Scope

This page documents the scale-out serving paths for separating request rendering, token generation, and response postprocessing. It focuses on token-in-token-out generation through `ServingTokens`, and on derendering generated tokens back into chat or completion responses through `ServingDerender` and `OnlineDerenderer`. [vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/serving.py:147-176]() [vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/serving.py:47-61]() [vllm/renderers/online_derenderer.py:70-88]()

These paths are useful when a deployment handles tokenization or response formatting outside the generation service. The render/derender documentation describes the round trip: `/render` turns requests into token IDs, generation consumes and returns token IDs, and `/derender` postprocesses those IDs into an OpenAI-compatible response without a GPU. [docs/serving/online_serving/derenderer.md:3-12]()

Sources: [vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/serving.py:147-176]() [vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/serving.py:47-61]() [vllm/renderers/online_derenderer.py:70-88]() [docs/serving/online_serving/derenderer.md:3-12]()

---

## Architectural Overview of Scale-Out Serving

The scale-out flow separates three responsibilities: rendering a user request into token IDs, generating from those IDs, and derendering generated IDs into a response. In this design, the generation service can operate on token-space inputs and outputs, while a rendering-side service handles text-oriented processing. [docs/serving/online_serving/derenderer.md:3-12]()

The token-in-token-out API is implemented by `ServingTokens`, which extends `GenerateBaseServing` and receives an `EngineClient`, models, and an `OnlineRenderer`. [vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/serving.py:147-176]() The derender API is implemented by `ServingDerender`, which receives models and an `OnlineDerenderer` and exposes chat/completion response postprocessing methods. [vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/serving.py:47-61]() The `OnlineDerenderer` owns the renderer and parser configuration and schedules CPU-bound detokenization and parsing work on the renderer’s executor. [vllm/renderers/online_derenderer.py:70-149]()

**Diagram: Scale-out request path mapped to code entities**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Client["Client request"]
    Render["/render"]
    Renderer["OnlineRenderer"]
    GenRequest["GenerateRequest"]
    ServingTokens["ServingTokens.serve_tokens"]
    EngineClient["EngineClient"]
    GenResponse["GenerateTokensResponse"]
    ServingDerender["ServingDerender"]
    Derenderer["OnlineDerenderer"]
    OpenAIResponse["ChatCompletionResponse or CompletionResponse"]

    Client -->|"chat or completion input"| Render
    Render -->|"token_ids and request metadata"| GenRequest
    GenRequest --> ServingTokens
    ServingTokens -->|"generation request"| EngineClient
    EngineClient -->|"generated token output"| ServingTokens
    ServingTokens --> GenResponse
    GenResponse -->|"derender request"| ServingDerender
    ServingDerender --> Derenderer
    Derenderer -->|"detokenized and parsed output"| OpenAIResponse
```

Sources: [docs/serving/online_serving/derenderer.md:3-12]() [vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/serving.py:147-176]() [vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/serving.py:47-61]() [vllm/renderers/online_derenderer.py:70-149]()

## Token-In-Token-Out Serving (`vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/`)

### `ServingTokens`

`ServingTokens` is the token-in-token-out serving implementation. It derives from `GenerateBaseServing`, stores the supplied `EngineClient`, model registry, and `OnlineRenderer`, and records options controlling detokenization, token-ID presentation, prompt token details, and output logging. [vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/serving.py:147-176]()

When `force_no_detokenize` is enabled, `ServingTokens` sets `has_tokenizer` to false and logs that incoming requests skip detokenization. Otherwise, tokenizer availability is determined from the renderer. [vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/serving.py:173-181]() The constructor also resolves model-specific sampling defaults and a possible `max_tokens` override from generation configuration. [vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/serving.py:183-192]()

**Diagram: `ServingTokens` setup and request entry**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    GenerateRequest["GenerateRequest"]
    ServeTokens["ServingTokens.serve_tokens"]
    CheckModel["_check_model"]
    Preflight["_preflight"]
    ServingTokens["ServingTokens"]
    Renderer["OnlineRenderer"]
    EngineClient["EngineClient"]

    GenerateRequest --> ServeTokens
    ServeTokens --> CheckModel
    CheckModel -->|"valid request"| Preflight
    Preflight --> ServingTokens
    ServingTokens --> Renderer
    ServingTokens --> EngineClient
```

Sources: [vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/serving.py:147-176]() [vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/serving.py:173-181]() [vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/serving.py:183-192]()

### Request and response protocol

The protocol defines output modes `"tokens"`, `"text"`, and `"derender"`. [vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/protocol.py:52]() The derenderer documentation specifies that derender endpoints accept token-mode output; text-mode output is already detokenized and is rejected by those endpoints. [docs/serving/online_serving/derenderer.md:46-48]()

| Protocol entity | Role |
|---|---|
| `GenerateRequest` | Carries generation input, including `token_ids`. |
| `GenerateTokensResponse` | Token-oriented generation response type consumed by derender methods. [vllm/renderers/online_derenderer.py:38-44]() |
| `GenerateTokensStreamResponse` | Streaming token-response type accepted by derender stream processing. [vllm/renderers/online_derenderer.py:38-44]() |
| `MultiModalFeatures` | Carries multimodal hashes, placeholder ranges, and optional serialized feature or metadata payloads. [vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/protocol.py:128-161]() |
| `PlaceholderRangeInfo` | Represents a multimodal placeholder’s token-sequence offset and length. [vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/protocol.py:106-113]() |

Sources: [vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/protocol.py:52]() [vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/protocol.py:106-113]() [vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/protocol.py:128-161]() [vllm/renderers/online_derenderer.py:38-44]() [docs/serving/online_serving/derenderer.md:46-48]()

### Multimodal feature metadata

`MultiModalFeatures` provides multimodal metadata for a token sequence: per-modality hashes and placeholder ranges, plus optional serialized `kwargs_data` and `mm_metadata`. [vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/protocol.py:128-161]() Its validator requires the modalities in these fields to agree, requires parallel per-modality lists to have matching lengths, and rejects globally overlapping placeholder ranges. [vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/protocol.py:163-180]()

A placeholder range uses a non-negative `offset` and a strictly positive `length`. [vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/protocol.py:106-113]() The protocol describes `kwargs_data` as base64-encoded multimodal items, with `None` indicating that an item should be resolved from cache; `mm_metadata` carries serialized metadata used for disaggregated prefill under the stated transfer conditions. [vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/protocol.py:142-161]()

Sources: [vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/protocol.py:106-113]() [vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/protocol.py:128-161]() [vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/protocol.py:163-180]()

### Sampling defaults and token logprobs

`ServingTokens` keeps the model’s differing sampling parameters and computes an override value from either the generation configuration or the model’s override configuration. [vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/serving.py:183-192]() This supports server-side defaulting when a caller omits `max_tokens`, rather than silently relying on the `SamplingParams` dataclass default. [vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/serving.py:183-192]()

The token-serving module’s `_logprob_token` helper returns a `token_id:N` placeholder without a tokenizer; with a tokenizer, it decodes the token and returns its UTF-8 bytes. [vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/serving.py:121-136]() `_clamp_logprob` maps NaN to `-9999.0` and floors values at `-9999.0`, ensuring values are bounded for response serialization. [vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/serving.py:112-119]()

Sources: [vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/serving.py:112-119]() [vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/serving.py:121-136]() [vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/serving.py:183-192]()

---

## Render and Derender Services

### Render-to-generate-to-derender flow

The `/render` and `/derender` APIs are the preprocessing and postprocessing ends of a token-in-token-out deployment. The render step produces token IDs; the generation service operates on token IDs; and derender reconstructs a response. [docs/serving/online_serving/derenderer.md:3-12]()

The derender step may need the original chat or completion request and prompt-token context, in addition to generated token IDs. This context enables parsing and detokenization to reflect the original request. [docs/serving/online_serving/derenderer.md:26-33]() For chat streaming, a client sends one generation chunk at a time and carries `stream_state` between calls. [docs/serving/online_serving/derenderer.md:65-83]()

**Diagram: Natural-language request through scale-out code entities**

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client as "Client"
    participant Render as "/render"
    participant Generate as "ServingTokens.serve_tokens"
    participant Engine as "EngineClient"
    participant Derender as "ServingDerender.derender_chat_response"
    participant Parser as "OnlineDerenderer"

    Client->>Render: "chat request"
    Render-->>Client: "GenerateRequest with token_ids"
    Client->>Generate: "GenerateRequest"
    Generate->>Engine: "generation request"
    Engine-->>Generate: "token output"
    Generate-->>Client: "GenerateTokensResponse"
    Client->>Derender: "GenerateTokensResponse and chat_request"
    Derender->>Parser: "derender_chat"
    Parser-->>Derender: "parsed chat choices"
    Derender-->>Client: "ChatCompletionResponse"
```

Sources: [docs/serving/online_serving/derenderer.md:3-12]() [docs/serving/online_serving/derenderer.md:26-33]() [docs/serving/online_serving/derenderer.md:65-83]() [vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/serving.py:147-176]() [vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/serving.py:142-154]() [vllm/renderers/online_derenderer.py:151-159]()

### `ServingDerender`

`ServingDerender` extends `BaseServing`, retains the supplied `OnlineDerenderer`, and provides derender operations for chat and completion responses. [vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/serving.py:47-61]() Before derendering, its bounds checks limit response counts, choice counts, token-ID and logprob lengths, prompt-logprob lengths, and top-logprob counts using server/model limits. [vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/serving.py:63-127]()

`derender_chat_response` checks the model and request bounds, validates prompt token IDs, and requires a `chat_request` when a tool or reasoning parser is configured. It then delegates chat-choice reconstruction to `OnlineDerenderer.derender_chat`. [vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/serving.py:142-178]() The method’s documented behavior is one-shot postprocessing of a complete generation response; the parser can split output into reasoning, content, and tool calls when chat context is supplied. [vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/serving.py:142-154]()

Sources: [vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/serving.py:47-61]() [vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/serving.py:63-127]() [vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/serving.py:142-178]()

### `OnlineDerenderer`

`OnlineDerenderer` is initialized with a `ModelConfig`, `BaseRenderer`, request logger, chat-template configuration, and optional parser/tool settings. [vllm/renderers/online_derenderer.py:70-88]() It configures a parser through `ParserManager.get_parser`, using the model and renderer tokenizer among the inputs. [vllm/renderers/online_derenderer.py:108-116]()

The class wraps chat derendering, completion derendering, delta detokenization, and parsed chat-stream derendering in asynchronous calls using the renderer’s executor. The implementation notes that detokenization, logprob resolution, and parsing are CPU-bound, and that parser replay is O(n) per chunk. [vllm/renderers/online_derenderer.py:134-150]() The public `derender_chat` method delegates to its executor-backed implementation. [vllm/renderers/online_derenderer.py:151-159]()

For chat output, `_drop_stop_token` handles whether the stop token is included in the returned text token sequence. It preserves tokens when the finish reason or stop reason indicates that trimming does not apply, and otherwise checks the final token against the stop token or model EOS IDs. [vllm/renderers/online_derenderer.py:161-176]()

Sources: [vllm/renderers/online_derenderer.py:70-88]() [vllm/renderers/online_derenderer.py:108-116]() [vllm/renderers/online_derenderer.py:134-150]() [vllm/renderers/online_derenderer.py:151-159]() [vllm/renderers/online_derenderer.py:161-176]()

### Streaming derender

Derender requests can process a single generation-stream chunk and carry `stream_state` into the next request. The API returns a chunk and updated state; the documented chat-stream path supports reasoning and tool-call parsing. [docs/serving/online_serving/derenderer.md:8-10]() [docs/serving/online_serving/derenderer.md:65-83]()

The `OnlineDerenderer` provides executor-backed helpers for delta detokenization and parsed chat-stream derendering. [vllm/renderers/online_derenderer.py:143-150]() The streaming test module describes coverage for `_detokenize_delta`, completion/chat stream derendering, and the parsed replay path; it also identifies the integration round trip through the streaming endpoint. [tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py:4-17]()

**Diagram: Streaming state carried across derender calls**

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Generator as "Generate stream"
    participant Client as "Client"
    participant Endpoint as "derender stream endpoint"
    participant Derenderer as "OnlineDerenderer"

    Generator-->>Client: "GenerateStreamResponse chunk 1"
    Client->>Endpoint: "generate_chunk 1 and stream_state"
    Endpoint->>Derenderer: "detokenize and parse delta"
    Derenderer-->>Endpoint: "response chunk 1 and updated state"
    Endpoint-->>Client: "chunk 1 and stream_state"
    Generator-->>Client: "GenerateStreamResponse chunk 2"
    Client->>Endpoint: "generate_chunk 2 and previous stream_state"
    Endpoint->>Derenderer: "continue stream processing"
    Derenderer-->>Endpoint: "response chunk 2 and updated state"
    Endpoint-->>Client: "chunk 2 and stream_state"
```

Sources: [docs/serving/online_serving/derenderer.md:8-10]() [docs/serving/online_serving/derenderer.md:65-83]() [vllm/renderers/online_derenderer.py:143-150]() [tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py:4-17]()

### Parser configuration and parity

`OnlineDerenderer` constructs its parser from its server-side parser options and the renderer tokenizer. [vllm/renderers/online_derenderer.py:108-116]() The derender documentation advises matching parser and chat-template settings between render and derender services and sending the full chat request, since request fields affect how generated output is parsed. [docs/serving/online_serving/derenderer.md:87-94]()

The parity test describes comparing the coupled chat-completion path with the disaggregated `/v1/chat/completions/derender` path using the same generated token IDs. It asserts parity for content, reasoning, tool calls, finish reason, token IDs, and usage. [tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_parity.py:4-19]() [tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_parity.py:160-170]()

Sources: [vllm/renderers/online_derenderer.py:108-116]() [docs/serving/online_serving/derenderer.md:87-94]() [tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_parity.py:4-19]() [tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_parity.py:160-170]()

## Integration with Engine Clients and Distributed Scale-Out

`ServingTokens` accepts an `EngineClient` in its constructor, making that client the serving layer’s engine-facing dependency. [vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/serving.py:147-160]() The multimodal protocol supports passing hashes, placeholder locations, serialized multimodal data, or metadata for cache and disaggregated-prefill use cases. [vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/protocol.py:128-161]() The derender path is a separate postprocessing operation and does not require GPU work, according to its API documentation. [docs/serving/online_serving/derenderer.md:3-12]()

**Diagram: Boundary between token-serving and response postprocessing**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    ExternalFrontend["External frontend"]
    GenerateRequest["GenerateRequest.token_ids"]
    ServingTokens["ServingTokens"]
    EngineClient["EngineClient"]
    GenerateTokensResponse["GenerateTokensResponse"]
    DerenderRequest["Derender request with chat_request"]
    ServingDerender["ServingDerender"]
    OnlineDerenderer["OnlineDerenderer"]
    ClientResponse["OpenAI-compatible response"]

    ExternalFrontend -->|"pre-tokenized input"| GenerateRequest
    GenerateRequest --> ServingTokens
    ServingTokens --> EngineClient
    EngineClient --> ServingTokens
    ServingTokens --> GenerateTokensResponse
    GenerateTokensResponse --> DerenderRequest
    DerenderRequest --> ServingDerender
    ServingDerender --> OnlineDerenderer
    OnlineDerenderer --> ClientResponse
```

Sources: [vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/serving.py:147-160]() [vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/protocol.py:128-161]() [vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/serving.py:47-61]() [vllm/renderers/online_derenderer.py:70-88]() [docs/serving/online_serving/derenderer.md:3-12]()

---

## Summary

The scale-out token-in-token-out path separates token-oriented generation from request rendering and response reconstruction. `ServingTokens` is the generation-facing serving class; `GenerateRequest` carries token IDs; `ServingDerender` and `OnlineDerenderer` handle response postprocessing. [vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/serving.py:147-176]() [vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/protocol.py:162-179]() [vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/serving.py:47-61]() [vllm/renderers/online_derenderer.py:70-88]()

For deployments using derendering, preserve the request context required by the derender API, especially the original chat request when tool or reasoning parsing is configured. Streaming callers must also carry `stream_state` between chunk-processing calls. [vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/serving.py:168-178]() [docs/serving/online_serving/derenderer.md:65-83]()

Sources: [vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/serving.py:147-176]() [vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/protocol.py:162-179]() [vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/serving.py:47-61]() [vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/serving.py:168-178]() [vllm/renderers/online_derenderer.py:70-88]() [docs/serving/online_serving/derenderer.md:65-83]()

## Purpose and scope

This page outlines how vLLM connects quantization configurations to layer methods and kernel selection, and how its `FusedMoE` pipeline combines routing with expert execution. It is a parent-page overview; implementation details belong in the linked child pages.

Sources: [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/modelopt.py:176-191](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/layer.py:92-159]()

For details, see:

- [Quantization Methods Overview](#7.1) — Quantization formats, configuration, and the linear kernel selection layer.
- [FP8 and Low-Precision Quantization](#7.2) — FP8, block quantization, MXFP4, NVFP4, and related kernel backends.
- [FusedMoE Layer Architecture](#7.3) — MoE routing, expert execution, and modular pipeline components.
- [MoE Quantization and Backend Selection](#7.4) — MoE quantization methods, backend selection, and parallelism considerations.
- [Custom Kernels and C++/CUDA Extensions](#7.5) — Native extensions, custom-op wrappers, kernel libraries, and warmup.

Sources: [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/modelopt.py:176-191](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/layer.py:18-39](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/quark/quark_moe.py:8-10]()

## Quantization Methods Overview

Quantization configurations describe how methods apply to model layers. For example, `ModelOptQuantConfigBase` (a base class for various ModelOpt quantization schemes like FP8, NVFP4, MXFP8) records checkpoint serialization, activation scheme, ignored layers, and optional weight block size; its `get_quant_method()` selects a method based on layer type. Quantization methods can also connect to kernel initialization, as shown by the FP8 linear implementation importing the `model_executor.kernels.linear` selection functions. For details, see [Quantization Methods Overview](#7.1). [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/modelopt.py:176-191](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/modelopt.py:16-20]()

The codebase also has methods for ModelOpt and Quark formats, alongside MXFP4 support. Their MoE paths integrate with `FusedMoE` method and backend abstractions rather than treating quantization as a standalone format choice. For details, see [FP8 and Low-Precision Quantization](#7.2) and [MoE Quantization and Backend Selection](#7.4). [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/modelopt.py:141-158](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/quark/quark_moe.py:13-18](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/mxfp4.py:86-113]()

Diagram: Quantization configuration to layer method
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Config["QuantizationConfig"] --> ModelOptConfig["ModelOptQuantConfigBase"]
    ModelOptConfig --> Select["get_quant_method()"]
    Select --> Linear["LinearBase"]
    Select --> Experts["RoutedExperts"]
    Linear --> LinearMethod["Linear kernel initialization"]
    Experts --> MoeMethod["FusedMoEMethodBase"]
```

Sources: [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/modelopt.py:176-191](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/modelopt.py:16-20](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/mxfp4.py:86-113]()

---

## FP8 and Low-Precision Quantization

`ModelOptQuantConfigBase` and its subclasses (e.g., `Fp8Config`) support static or dynamic activation schemes and optional block-shaped weight quantization; its configuration validates the activation scheme and block-size requirements. MXFP4 has a dedicated `Mxfp4Config`, whose method selection assigns a MoE method to `RoutedExperts` while leaving unsupported linear and attention cases unquantized. For details, see [FP8 and Low-Precision Quantization](#7.2). [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/modelopt.py:176-191](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/mxfp4.py:55-113]()

MoE low-precision support connects quantization formats to backend oracles. The FP8 oracle defines backend choices including FlashInfer, DeepGEMM, Triton, AITER, and CPU variants; the MXFP4 and NVFP4 oracles likewise define backend families. These choices are part of the MoE execution path, rather than a single universal kernel. For details, see [MoE Quantization and Backend Selection](#7.4). [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/oracle/fp8.py:54-76](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/oracle/mxfp4.py:144-187](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/oracle/nvfp4.py:45-57]()

Sources: [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/modelopt.py:176-191](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/mxfp4.py:55-113](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/oracle/fp8.py:54-76](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/oracle/mxfp4.py:144-187](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/oracle/nvfp4.py:45-57]()

---

## FusedMoE Layer Architecture

`FusedMoEFactory` assembles a MoE execution pipeline from a router, `RoutedExperts`, and a `MoERunner`; it also accepts parallelism, quantization, routing, and expert-related configuration. `make_parallel_config()` derives the MoE parallel configuration from tensor-, data-, and context-parallel inputs. For details, see [FusedMoE Layer Architecture](#7.3). [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/layer.py:47-73](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/layer.py:92-159]()

This separation gives the layer a clear flow: routing produces expert assignments, expert kernels perform the routed work, and the runner coordinates execution. Quantization and backend selection plug into the expert path; routing method types are represented separately in `RoutingMethodType`. For details, see [FusedMoE Layer Architecture](#7.3) and [MoE Quantization and Backend Selection](#7.4). [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/layer.py:30-39](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/config.py:108-136]()

Diagram: FusedMoE concepts mapped to code entities
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Factory["FusedMoEFactory"] --> Router["FusedMoERouter"]
    Factory --> Experts["RoutedExperts"]
    Factory --> Runner["MoERunner"]
    Router --> Assignments["RoutingMethodType"]
    Runner --> Experts
```

Sources: [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/layer.py:30-39](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/layer.py:92-159](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/config.py:108-136]()

## MoE Quantization and Backend Selection

MoE quantization configuration represents activation and weight quantization separately. `FusedMoEQuantDesc` describes data type and quantization group shape, while quantization-specific oracles provide backend selection and map backend choices to expert-kernel classes. For details, see [MoE Quantization and Backend Selection](#7.4). [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/config.py:178-194](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/oracle/nvfp4.py:86-169]()

Backend availability and preference can depend on the platform, quantization keys, and MoE parallel configuration. For example, the FP8 oracle adjusts backend priority for selected CUDA capabilities, expert-parallel configurations, XPU, and CPU. The NVFP4 oracle maps configured backend names to its backend enum. These mechanisms connect quantization formats to platform-specific expert kernels. [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/oracle/fp8.py:84-149](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/oracle/nvfp4.py:174-190]()

Diagram: MoE quantization and backend selection in code
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Method["Fp8MoeMethod or low-precision MoE method"] --> Oracle["select_fp8_moe_backend or format-specific selector"]
    Oracle --> Backend["Fp8MoeBackend or format-specific backend enum"]
    Backend --> KernelMap["backend_to_kernel_cls()"]
    KernelMap --> Experts["Expert kernel classes"]
    Parallel["FusedMoEParallelConfig"] --> Oracle
    QuantKeys["weight_key and activation_key"] --> Oracle
```

Sources: [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/oracle/fp8.py:84-108](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/oracle/fp8.py:153-185](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/oracle/nvfp4.py:86-104]()

## Custom Kernels and C++/CUDA Extensions

The extension layout, build process, kernel libraries, and warmup are covered in [Custom Kernels and C++/CUDA Extensions](#7.5); this parent page does not detail those implementations. ## Purpose and Scope

This page introduces vLLM’s quantization concepts and implementation entry points. It covers the quantization-method registry, FP8 and INT8 quantization descriptors and kernels, GPTQ and AWQ method identifiers, compressed-tensors and Quark configuration (including OCP MX and NVFP4), online quantization entry points, and the linear-kernel import layer under `vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear`. It also describes how routed MoE experts receive quantization configuration via `CompressedTensorsMoEMethod` and `QuarkMoEMethod`, and how the kernel configuration exposes MoE backend choices (`MoEBackend`). [vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/__init__.py:4-12](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors_moe/compressed_tensors_moe.py:26-75](), [vllm/config/kernel.py:122-147]()

Quantization is not a single kernel or format: method names resolve to configuration classes, those configurations select per-layer quantization methods and schemes, and kernel implementations provide execution paths for particular formats and hardware providers. [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors.py:89-117, 159-184](), [vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/__init__.py:21-37, 172-183]()

Sources: [vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/__init__.py:4-12, 21-37, 172-183](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors.py:89-117, 159-184](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors_moe/compressed_tensors_moe.py:26-75](), [vllm/config/kernel.py:122-147]()

---

## Quantization Concepts

Quantization describes values using a lower-precision representation and associated scale metadata. In vLLM’s quantization utilities (`vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/quant_utils.py`), scale descriptors (`ScaleDesc`) and quantization keys (`QuantKey`) define the data types, static vs. dynamic scaling, group shapes (`GroupShape`), and symmetry. [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/quant_utils.py:116-194]()

Quantization granularity spans per-tensor, per-channel, per-token, and block-wise schemes (e.g., OCP MX e8m0 block scales and 128-block FP8 formats). Weights and activation scales are reduced across tensor parallel or expert parallel groups when sharded using helpers like `amax_for_tp_weight_quant` and `amax_for_moe_weight_quant`. [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/quant_utils.py:48-74, 144-167]()

A core distinction exists between checkpoint quantization (how model weights are serialized on disk, e.g., via `compressed-tensors` or `quark`) and online quantization (applying quantization dynamically or wrapping unquantized checkpoints at runtime). 

Sources: [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/quant_utils.py:48-74, 116-194]()

---

## Supported Quantization Methods and Registry

The supported quantization methods include `fp8`, `auto_awq`, `auto_gptq`, `gptq`, `gptq_marlin`, `awq`, `awq_marlin`, `compressed-tensors`, `quark`, and `online`. 

| Method identifier(s) | Configuration class | Implementation details & citation |
|---|---|---|
| `fp8` | `Fp8Config` | Configures FP8 static/dynamic tensor and block scaling. |
| `awq`, `auto_awq`, `awq_marlin` | `AutoAWQConfig` | Resolves to AWQ weight-only quantization methods. |
| `gptq`, `auto_gptq`, `gptq_marlin` | `AutoGPTQConfig` | Resolves to GPTQ quantization configurations. |
| `compressed-tensors` | `CompressedTensorsConfig` | Manages target-to-scheme mappings, sparsity, transform configurations, and KV-cache schemes. [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors.py:89-117]() |
| `quark` | `QuarkConfig` | Handles AMD Quark checkpoints, rotation configs, packing methods, and OCP MX/NVFP4 schemes. [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/quark/quark.py:104-130]() |
| `online` | `OnlineQuantizationConfig` | Handles runtime shorthand quantization formats (e.g., `fp8_per_tensor`, `mxfp8`, `nvfp4_per_token`). |

Sources: [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors.py:89-117](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/quark/quark.py:104-130]()

---

## Configuration Assembly and Method Resolution

Configuration classes parse model metadata and assign appropriate execution methods via `get_quant_method()`. For example, `CompressedTensorsConfig.get_quant_method()` inspects linear layers, matches them against the target-scheme map, and returns either `CompressedTensorsLinearMethod` or `UnquantizedLinearMethod`, wrapping them with `CompressedTensorsLinearTransformMethod` if input/output transforms are present. [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors.py:159-184]()

Similarly, `QuarkConfig` utilizes `apply_vllm_mapper()` to translate HuggingFace layer paths to vLLM's internal naming conventions. [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/quark/quark.py:144-176]()

    QuarkConfig["QuarkConfig"]

    CTLinearMethod["CompressedTensorsLinearMethod"]

    KernelLayer["vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear"]
    ScaledMM["FP8ScaledMMLinearKernel"]

    Method --> CTConfig
    Method --> QuarkConfig
    CTConfig --> GetQuantMethod
    QuarkConfig --> GetQuantMethod

## Kernel Selection and Layer Integration (`model_executor/kernels`)

The linear kernel package (`vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/__init__.py`) provides a stable import boundary, re-exporting mixed-precision, FP8, INT8, MXFP4, MXFP6, MXFP8, and NVFP4 kernel classes by provider and precision. [vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/__init__.py:4-12]()

### MoE Quantization and Routing (`CompressedTensorsMoEMethod`)

For Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) layers, `CompressedTensorsMoEMethod.get_moe_method()` examines the scheme dictionary for gate, up, and down projections across routed experts (`RoutedExperts`), returning specialized MoE methods such as `CompressedTensorsW8A8Fp8MoEMethod`, `CompressedTensorsW4A8Mxfp4MoEMethod`, or `CompressedTensorsW4A4Nvfp4MoEMethod`. [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors_moe/compressed_tensors_moe.py:26-75, 145-168]()

**Diagram: MoE Quantization Dispatch to Execution Backend**

```mermaid
graph TD
    Routed["RoutedExperts"]
    MoEMethod["CompressedTensorsMoEMethod"]
    CheckMXFP4["quant_config._is_mxfp4_w4a8_fp8"]
    CheckNVFP4["quant_config._is_nvfp4_format"]
    CheckFP8["quant_config._is_fp8_w8a8"]
    MethodW8A8["CompressedTensorsW8A8Fp8MoEMethod"]
    MethodNVFP4["CompressedTensorsW4A4Nvfp4MoEMethod"]
    Backend["MoEBackend (triton, deep_gemm, cutlass, etc.)"]

    Routed --> MoEMethod
    MoEMethod --> CheckMXFP4
    MoEMethod --> CheckNVFP4
    MoEMethod --> CheckFP8
    CheckFP8 --> MethodW8A8
    CheckNVFP4 --> MethodNVFP4
    MethodW8A8 --> Backend
    MethodNVFP4 --> Backend
```

Sources: [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors_moe/compressed_tensors_moe.py:26-75, 145-168](), [vllm/config/kernel.py:122-147]()

## Advanced Formats: OCP MX, NVFP4, and Quark Schemes

The Quark integration supports advanced OCP Microscaling Formats (`QuarkOCP_MX`) and NVFP4 (`QuarkNVFP4`). `QuarkOCP_MX` handles `mxfp4`, `mxfp6_e3m2`, `mxfp6_e2m3`, and `mxfp8` weights with block-wise e8m0 scales, managing block expansion and bit packing via `get_packed_dim()` and `_expanding_scale_loader()`. [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/quark/schemes/quark_ocp_mx.py:50-148]()

Sources: [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/quark/schemes/quark_ocp_mx.py:50-148]()

## FP8 Data Types and Platform Considerations

The FP8 utility module recognizes both `torch.float8_e4m3fn` and `torch.float8_e4m3fnuz` as FP8. Its `is_fp8` helper accepts either a dtype or a tensor, converting a tensor argument to its dtype before checking. [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/fp8_utils.py:47-50]()

`QuantFP8` obtains its default FP8 dtype from `current_platform.fp8_dtype()` and derives its minimum and maximum representable values with `get_fp8_min_max()`. The AITER operations module also caches the platform FP8 dtype and defines a set containing the available E4M3 dtype variants (`_FP8_E4M3_DTYPES`). [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/input_quant_fp8.py:16-25]() [vllm/_aiter_ops.py:28-39]()

| Code point | Role |
|---|---|
| `current_platform.fp8_dtype()` | Supplies the platform-selected FP8 dtype used by `QuantFP8`. [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/input_quant_fp8.py:16-25]() |
| `is_fp8` | Recognizes the two E4M3 dtype variants listed in the utility. [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/fp8_utils.py:47-50]() |
| `FP8_DTYPE` | Caches the result of `current_platform.fp8_dtype()` in the AITER operations module. [vllm/_aiter_ops.py:28-32]() |

Sources: [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/fp8_utils.py:47-50](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/input_quant_fp8.py:16-25](), [vllm/_aiter_ops.py:28-39]()

## Quantization Granularities and Data Layouts

`QuantFP8` accepts a `GroupShape` describing per-token, per-tensor, per-channel, or arbitrary block quantization. It records whether the requested shape is per-group and, for group quantization, uses the group’s column dimension as `group_size`. For dynamic non-group quantization, initialization restricts the supported shapes to per-token and per-tensor. [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/input_quant_fp8.py:37-81]()

The output scale layout can be configured for group quantization. `column_major_scales` requests column-major scales, while `tma_aligned_scales` requests a TMA-aligned layout. The dynamic group path forwards these options to `per_token_group_quant_fp8`. [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/input_quant_fp8.py:37-56]() [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/input_quant_fp8.py:106-116]()

| Granularity | Configuration or path | Scale behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Per-tensor | `GroupShape.PER_TENSOR` | Dynamic and static cases are supported through the non-group path; the operation receives the optional static `scale`. [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/input_quant_fp8.py:72-81]() [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/input_quant_fp8.py:118-134]() |
| Per-token | `GroupShape.PER_TOKEN` | Dynamic non-group quantization uses the per-token mode; an optional one-element `scale_ub` is permitted only for this dynamic mode. [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/input_quant_fp8.py:72-81]() [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/input_quant_fp8.py:118-134]() |
| Per-group | A group shape for which `is_per_group()` is true | The group width is `group_shape.col`; dynamic CUDA and XPU paths invoke `per_token_group_quant_fp8`. [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/input_quant_fp8.py:72-81]() [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/input_quant_fp8.py:106-116]() [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/input_quant_fp8.py:171-180]() |
| Static group | Per-group shape with `static=True` | The CUDA method falls through to `scaled_fp8_quant`, passing the configured group shape. [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/input_quant_fp8.py:118-134]() |

Sources: [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/input_quant_fp8.py:37-81](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/input_quant_fp8.py:106-134](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/input_quant_fp8.py:171-180]()

## Scale Factor Formats and `DeepGemmQuantScaleFMT`

`QuantFP8` initializes `use_ue8m0` from `is_deep_gemm_e8m0_used()` unless the caller supplies an explicit value. It separately records whether DeepGEMM is supported. The special packed DeepGEMM quantization path is used only when the input is dynamic group quantization, the group size is 128, UE8M0 is enabled, DeepGEMM is supported, and `DeepGemmQuantScaleFMT.from_oracle()` returns `UE8M0`. [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/input_quant_fp8.py:60-68]() [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/input_quant_fp8.py:92-104]()

The supplied `fp8_utils.py` implementation shows how group scales are formed. For each group, `_per_token_group_quant_fp8` computes an absolute maximum with an epsilon floor, derives a scale from the FP8 maximum, and—when `use_ue8m0` is true—rounds the scale upward to a power of two using `exp2(ceil(log2(...)))`. It divides the group values by that scale, clamps to the FP8 range, stores the quantized values, and writes one scale per group. [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/fp8_utils.py:82-138]()

| Scale path | Behavior visible in the supplied code |
|---|---|
| Ordinary group scale | `scale_raw = absmax * (1.0 / fp8_max)`; this is stored directly when `use_ue8m0` is false. [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/fp8_utils.py:125-138]() |
| UE8M0 group scale | The raw scale is rounded up to the next power of two using `exp2(ceil(log2(scale_raw)))`. [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/fp8_utils.py:127-138]() |
| DeepGEMM packed path | `per_token_group_quant_fp8_packed_for_deepgemm` is selected for the eligible dynamic 128-element group case. [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/input_quant_fp8.py:92-104]() |

`DeepGemmQuantScaleFMT` defines the formats `FLOAT32`, `FLOAT32_CEIL_UE8M0`, and `UE8M0`, initializing via `init_oracle_cache()` and returning decisions through `from_oracle()`. [vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py:58-110]()

Sources: [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/input_quant_fp8.py:17-20](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/input_quant_fp8.py:60-68](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/input_quant_fp8.py:92-104](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/fp8_utils.py:82-138](), [vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py:58-110]()

---

## Scale Tensor Memory Layout Variants

`QuantFP8` exposes two layout options for group scales: `column_major_scales` and `tma_aligned_scales`. The dynamic CUDA group path forwards both options to `per_token_group_quant_fp8`; the dynamic XPU group path forwards `column_major_scales` but does not pass `tma_aligned_scales` in the shown call. [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/input_quant_fp8.py:37-56]() [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/input_quant_fp8.py:106-116]() [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/input_quant_fp8.py:171-180]()

`fp8_utils.py` imports `get_tma_aligned_size` and `transform_sf_into_required_layout` from `vllm.utils.deep_gemm`, showing that scale-layout transformation utilities are part of the FP8 utility layer. [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/fp8_utils.py:32-36]()

## Input Quantization Workflow: `QuantFP8`

`QuantFP8` is registered as a `CustomOp` named `quant_fp8`. Its constructor records static-versus-dynamic mode, the requested group shape, optional token padding, scale layout options, UE8M0 mode, DeepGEMM support, and whether ROCm AITER linear FP8 is enabled. [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/input_quant_fp8.py:28-80]()

On CUDA, `forward_cuda` selects among three broad paths:

1. Eligible dynamic 128-wide group quantization with the UE8M0 scale oracle result calls `per_token_group_quant_fp8_packed_for_deepgemm`. [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/input_quant_fp8.py:92-104]()
2. Other dynamic group quantization calls `per_token_group_quant_fp8`, passing the configured scale layouts and FP8 dtype. [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/input_quant_fp8.py:106-116]()
3. Non-group or static quantization calls `ops.scaled_fp8_quant`, passing the static scale when required, optional `scale_ub`, token padding, and the relevant group-shape information. [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/input_quant_fp8.py:118-134]()

The Triton kernel `_per_token_group_quant_fp8` maps each program to a row and group, loads the group, computes its absolute maximum, calculates a scale, quantizes and clamps values, and stores the quantized group and scale. [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/fp8_utils.py:82-138]()

### Diagram: `QuantFP8.forward_cuda` Dispatch

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    "QuantFP8.forward_cuda" --> "is_dynamic_group_quant"
    "is_dynamic_group_quant" --> "is_UE8M0_DeepGEMM_group_size_128"
    "is_UE8M0_DeepGEMM_group_size_128" --> "per_token_group_quant_fp8_packed_for_deepgemm"
    "is_dynamic_group_quant" --> "other_dynamic_group_path"
    "other_dynamic_group_path" --> "per_token_group_quant_fp8"
    "per_token_group_quant_fp8" --> "_per_token_group_quant_fp8"
    "is_dynamic_group_quant" --> "non_group_or_static_path"
    "non_group_or_static_path" --> "ops.scaled_fp8_quant"
```

Sources: [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/input_quant_fp8.py:28-80](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/input_quant_fp8.py:83-134](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/fp8_utils.py:82-138]()

### Platform-specific activation quantization

On HIP, `forward_hip` uses AITER only when AITER linear FP8 is enabled, `scale_ub` is absent, and the input is contiguous. It then dispatches per-group, per-tensor, or per-token quantization to the corresponding `rocm_aiter_ops` method; otherwise it falls back to `QuantFP8.forward_cuda`. [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/input_quant_fp8.py:136-162]()

On XPU, dynamic group quantization calls `per_token_group_quant_fp8`; other cases are handled by the remainder of the XPU implementation. [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/input_quant_fp8.py:164-180]()

Sources: [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/input_quant_fp8.py:136-180]()

## GEMM Backend Dispatch and Oracle Pattern

The linear-kernel package re-exports implementations grouped under scaled-MM, mixed-precision, MXFP4, MXFP6, MXFP8, and NVFP4 modules. [vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/__init__.py:4-12]() [vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/__init__.py:21-24]() [vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/__init__.py:69-179]()

The configuration module defines a `MoEBackend` literal containing `auto` and named choices including `triton`, `deep_gemm`, `cutlass`, multiple FlashInfer variants, `aiter`, `emulation`, and others. [vllm/config/kernel.py:122-147]()

### Linear FP8 kernel example: XPU

`XPUW8A8FP8LinearKernel` supports XPU and declares accepted activation quantization keys for dynamic/static per-tensor and per-token modes. Its weight keys are static per-channel and per-tensor. `can_implement` rejects unsupported keys and FP8 dtypes other than `torch.float8_e5m2` and `torch.float8_e4m3fn`. [vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/scaled_mm/xpu.py:23-63]()

After loading, the XPU W8A8 kernel ensures the weight is in C-contiguous `[K, N]` form. Its `apply_scaled_mm` calls `torch.ops._xpu_C.fp8_gemm` with activations, weights, output dtype, activation and weight scales, optional bias, and then reshapes the result. [vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/scaled_mm/xpu.py:70-98]() [vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/scaled_mm/xpu.py:100-119]()

Sources: [vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/scaled_mm/xpu.py:23-63](), [vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/scaled_mm/xpu.py:70-119]()

## MXFP4 and NVFP4 Quantization Implementations

### MXFP4

The linear-kernel exports include `MxFp4LinearKernel` and `MxFp4LinearLayerConfig`, together with provider or implementation classes for AITER, B12x, emulation, FlashInfer, Humming, Marlin, PyTorch, and XPU. [vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/__init__.py:69-95]()

The ROCm AITER implementation defines `AiterMxfp4LinearKernel`. Its support check requires that the current platform supports MX computation; the implementation also queries whether AITER is available and checks the configured linear backend and disabled-kernel list. [vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/mxfp4/aiter.py:157-185]()

The AITER helper `gemm_with_dynamic_quant` can dynamically quantize activations with `dynamic_mxfp4_quant` when activation scales are not already provided, then invokes AITER GEMM. [vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/mxfp4/aiter.py:44-134]()

The `mxfp4_utils.py` module provides utilities for MXFP4 quantization, including functions to determine if specific ROCm platforms use swizzled scale layouts. [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/mxfp4_utils.py:16-45]() The `_swizzle_mxfp4` function handles weight swizzling for MXFP4 MoE, adapting to different Triton kernel versions and CUDA/ROCm platforms. [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/mxfp4_utils.py:65-171]()

### NVFP4

The linear-kernel exports include `NvFp4LinearKernel`, its layer config, and implementations or adapters named B12x, CUTLASS, emulation, FBGEMM, FlashInfer, Humming, Marlin, and PyTorch. [vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/__init__.py:138-170]()

The `flashinfer_fp4_moe.py` module provides specific utilities for NVFP4 with FlashInfer fused-MoE, including `reorder_w1w3_to_w3w1` and `interleave_linear_and_gate`. [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/flashinfer_fp4_moe.py:38-87]() The `_shard_nvfp4_moe_weights_per_die` function handles sharding of NVFP4 MoE weights across locality domains. [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/flashinfer_fp4_moe.py:119-182]()

## Block Quantization, ModelOpt, and Quark MoE Support

`Fp8Config` handles FP8 quantization with options for checkpoint serialization, activation schemes (`static` or `dynamic`), ignored layers, and `weight_block_size`. [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/fp8.py:89-133]()

ModelOpt integration defines linear algorithms (`LINEAR_ALGOS`) covering FP8, NVFP4, W4A16_NVFP4, and MXFP8, mapped via `ModelOptQuantConfigBase`, `ModelOptFp8Config`, `ModelOptNvFp4Config`, and `ModelOptMxFp8Config` [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/modelopt.py:150-163] [tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py:36-43].

Quark MoE methods (`QuarkMoEMethod`, `QuarkW4A8Fp8MoEMethod`, `QuarkNvfp4MoEMethod`, `QuarkW8A8Mxfp8MoEMethod`, etc.) parse quantization targets, weights, and input tensor hints for mixture-of-experts layers [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/quark/quark_moe.py:141-206].

Sources: [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/fp8.py:89-133](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/modelopt.py:150-163](), [tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py:36-43](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/quark/quark_moe.py:141-206]()

## DeepGEMM Utilities and Support

The FP8 quantization module imports DeepGEMM helpers for TMA-aligned sizes, scale-format selection, and transforming scale factors into required layouts. `QuantFP8` uses `is_deep_gemm_supported`, `is_deep_gemm_e8m0_used`, and `DeepGemmQuantScaleFMT.from_oracle()` to determine whether the specialized packed dynamic group path applies. [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/fp8_utils.py:32-36]() [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/input_quant_fp8.py:17-20]() [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/input_quant_fp8.py:60-68]() [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/input_quant_fp8.py:92-104]()

CMake integration accepts a local DeepGEMM source tree via `DEEPGEMM_SRC_DIR`; otherwise it fetches a pinned vLLM-project revision. It determines supported CUDA architecture targets and builds the `_deep_gemm_C` extension target [cmake/external_projects/deepgemm.cmake:3-140].

## Purpose and Scope

This page describes vLLM’s fused Mixture-of-Experts execution architecture: the modular kernel interfaces, expert computation, backend selection, routing, and the roles of the `experts/`, `oracle/`, `runner/`, and prepare/finalize components. It focuses on code entities visible in the provided source excerpts; backend-specific behavior is described only where those excerpts show it [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/modular_kernel.py:51-85]().

Sources: [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/modular_kernel.py:51-85]()

---

## Core FusedMoE Class and Initialization

`FusedMoE` is the main class for a Mixture-of-Experts layer. It initializes with a `FusedMoEConfig` and a `FusedMoEQuantConfig`. It selects a `FusedMoEPrepareAndFinalize` implementation and a `FusedMoEExpertsModular` implementation based on the configuration [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/__init__.py:100-108]().

The `FusedMoE` layer manages the weights for the experts. For example, `w13_weight` stores the fused first projection weights (gate and up projections), and `w2_weight` stores the down-projection weights. These are registered as non-trainable parameters [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/__init__.py:110-130]().

### Diagram: FusedMoE Initialization Flow

```mermaid
graph LR
    A["FusedMoE.__init__"] --> B["FusedMoEConfig"]
    A --> C["FusedMoEQuantConfig"]
    A --> D["FusedMoEFactory.select_moe_implementation"]
    D --> E["prepare_finalize_cls"]
    D --> F["experts_cls"]
    A --> G["self.prepare_finalize = prepare_finalize_cls(...)"]
    A --> H["self.experts = experts_cls(...)"]
    A --> I["self.w13_weight"]
    A --> J["self.w2_weight"]
```

Sources: [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/__init__.py:100-130]()

### Weight Layout and Dimensions

| Parameter | Role |
|---|---|
| `w13_weight` | Per-expert fused first projection (gate and up). Its output dimension is `intermediate_size * 2` for gated activations [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/__init__.py:110-119](). |
| `w2_weight` | Per-expert down projection. Shape is `(num_experts, hidden_size, intermediate_size)` [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/__init__.py:120-129](). |
| `w13_bias`, `w2_bias` | Optional biases for the projections, created if `moe_config.add_bias` is true [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/__init__.py:130-139](). |

Sources: [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/__init__.py:110-139]()

---

## Modular Kernel Architecture

The modular design separates expert routing, input preparation and dispatch, expert computation, and output combination. The design goal stated in `modular_kernel.py` is to let communication mechanisms be combined with fused MoE kernels without requiring a separate implementation for every combination. The file describes the high-level pipeline as Router → Quantize-Dispatch → Permute-Experts-Unpermute → Combine [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/modular_kernel.py:51-85]().

`FusedMoEPrepareAndFinalize` provides the abstract prepare/finalize interface. Its modular variant operates on top-K IDs and weights, while the monolithic variant operates on router logits. `FusedMoEExpertsModular` represents the main expert operation—matrix multiplication, activation/multiplication, and optionally quantization and a second matrix multiplication. `FusedMoEModularKernel` combines a prepare/finalize implementation with an expert implementation [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/modular_kernel.py:65-85](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/modular_kernel.py:186-193]().

The `TopKWeightAndReduce` interface lets the expert implementation determine how routing weights are applied and how expert outputs are reduced. Its `apply` method receives an optional output buffer, fused expert output, top-K weights and IDs, and a flag indicating whether router weights are applied on the input [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/modular_kernel.py:126-142]().

### Pipeline Architecture

```mermaid
graph LR
    A["Router"] --> B["FusedMoEPrepareAndFinalize.prepare"]
    B --> C["Quantize_and_dispatch"]
    C --> D["FusedMoEExpertsModular.apply"]
    D --> E["TopKWeightAndReduce"]
    E --> F["FusedMoEPrepareAndFinalize.finalize"]
    F --> G["Combined_MoE_output"]
```

Sources: [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/modular_kernel.py:51-85](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/modular_kernel.py:126-142](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/modular_kernel.py:186-193]()

### Modular Kernel Interfaces

| Interface | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `FusedMoEPrepareAndFinalize` | Abstract base for the prepare and finalize phases. The modular interface works with top-K IDs and weights; the monolithic interface works with router logits [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/modular_kernel.py:186-193](). |
| `FusedMoEExpertsModular` | Abstract expert-computation interface for the fused MoE operation, including the projection/activation/projection sequence [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/modular_kernel.py:65-75](). |
| `FusedMoEModularKernel` | Combines a prepare/finalize implementation and an expert implementation into the standard modular kernel interface [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/modular_kernel.py:76-85](). |
| `TopKWeightAndReduce` | Defines how top-K routing weights are applied and expert outputs reduced [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/modular_kernel.py:126-142](). |
| `ExpertTokensMetadata` | Carries per-expert token counts, with optional CPU and GPU count tensors, per-rank receive counts, and a rank expert offset [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/modular_kernel.py:99-108](). |

`PrepareResultType` makes the modular prepare boundary explicit: it can return prepared activations, optional activation scales, optional expert-token metadata, optional dispatched top-K IDs, and optional dispatched top-K weights [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/modular_kernel.py:145-163]().

Sources: [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/modular_kernel.py:65-85](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/modular_kernel.py:99-108](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/modular_kernel.py:126-163](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/modular_kernel.py:186-193]()

---

## Expert Execution Backends and Oracle Selection

The `FusedMoEFactory` is responsible for selecting the appropriate MoE implementation (prepare/finalize and expert classes) based on the `FusedMoEConfig` and `FusedMoEQuantConfig`. It uses an oracle system to determine the best backend [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/__init__.py:150-158]().

The oracle system considers various factors like quantization scheme, hardware capabilities, and parallel configuration to select the most performant backend, such as selecting WNA16 backends via `select_wna16_moe_backend` [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors_moe/compressed_tensors_moe_wna16.py:101-108]().

### Backend Selection Diagram

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["FusedMoEFactory.select_moe_implementation"] --> B["Oracle_system"]
    B --> C{"Quantization_Scheme?"}
    C -- "Unquantized" --> D["UnquantizedMoeBackend"]
    C -- "FP8" --> E["Fp8MoeBackend"]
    C -- "WNA16/INT4/INT8" --> F["WNA16MoEBackend"]
    D --> G["prepare_finalize_cls"]
    D --> H["experts_cls"]
    E --> G
    E --> H
    F --> G
    F --> H
```

Sources: [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/__init__.py:150-158](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors_moe/compressed_tensors_moe_wna16.py:101-108]()

### Backend and Kernel Examples

- **Triton:** `TritonExperts` is a general-purpose Triton-based implementation. It supports various quantization schemes (INT8, FP8) and activations. The `fused_moe_kernel_gptq_awq` kernel in `fused_moe.py` handles quantized weights (GPTQ/AWQ) [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/triton_moe.py:67-70](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/triton_moe.py:128-180](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/fused_moe.py:64-111]().
- **Marlin:** `MarlinExperts` and batched Marlin variants provide optimized kernels for quantized (INT4, INT8, FP8) MoE layers, used for AWQ/GPTQ [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/oracle/int_wna16.py:83-86]().
- **Humming / Batched Grouped Experts:** `HummingGroupedExperts` integrates specialized GEMM operations and tuning configurations [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/oracle/int_wna16.py:71-82]().

Sources: [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/triton_moe.py:67-70](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/triton_moe.py:128-180](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/fused_moe.py:64-111](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/oracle/int_wna16.py:71-86]()

---

## Router Implementations

The `MoERunner` layer uses a router to determine which experts each token should be dispatched to. Routers are responsible for taking gating outputs and calculating top-K expert assignments and weights [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/router/router_factory.py:15-20]().

Common router types and routing methodologies in vLLM include top-K routing (`fused_topk`), bias-corrected routing, and grouped expert routing.

### Router-to-Execution Data Flow

```mermaid
graph LR
    A["hidden_states"] --> B["MoERunner.forward"]
    B --> C["GateLinear"]
    C --> D["Router"]
    D -- "gating_output" --> E["fused_topk"]
    E --> F["topk_weights, topk_ids"]
    F --> G["FusedMoEPrepareAndFinalize.prepare"]
    G --> H["Expert_execution"]
    H --> I["Weighted_expert_output"]
```

Sources: [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/router/router_factory.py:15-20](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/router/fused_topk_router.py:15-36]()

---

## Sub-modules: Experts, Oracle, Runner, and Prepare/Finalize

The codebase organizes MoE logic into distinct sub-modules:

| Area | Role |
|---|---|
| `experts/` | Implements expert kernels for various hardware and quantization schemes (e.g., Triton, Marlin, Humming, XPU) [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/triton_moe.py:67-70](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/oracle/int_wna16.py:67-123](). |
| `oracle/` | Selects the optimal MoE backend (prepare/finalize and expert classes) based on configuration, hardware, and quantization (e.g., `select_wna16_moe_backend`) [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors_moe/compressed_tensors_moe_wna16.py:101-108](). |
| `runner/` | Orchestrates the MoE forward pass, including routing and dispatching to experts [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/runner/moe_runner.py:112-134](). |
| Prepare/finalize | Groups input preparation (quantization, dispatch, all-to-all communication) and output finalization [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/modular_kernel.py:186-193](). |

Sources: [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/triton_moe.py:67-70](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/oracle/int_wna16.py:67-123](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors_moe/compressed_tensors_moe_wna16.py:101-108](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/runner/moe_runner.py:112-134](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/modular_kernel.py:186-193]()

### Diagram: Natural Language Responsibilities to Code Entities

```mermaid
graph LR
    A["Expert_computation"] --> B["vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.experts.triton_moe.TritonExperts"]
    A --> C["vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.experts.marlin_moe.MarlinExperts"]
    D["Backend_choice"] --> E["vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.oracle.int_wna16.select_wna16_moe_backend"]
    F["Layer_forward_dispatch"] --> G["vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.runner.moe_runner.MoERunner.forward"]
    H["Input_preparation"] --> I["vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.modular_kernel.FusedMoEPrepareAndFinalize"]
    J["TopK_weighting_and_reduction"] --> K["vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.modular_kernel.TopKWeightAndReduce"]
    L["Routing_logic"] --> M["vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.router.router_factory.create_fused_moe_router"]
```

Sources: [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/triton_moe.py:67-70](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/oracle/int_wna16.py:67-123](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/runner/moe_runner.py:112-134](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/modular_kernel.py:65-85](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/modular_kernel.py:126-142](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/router/router_factory.py:15-20]()

---

## Summary

The modular MoE design separates preparation/finalization, expert computation, and top-K weight application/reduction, allowing those interfaces to be combined flexibly [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/modular_kernel.py:51-85](). The oracle and factory systems select optimal implementations based on hardware and quantization constraints [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/__init__.py:150-158](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors_moe/compressed_tensors_moe_wna16.py:101-108]().

Sources: [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/modular_kernel.py:51-85](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/__init__.py:150-158](), [vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors_moe/compressed_tensors_moe_wna16.py:101-108]()
