## CUDA `base` Stage and Build Pipeline

The CUDA Dockerfile’s `base` stage derives from `BUILD_BASE_IMAGE`, defaulting to a PyTorch manylinux CUDA 13 builder matching the glibc floor of PyTorch's published wheels [docker/Dockerfile:36-47](). It configures `uv` virtual environments under `/opt/venv` and `/opt/uv` to prevent root-owned layout blocks in downstream layers [docker/Dockerfile:116-131]().

System dependencies include `ccache`, `git`, `curl`, `sudo`, `elfutils-devel`, and `rdma-core-devel`. When `USE_SCCACHE=1`, an architecture-specific sccache binary is downloaded and installed [docker/Dockerfile:133-157]().

**Diagram: CUDA `base` setup flow**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    BUILD_BASE["BUILD_BASE_IMAGE"]
    BASE["base"]
    UV_ENV["UV paths and /opt/venv"]
    DNF["dnf build dependencies"]
    SCCACHE_FLAG["USE_SCCACHE"]
    PLATFORM["TARGETPLATFORM"]
    SCCACHE["sccache installation"]

    BUILD_BASE --> BASE
    UV_ENV --> BASE
    DNF --> BASE
    BASE --> SCCACHE_FLAG
    SCCACHE_FLAG --> PLATFORM
    PLATFORM --> SCCACHE
```

Sources: [docker/Dockerfile:36-47](), [docker/Dockerfile:101-103](), [docker/Dockerfile:116-157]()

---

## CPU Dockerfile Stages

`docker/Dockerfile.cpu` provides multi-platform builds (`linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`) with dedicated targets for serving (`vllm-openai`), testing (`vllm-test`), and development (`vllm-dev`) [docker/Dockerfile.cpu:1-20](). 

It features a `binutils-build` stage to compile newer GNU assemblers supporting the AMX-FP8 instruction set [docker/Dockerfile.cpu:55-78](). The `base-common-pydeps` stage handles conditional PyTorch nightly installation alongside `requirements/cpu.txt` [docker/Dockerfile.cpu:139-165]().

Sources: [docker/Dockerfile.cpu:1-165]()

---

## ROCm Dockerfile Stages

`docker/Dockerfile.rocm` manages AMD ROCm builds, integrating specialized stages such as `build_nixl` (building UCX and NIXL with ROCm support) and `lmcache_source` (fetching and filtering LMCache dependencies) [docker/Dockerfile.rocm:37-160](). It configures `uv` with copy link modes to prevent hardlink issues across Docker cache mounts [docker/Dockerfile.rocm:28-35]().

Sources: [docker/Dockerfile.rocm:1-160]()

---

## Build Optimization and Caching

The build pipelines employ several caching and optimization mechanisms:

| Mechanism | Role in the build pipeline |
|---|---|
| `/opt/uv` and `/opt/venv` layout | Places uv-managed binaries, cache, Python, and the virtual environment under shared paths accessible to descendant stages [docker/Dockerfile:116-131](). |
| `ccache` & `sccache` | Integrated across CUDA, CPU, and ROCm stages to cache object files locally or remotely via S3 buckets [docker/Dockerfile:133-157](), [docker/Dockerfile.cpu:41-53](), [docker/Dockerfile.rocm:66-107](). |
| BuildKit cache mounts | Used extensively for `/root/.cache/uv` and `/root/.cache/ccache` during package and extension compilation [docker/Dockerfile.rocm:18-33](). |
| Binutils bin customization | Compiles newer binutils during CPU builds to support advanced instruction sets like AMX-FP8 [docker/Dockerfile.cpu:55-78](). |

Sources: [docker/Dockerfile:116-157](), [docker/Dockerfile.cpu:41-78](), [docker/Dockerfile.rocm:18-107]()

---

## Image Variants and Build Entry Points

Release pipelines invoke Docker builds for wheel production, while publishing scripts promote images across registries [`.buildkite/release-pipeline.yaml:21-50](), [.buildkite/scripts/publish-release-images.sh:5-18]()`.

| Build or publication path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| CUDA wheel build | Runs `docker build` on `docker/Dockerfile` targeting `--target build` for `x86_64` and `aarch64` architectures [`.buildkite/release-pipeline.yaml:21-50]()`. |
| CUDA release image family | Pulls staging images from ECR, pushes architecture-specific tags, and constructs multi-architecture `latest` and versioned manifests [`.buildkite/scripts/publish-release-images.sh:24-53]()`. |
| ROCm & XPU variants | Promotes specialized device images and tag mirrors under `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm` and `vllm/vllm-openai-xpu` [`.buildkite/scripts/publish-release-images.sh:119-169]()`. |
| CPU image family | Executes an all-or-nothing check across architectures before publishing CPU serving containers [`.buildkite/scripts/publish-release-images.sh:171-177]()`. |

Sources: [`.buildkite/release-pipeline.yaml:21-50](), [.buildkite/scripts/publish-release-images.sh:5-177]()

---

## Build Arguments and Version Management

Dockerfiles source default argument values directly, which are synchronized to `docker/versions.json` via `tools/generate_versions_json.py` [docker/Dockerfile:8-23]().

| Argument | Default Value | Purpose |
|---|---:|---|
| `CUDA_VERSION` | `13.0.3` | Specifies the CUDA version for runtime base images [docker/Dockerfile:25-27](). |
| `PYTHON_VERSION` | `3.12` | Default Python version for the build environment [docker/Dockerfile:25-27](). |
| `UBUNTU_VERSION` | `24.04` | Base Ubuntu release version [docker/Dockerfile:25-27](). |
| `NCCL_VERSION` | `2.31.2` | Pinned NCCL version ensuring DeepEPv2 and runtime compatibility [docker/Dockerfile:31-35](). |
| `INSTALL_KV_CONNECTORS` | `false` | Enables built-in KV-connector dependency libraries [docker/Dockerfile:93-95](). |

Sources: [docker/Dockerfile:8-47](), [docker/versions.json:1-89]()

---

## Summary

The vLLM Docker multi-stage build system leverages specialized base images, remote/local caching via `sccache` and `ccache`, modular Python virtual environments managed by `uv`, and platform-specific Dockerfiles (`Dockerfile`, `Dockerfile.cpu`, `Dockerfile.rocm`) to produce optimized serving, testing, and development images across CUDA, ROCm, XPU, and CPU backends [docker/Dockerfile:1-157](), [docker/Dockerfile.cpu:1-165](), [docker/Dockerfile.rocm:1-162]().

Sources: [docker/Dockerfile:1-157](), [docker/Dockerfile.cpu:1-165](), [docker/Dockerfile.rocm:1-162]()

## Purpose and scope

This page describes vLLM’s shared and test dependency declarations, PyTorch version checks during native builds, precompiled Rust extension detection, and the connection between Python packaging and CMake. The supplied build configuration identifies supported Python versions and expected CUDA/ROCm PyTorch versions; these need to stay aligned with dependency declarations and platform build inputs. [CMakeLists.txt:49-52](), [CMakeLists.txt:65-84]()

Sources: [CMakeLists.txt:49-52](), [CMakeLists.txt:65-84]()

---

## Requirements Files Overview

The requirements tree separates shared runtime constraints from platform and test dependencies. `requirements/common.txt` contains broadly shared runtime dependencies, including Transformers, serving libraries, serialization, and multimodal support. The supplied test inputs include the shared file and add test tools and feature-specific packages. [requirements/common.txt:1-62](), [requirements/test/cuda.in:1-47](), [requirements/test/rocm.in:1-44]()

The supplied test lock files are generated by `uv pip compile`. CUDA and ROCm lock generation uses the corresponding platform requirements as a constraint; the XPU lock also uses `requirements/xpu.txt` as a constraint. The CUDA lock command specifies a PyTorch backend, target platform, and Python version. The ROCm lock command excludes PyTorch and related packages from the emitted lock output. [requirements/test/cuda.txt:1-2](), [requirements/test/rocm.txt:1-2](), [requirements/test/xpu.txt:1-2]()

| File | Role evidenced by the supplied files |
|---|---|
| `requirements/common.txt` | Shared runtime dependency constraints. [requirements/common.txt:1-62]() |
| `requirements/test/cuda.in` | CUDA test input; includes `common.txt`, test dependencies, and explicit PyTorch-related pins. [requirements/test/cuda.in:1-2](), [requirements/test/cuda.in:31-44]() |
| `requirements/test/rocm.in` | ROCm test input; includes `common.txt` and ROCm test extras. [requirements/test/rocm.in:1-2](), [requirements/test/rocm.in:106-111]() |
| `requirements/test/cuda.txt` | Generated CUDA test lock file. [requirements/test/cuda.txt:1-2]() |
| `requirements/test/rocm.txt` | Generated ROCm test lock file. [requirements/test/rocm.txt:1-2]() |
| `requirements/test/xpu.txt` | Generated XPU test lock file. [requirements/test/xpu.txt:1-2]() |
| `requirements/test/cpu.txt` | Generated CPU test lock file, compiled from the CUDA test input with a CPU PyTorch backend. [requirements/test/cpu.txt:1-2]() |

Sources: [requirements/common.txt:1-62](), [requirements/test/cuda.in:1-47](), [requirements/test/rocm.in:1-44](), [requirements/test/cuda.txt:1-2](), [requirements/test/rocm.txt:1-2](), [requirements/test/xpu.txt:1-2](), [requirements/test/cpu.txt:1-2]()

## Core Runtime Dependencies (`common.txt`)

`requirements/common.txt` defines shared constraints rather than a fully locked environment. Notable groups include:

- **Model and tokenizer ecosystem:** `transformers`, `huggingface_hub`, `tokenizers`, `sentencepiece`, and `safetensors`. [requirements/common.txt:4-14]()
- **Serving and API libraries:** FastAPI, Starlette, `aiohttp`, `openai`, and Pydantic. [requirements/common.txt:17-23]()
- **Structured output and schema support:** `lm-format-enforcer`, `llguidance`, `outlines_core`, `lark`, `xgrammar`, and `jsonschema`. [requirements/common.txt:28-36]()
- **Multimodal and media dependencies:** Pillow, `mistral_common[image]`, and `opencv-python-headless`. [requirements/common.txt:25-40]()
- **Serialization, communication, and observability:** `pyzmq`, `msgspec`, `cbor2`, and OpenTelemetry packages. [requirements/common.txt:37-38](), [requirements/common.txt:52-62]()
- **Build and compilation support:** `setuptools` and `ninja`. [requirements/common.txt:42-50]()

Several constraints include platform markers or upper bounds. For example, protobuf uses a platform-specific version rule for `s390x`, while `llguidance` and `xgrammar` restrict installation by machine architecture. [requirements/common.txt:15-16](), [requirements/common.txt:29-33]()

Sources: [requirements/common.txt:4-16](), [requirements/common.txt:17-40](), [requirements/common.txt:42-62]()

---

## Platform-Specific Dependencies and Test Inputs

### CUDA Test Dependencies

The supplied CUDA test input includes `common.txt`, test runners and utilities, multimodal test dependencies, evaluation packages, and explicit PyTorch-family pins. It pins `torch==2.14.0`, `torchaudio==2.11.0`, and `torchvision==0.29.0`; it also pins Transformers for this test environment. [requirements/test/cuda.in:1-2](), [requirements/test/cuda.in:31-44]()

The generated CUDA lock header records that compilation used `--torch-backend cu130`, a manylinux target, and Python 3.12, with `requirements/cuda.txt` as a constraint. [requirements/test/cuda.txt:1-2]()

### ROCm Test Dependencies

The ROCm test input shares the common dependency base and adds test and ROCm-relevant packages. It constrains `ray[default]` to `>=2.56.0,<2.57`, and includes test packages such as `bitsandbytes` and `tilelang`. The file also has a ROCm-specific extras section. [requirements/test/rocm.in:1-2](), [requirements/test/rocm.in:22-44](), [requirements/test/rocm.in:106-111]()

The generated ROCm lock command constrains against `requirements/rocm.txt` and excludes PyTorch and a number of CUDA-related packages from the emitted output. [requirements/test/rocm.txt:1-2]()

### XPU and CPU Test Locks

The supplied XPU lock is generated using `requirements/xpu.txt` as a constraint, with a manylinux target and Python 3.12. The CPU test lock is generated from the CUDA test input using the CPU PyTorch backend. [requirements/test/xpu.txt:1-2](), [requirements/test/cpu.txt:1-2]()

Sources: [requirements/test/cuda.in:1-2](), [requirements/test/cuda.in:31-44](), [requirements/test/cuda.txt:1-2](), [requirements/test/rocm.in:1-2](), [requirements/test/rocm.in:22-44](), [requirements/test/rocm.in:106-111](), [requirements/test/rocm.txt:1-2](), [requirements/test/xpu.txt:1-2](), [requirements/test/cpu.txt:1-2]()

---

## PyTorch Version Handling

PyTorch version requirements are represented in more than one part of the build configuration:

1. The CUDA test input explicitly pins PyTorch and its associated audio and vision packages. [requirements/test/cuda.in:31-33]()
2. `CMakeLists.txt` defines expected CUDA and ROCm Torch versions as `2.14.0`. Its comments state that a mismatch currently results in a warning rather than an error. [CMakeLists.txt:65-75]()
3. CMake detects `TORCH_NIGHTLY_BUILD` only when the environment variable `TORCH_NIGHTLY` is exactly `"1"`. [CMakeLists.txt:76-84]()

The CMake configuration comments state that the CUDA Torch version is derived from `pyproject.toml` and various `requirements.txt` files, and the ROCm Torch version from `docker/Dockerfile.rocm`; these values should remain consistent. [CMakeLists.txt:67-72]()

| Build input or setting | Behavior shown |
|---|---|
| `TORCH_SUPPORTED_VERSION_CUDA` | Expected CUDA Torch version: `2.14.0`. [CMakeLists.txt:74-75]() |
| `TORCH_SUPPORTED_VERSION_ROCM` | Expected ROCm Torch version: `2.14.0`. [CMakeLists.txt:74-75]() |
| `TORCH_NIGHTLY=1` | Marks the CMake build as nightly for the supported-version check. [CMakeLists.txt:76-84]() |
| Other `TORCH_NIGHTLY` values, including `0` | Do not satisfy the exact `"1"` test and therefore do not mark the build as nightly. [CMakeLists.txt:76-84]() |

CMake adds the selected Python installation’s Torch CMake prefix and then calls `find_package(Torch REQUIRED)`. [CMakeLists.txt:87-101](), [CMakeLists.txt:109-115]()

Sources: [requirements/test/cuda.in:31-33](), [CMakeLists.txt:65-84](), [CMakeLists.txt:87-101](), [CMakeLists.txt:109-115]()

---

## Precompiled Wheels and Rust Frontend Integration

### Precompiled Rust Extension Detection

`setup.py` identifies the Rust frontend artifact directory and discovers installed-style extension files globbing `vllm/_rust_*.so`. It reads `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED` from the loaded environment module and uses that setting, or `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED_RUST`, to derive whether the precompiled Rust frontend is enabled. [setup.py:49-67](), [setup.py:74-75]()

### Python Packaging and Native Build Entities

`CMakeLists.txt` requires CMake 3.26 and sets C++20, CUDA 20, and HIP 20 language standards. It requires an explicitly supplied `VLLM_PYTHON_EXECUTABLE`, checks supported Python versions, adds the Torch CMake prefix path, and requires Torch via `find_package(Torch REQUIRED)`. [CMakeLists.txt:1-21](), [CMakeLists.txt:49-52](), [CMakeLists.txt:87-101](), [CMakeLists.txt:109-115]()

The CMake project sets `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE` to CUDA by default. [CMakeLists.txt:32-38]()

**Diagram: Build Configuration and Native Targets**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    cmake["CMakeLists.txt"]
    findTorch["find_package(Torch REQUIRED)"]
    spinloopTarget["spinloop"]
    fsIoTarget["fs_io_C"]
    bindingsCpp["csrc/torch_bindings.cpp"]
    opsH["csrc/ops.h"]
    customOps["vllm/_custom_ops.py"]

    cmake --> findTorch
    findTorch --> spinloopTarget
    findTorch --> fsIoTarget
    spinloopTarget --> bindingsCpp
    fsIoTarget --> opsH
    bindingsCpp --> customOps
```

Sources: [CMakeLists.txt:1-21](), [CMakeLists.txt:87-115](), [csrc/torch_bindings.cpp:1-10](), [csrc/ops.h:1-12](), [vllm/_custom_ops.py:1-21]()

### CMake Extension Targets and Installation

The CMake project defines pure-C++ `spinloop` and `fs_io_C` extension targets before the non-CUDA device branch. Both target the `vllm` package destination and use the CPython stable ABI at version 3.11. [CMakeLists.txt:137-167]()

For non-CUDA and non-ROCm targets, CMake includes `cmake/cpu_extension.cmake` when the selected device is `cpu`, then returns before the CUDA/ROCm build path. [CMakeLists.txt:170-178]()

**Diagram: Python Setup to CMake Execution Flow**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    setupPy["setup.py"]
    cmakeProj["CMakeLists.txt"]
    pyExec["VLLM_PYTHON_EXECUTABLE"]
    torchPkg["torch"]
    extTarget["define_extension_target"]

    setupPy -->|"invokes CMake"| cmakeProj
    cmakeProj --> pyExec
    pyExec --> torchPkg
    torchPkg --> extTarget
```

Sources: [setup.py:17-23](), [CMakeLists.txt:87-115](), [CMakeLists.txt:137-178]()

---

## Build-Time Device and Python Selection

CMake requires callers to provide `VLLM_PYTHON_EXECUTABLE`. It searches supported Python versions in order, with the list declared as Python 3.11, 3.12, 3.13, and 3.14. [CMakeLists.txt:49-52](), [CMakeLists.txt:87-96]()

CMake’s top-level target defaults to `cuda`, but it can be overridden with `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE`. [CMakeLists.txt:32-38](), [CMakeLists.txt:170-178]()

Sources: [CMakeLists.txt:32-38](), [CMakeLists.txt:49-52](), [CMakeLists.txt:87-96](), [CMakeLists.txt:170-178]()

---

## Summary

Dependency declarations are layered: `requirements/common.txt` supplies shared runtime constraints, test `.in` files add test-specific packages, and generated platform lock files record resolved environments and their compile settings. [requirements/common.txt:1-62](), [requirements/test/cuda.in:1-2](), [requirements/test/rocm.in:1-2](), [requirements/test/cuda.txt:1-2](), [requirements/test/rocm.txt:1-2](), [requirements/test/xpu.txt:1-2](), [requirements/test/cpu.txt:1-2]()

PyTorch compatibility is checked during CMake configuration against expected CUDA and ROCm versions, with an exact `TORCH_NIGHTLY=1` condition for nightly builds. [CMakeLists.txt:65-115](), [setup.py:49-93](), [setup.py:202-206]()

Sources: [requirements/common.txt:1-62](), [requirements/test/cuda.in:1-2](), [requirements/test/rocm.in:1-2](), [requirements/test/cuda.txt:1-2](), [requirements/test/rocm.txt:1-2](), [requirements/test/xpu.txt:1-2](), [requirements/test/cpu.txt:1-2](), [CMakeLists.txt:65-115](), [setup.py:49-93](), [setup.py:202-206]()

## Purpose and Scope

This page explains the build variants and configuration inputs evidenced in the supplied files: CUDA, ROCm, XPU, and CPU builds; nightly PyTorch builds; ARM64 targets; and selected build-time options. The available file excerpts do not provide full implementation details for an s390x build beyond references in `setup.py`, so this page focuses primarily on documented platform paths and configuration options [docker/Dockerfile:25-47](), [setup.py:142-149](), [requirements/cuda.txt:1-33](), [requirements/xpu.txt:1-23](), [docker/Dockerfile.cpu:1-18](), [.buildkite/release-pipeline.yaml:21-45]().

Sources: [docker/Dockerfile:25-47](), [setup.py:142-149](), [requirements/cuda.txt:1-33](), [requirements/xpu.txt:1-23](), [docker/Dockerfile.cpu:1-18](), [.buildkite/release-pipeline.yaml:21-45]()

---

## Build Variant Overview

The build configuration is distributed across platform-specific requirements, Dockerfiles, and CI pipeline settings. CUDA has a primary Dockerfile with configurable CUDA and base-image arguments, plus NVIDIA-specific dependencies. XPU has its own requirements and Dockerfile; CPU has a dedicated Dockerfile with CPU-specific targets and a PyTorch-nightly option. Release CI also builds CUDA and CPU wheels for x86_64 and aarch64 [docker/Dockerfile:25-47](), [requirements/cuda.txt:1-33](), [requirements/xpu.txt:1-23](), [docker/Dockerfile.cpu:1-18](), [.buildkite/release-pipeline.yaml:21-45](), [.buildkite/release-pipeline.yaml:62-74]().

| Variant or target | Configuration evidence | Build-specific notes |
|---|---|---|
| CUDA | `CUDA_VERSION`, `BUILD_BASE_IMAGE`, `FINAL_BASE_IMAGE`, and `NCCL_VERSION` are Docker build arguments [docker/Dockerfile:25-47](). | `requirements/cuda.txt` pins CUDA-oriented PyTorch and related packages, including `torch==2.14.0`, `flashinfer-python`, and NVIDIA kernel dependencies [requirements/cuda.txt:1-33](). |
| ROCm | The release pipeline and publisher use `rocm` and `rocm72` targets and configure stacks through `docker/Dockerfile.rocm` and base context mapping [docker/Dockerfile.rocm:1-17](), [.buildkite/scripts/publish-release-images.sh:119-149](). | ROCm wheel building relies on Meson and UCX integration layers configured via container build stages [docker/Dockerfile.rocm:37-124](). |
| XPU | `requirements/xpu.txt` adds XPU wheel indexes, `triton==3.9.0+xpu`, the PyTorch XPU index, and `torch==2.15.0` [requirements/xpu.txt:1-24](). | `docker/Dockerfile.xpu` installs Intel GPU runtime components and configures the XPU package index [docker/Dockerfile.xpu:42-80](), [docker/Dockerfile.xpu:102-125](). |
| CPU | `docker/Dockerfile.cpu` documents `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` support and CPU build arguments [docker/Dockerfile.cpu:1-18](). | `PYTORCH_NIGHTLY` selects nightly CPU PyTorch dependencies in the CPU dependency stage [docker/Dockerfile.cpu:143-165](). |
| ARM64 / aarch64 | CUDA release wheels use an aarch64 builder and the `CUDA_ARCH_AARCH64` list; CPU builds also have an aarch64 target [.buildkite/release-pipeline.yaml:1-12](), [.buildkite/release-pipeline.yaml:24-34](), [docker/Dockerfile.cpu:1-8](). | The release pipeline assembles CUDA image manifests from `x86_64` and `aarch64` images [.buildkite/scripts/publish-release-images.sh:24-53](). |
| s390x | `setup.py` references `s390x` when checking `should_bundle_tcmalloc()` for CPU Linux builds [setup.py:142-149](). | No dedicated s390x CI build target or container image file is present in the main build files. |

## CUDA Build Variant

### CUDA Docker and Dependency Inputs

The CUDA Dockerfile defines defaults for `CUDA_VERSION`, `PYTHON_VERSION`, `UBUNTU_VERSION`, and `NCCL_VERSION`. It also makes the build and runtime base images configurable through `BUILD_BASE_IMAGE` and `FINAL_BASE_IMAGE` [docker/Dockerfile:25-47]().

The file provides configurable Python package indexes through `PIP_INDEX_URL`, `PIP_EXTRA_INDEX_URL`, `UV_INDEX_URL`, and `UV_EXTRA_INDEX_URL`. PyTorch’s package index base is separately configured by `PYTORCH_CUDA_INDEX_BASE_URL` [docker/Dockerfile:67-82]().

The CUDA requirements include `torch==2.14.0`, `torchaudio==2.11.0`, and `torchvision==0.29.0`. They also specify CUDA-oriented dependencies such as `flashinfer-python`, NVIDIA cuDNN frontend, CUTLASS DSL, and Humming kernels [requirements/cuda.txt:1-33]().

### CUDA Architecture Targets

Release CI defines separate architecture lists for x86 and aarch64. `CUDA_ARCH_X86` includes architectures from `7.5` through `12.0`; `CUDA_ARCH_AARCH64` includes aarch64-specific targets such as `8.7`, `11.0`, and `12.0` [.buildkite/release-pipeline.yaml:1-12]().

The CUDA release pipeline passes the relevant architecture list as `torch_cuda_arch_list` when building the wheel [.buildkite/release-pipeline.yaml:21-45]().

### CUDA Nightly Wheel Installation

The CUDA installation documentation describes nightly vLLM wheels at `https://wheels.vllm.ai/nightly` and variant-specific subdirectories, including `cu130` and `cpu` [docs/getting_started/installation/gpu.cuda.inc.md:63-82]().

Sources: [docker/Dockerfile:25-47](), [docker/Dockerfile:67-82](), [requirements/cuda.txt:1-33](), [.buildkite/release-pipeline.yaml:1-12](), [.buildkite/release-pipeline.yaml:21-45](), [docs/getting_started/installation/gpu.cuda.inc.md:63-82]()

---

## ROCm Build Variant

The ROCm build pipeline (`docker/Dockerfile.rocm`) configures development environments, builds `UCX`, compiles `NIXL` via Meson with ROCm variants `-Dwheel_variant=rocm`, and constructs wheels using `uv build` and `auditwheel` [docker/Dockerfile.rocm:37-138]().

**Diagram: ROCm build and NIXL packaging workflow**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    rocmDev["docker/Dockerfile.rocm dev"] --> ucxBuild["build_nixl UCX_REPO"]
    ucxBuild --> nixlMeson["meson setup build -Dwheel_variant=rocm"]
    nixlMeson --> uvBuild["uv build --wheel"]
    uvBuild --> auditWheel["auditwheel repair --exclude libamdhip64"]
    auditWheel --> wheelOutput["nixl_rocm wheel package"]
```

Sources: [docker/Dockerfile.rocm:37-138]()

---

## XPU Build Variant (Intel GPU)

### Requirements and Package Indexes

`requirements/xpu.txt` includes common requirements, adds extra indexes, and pins `triton==3.9.0+xpu`, `torch==2.15.0`, `auto_round_lib==0.16.0`, and `vllm_xpu_kernels==0.1.16.3` [requirements/xpu.txt:1-24]().

### Docker Stages and Configuration

`docker/Dockerfile.xpu` defines a dedicated Rust build path (`rust-build-cache` and `rust-build`) to produce `vllm-rs` and `_rust_*.so` artifacts. The `vllm-base` stage uses Ubuntu 24.04 and installs Intel GPU runtime packages (`intel-gpu-compute`) [docker/Dockerfile.xpu:1-42](), [docker/Dockerfile.xpu:73-86]().

The `vllm-build` stage installs XPU requirements, copies prebuilt Rust components from `rust-build`, and runs `python3 setup.py bdist_wheel` with `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=xpu` [docker/Dockerfile.xpu:117-142]().

### XPU Dependencies Mapped to Build Stages

**Diagram: XPU indexes, requirements, and Rust artifacts**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    xpuReq["requirements/xpu.txt"] --> xpuIndex["https://wheels.vllm.ai/xpu/"]
    xpuReq --> torchIndex["https://download.pytorch.org/whl/xpu"]
    xpuReq --> triton["triton==3.9.0+xpu"]
    xpuReq --> kernels["vllm_xpu_kernels"]
    rustInputs["rust files and tools/build_rust.sh"] --> rustCache["rust-build-cache"]
    rustCache --> rustBuild["rust-build"]
    rustBuild --> rustArtifacts["vllm-rs and _rust_*.so"]
    rustArtifacts --> wheelBuild["vllm-build"]
    xpuReq --> wheelBuild
    xpuIndex --> base["vllm-base"]
```

Sources: [requirements/xpu.txt:1-24](), [docker/Dockerfile.xpu:1-42](), [docker/Dockerfile.xpu:73-86](), [docker/Dockerfile.xpu:117-142]()

---

## CPU Build Variant

### CPU Docker Targets and Build Arguments

The CPU Dockerfile (`docker/Dockerfile.cpu`) documents support for `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`. It identifies `vllm-openai`, `vllm-test`, and `vllm-dev` as build targets. Build arguments include `PYTHON_VERSION`, `VLLM_CPU_X86`, and `VLLM_CPU_ARM_BF16` [docker/Dockerfile.cpu:1-18]().

The shared `base-common` stage sets `MAX_JOBS` from `max_jobs`, installs GCC-15, and configures `ccache` [docker/Dockerfile.cpu:80-123]().

### CPU Nightly PyTorch Option

The CPU dependency stage defines `PYTORCH_NIGHTLY=0` by default. When set to `1`, it installs prerelease CPU packages for PyTorch and runs `tools/use_existing_torch.py --prefix` before installing `requirements/cpu.txt` [docker/Dockerfile.cpu:143-165]().

**Diagram: CPU nightly dependency installation flow**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    nightlyArg["PYTORCH_NIGHTLY"] --> condition["base-common-pydeps"]
    condition -->| "1" | nightlyIndex["PYTORCH_CPU_INDEX_BASE_URL/nightly/cpu"]
    nightlyIndex --> torchNightly["torch torchaudio torchvision torchcodec"]
    torchNightly --> existingTorch["tools/use_existing_torch.py --prefix"]
    existingTorch --> cpuRequirements["requirements/cpu.txt"]
    condition -->| "0" | releasePath["release dependency path"]
```

Sources: [docker/Dockerfile.cpu:143-165]()

---

## Nightly PyTorch Builds

The CPU Dockerfile’s `PYTORCH_NIGHTLY` argument controls whether the CPU image installs nightly PyTorch packages [docker/Dockerfile.cpu:143-165](). For CUDA installations, nightly vLLM wheels are fetched from dedicated indices using `uv` [docs/getting_started/installation/gpu.cuda.inc.md:63-82]().

Sources: [docker/Dockerfile.cpu:143-165](), [docs/getting_started/installation/gpu.cuda.inc.md:63-82]()

---

## ARM64 and S390x Targets

### ARM64 (aarch64)

The CPU Dockerfile supports `linux/arm64` via Docker Buildx platform options, mapping `TARGETARCH=arm64` to `aarch64` sccache binaries [docker/Dockerfile.cpu:1-8](), [docker/Dockerfile.cpu:37-53](). The CUDA release pipeline defines `CUDA_ARCH_AARCH64` for aarch64 CUDA wheel builds [.buildkite/release-pipeline.yaml:1-12](), [.buildkite/release-pipeline.yaml:24-34]().

### S390x

`setup.py` includes `s390x` in `should_bundle_tcmalloc()` checks for Linux CPU builds, but dedicated container build stages or CI pipelines for s390x are not present in the supplied build file excerpts [setup.py:142-149]().

### Architecture and Release Targets Mapped to Code Entities

**Diagram: Architecture labels connected to build identifiers**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    ARM64["ARM64"] --> cpuPlatform["linux/arm64"]
    ARM64 --> cpuArch["TARGETARCH arm64"]
    cpuArch --> armSccache["SCCACHE_ARCH aarch64"]
    ARM64 --> cudaList["CUDA_ARCH_AARCH64"]
    cudaList --> cudaWheel["build-wheel-arm64-cuda-13-0"]
    X86["x86_64"] --> cudaX86["CUDA_ARCH_X86"]
    X86 --> cpuX86["VLLM_CPU_X86"]
    S390X["s390x"] --> tcmallocCheck["should_bundle_tcmalloc s390x"]
```

Sources: [setup.py:142-149](), [docker/Dockerfile.cpu:1-18](), [docker/Dockerfile.cpu:37-53](), [.buildkite/release-pipeline.yaml:1-12](), [.buildkite/release-pipeline.yaml:24-45]()

## Build-Time Configuration Options

### CUDA Docker Build Arguments

The CUDA Dockerfile arguments include `CUDA_VERSION`, `PYTHON_VERSION`, `UBUNTU_VERSION`, `NCCL_VERSION`, `BUILD_BASE_IMAGE`, and `FINAL_BASE_IMAGE` [docker/Dockerfile:25-47](). `docker/versions.json` records generated defaults for these build parameters [docker/versions.json:1-23]().

### Parallelism and Compiler Caching

CPU builds set `MAX_JOBS` from `max_jobs` and configure GCC-15 with `ccache` [docker/Dockerfile.cpu:87-123](). CUDA builds support `USE_SCCACHE` for remote caching [docker/Dockerfile:105-156]().

### Build Configuration Data Flow

**Diagram: Configuration inputs mapped to build-stage entities**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    cudaVersion["CUDA_VERSION"] --> cudaImage["BUILD_BASE_IMAGE and FINAL_BASE_IMAGE"]
    cudaArch["torch_cuda_arch_list"] --> releaseWheel["CUDA release wheel build"]
    cpuNightly["PYTORCH_NIGHTLY"] --> cpuDeps["base-common-pydeps"]
    cpuDeps --> cpuIndex["PYTORCH_CPU_INDEX_BASE_URL/nightly/cpu"]
    maxJobs["max_jobs"] --> cpuMaxJobs["MAX_JOBS"]
    sccache["USE_SCCACHE and TARGETARCH"] --> cacheBinary["architecture-specific sccache"]
    rustInputs["rust files and tools/build_rust.sh"] --> rustStages["rust-build-cache and rust-build"]
```

Sources: [docker/Dockerfile:25-47](), [docker/Dockerfile:105-156](), [.buildkite/release-pipeline.yaml:21-45](), [docker/Dockerfile.cpu:87-90](), [docker/Dockerfile.cpu:143-165](), [docker/Dockerfile.xpu:1-40]()

The build configuration supports CUDA, ROCm, XPU, and CPU platforms through dedicated Dockerfiles, requirements files, and CI pipelines. Build-time options control parallel compilation, caching, architecture targets, and nightly PyTorch dependencies [docker/Dockerfile:25-47](), [docker/Dockerfile.rocm:37-138](), [requirements/cuda.txt:1-33](), [requirements/xpu.txt:1-24](), [docker/Dockerfile.cpu:1-18](), [.buildkite/release-pipeline.yaml:1-12]().

## Purpose and Scope

This page documents runtime kernel preparation and warmup as evidenced by the codebase: DeepGEMM’s build integration and runtime-JIT boundary, worker-level JIT warmup, FlashInfer autotuning, and model-specific Triton warmup entry points [cmake/external_projects/deepgemm.cmake:97-107](), [vllm/model_executor/warmup/kernel_warmup.py:18-47](), [vllm/model_executor/warmup/kernel_warmup.py:123-146](). It distinguishes these activities from model-weight preloading: the weight cache keeps processed weights resident across engine restarts, while its preload flow can also run FlashInfer autotuning before an engine starts.

Sources: [cmake/external_projects/deepgemm.cmake:97-107](), [vllm/model_executor/warmup/kernel_warmup.py:18-47](), [vllm/model_executor/warmup/kernel_warmup.py:123-146]()

---

## Overview: Compilation, Autotuning, and Warmup

The code and documentation describe several related but distinct runtime compilation and warmup subsystems:

- **Build-time extension integration:** CMake selects DeepGEMM sources, filters supported CUDA architectures, and delegates construction of its extension to `tools/build_deepgemm_C.py` [cmake/external_projects/deepgemm.cmake:3-28](), [cmake/external_projects/deepgemm.cmake:68-105](), [cmake/external_projects/deepgemm.cmake:123-145]().
- **Worker-level JIT warmup:** Functions such as `_warmup_flashinfer_attention()`, `_warmup_ll_bf16_router_gemm()`, and `_warmup_skinny_gemm()` pre-compile and initialize model-specific kernels prior to inference execution [vllm/model_executor/warmup/kernel_warmup.py:63-101](), [vllm/model_executor/warmup/kernel_warmup.py:123-146](), [vllm/model_executor/warmup/kernel_warmup.py:148-167]().
- **FlashInfer autotuning:** FlashInfer checks availability of `nvcc`, `ninja`, and precompiled cubins via `has_flashinfer()` and `warn_if_flashinfer_kernels_missing()` to guide runtime kernel JIT behavior [vllm/utils/flashinfer.py:85-115](), [vllm/utils/flashinfer.py:131-163]().
- **Model-specific Triton warmup:** `kernel_warmup.py` imports named warmup functions for several model-specific Triton paths like `kimi_k3_triton_warmup`, `mamba_triton_warmup`, and `qwen_triton_warmup` [vllm/model_executor/warmup/kernel_warmup.py:34-42]().

## DeepGEMM Compilation

### Source selection and build integration

`cmake/external_projects/deepgemm.cmake` uses `DEEPGEMM_SRC_DIR` when supplied through the environment or CMake configuration [cmake/external_projects/deepgemm.cmake:7-28](). It normalizes the path, checks that it names an existing directory, and uses it as the source tree. Otherwise, it configures `FetchContent` to retrieve a pinned vLLM-project DeepGEMM revision and its specified submodules [cmake/external_projects/deepgemm.cmake:29-66]().

The CMake file derives candidate DeepGEMM architectures from the CUDA compiler version, intersecting those candidates with `CUDA_ARCHS` [cmake/external_projects/deepgemm.cmake:73-94](). When nonempty, it adds a custom build command invoking `tools/build_deepgemm_C.py`, tracking extension sources and headers as dependencies, and installing the built `_C.py` shim and `_C_extension*.so` into `vllm/third_party/deep_gemm` [cmake/external_projects/deepgemm.cmake:116-148]().

### Build-time extension versus runtime kernel compilation

Building the Python shim and extension is a build-system task; DeepGEMM’s CUDA kernels are compiled at runtime via JIT (`deep_jit`), requiring an active CUDA toolkit (`nvcc`) [cmake/external_projects/deepgemm.cmake:97-109](), [vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py:116-151]().

| Concern | Mechanism shown | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Source selection | Local `DEEPGEMM_SRC_DIR` or pinned FetchContent source | [cmake/external_projects/deepgemm.cmake:3-66]() |
| Architecture selection | CUDA-version-dependent candidates intersected with `CUDA_ARCHS` | [cmake/external_projects/deepgemm.cmake:73-94]() |
| Extension build | Custom command runs `tools/build_deepgemm_C.py` | [cmake/external_projects/deepgemm.cmake:127-140]() |
| Extension packaging | Installs `_C.py` and `_C_extension*.so` under `vllm/third_party/deep_gemm` | [cmake/external_projects/deepgemm.cmake:142-147]() |
| CUDA kernel compilation | Runtime JIT via `nvcc` remains required | [cmake/external_projects/deepgemm.cmake:97-107](), [vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py:136-151]() |

Sources: [cmake/external_projects/deepgemm.cmake:3-66](), [cmake/external_projects/deepgemm.cmake:73-147](), [vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py:136-151]()

### Natural-language concepts mapped to DeepGEMM entities

**Diagram: DeepGEMM build-time and runtime boundary**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    SourceChoice["Choose DeepGEMM source"] --> Local["DEEPGEMM_SRC_DIR"]
    SourceChoice --> Fetch["FetchContent_Populate pinned source"]
    Local --> ArchFilter["DEEPGEMM_SUPPORT_ARCHS intersect CUDA_ARCHS"]
    Fetch --> ArchFilter
    ArchFilter --> Supported{"DEEPGEMM_ARCHS nonempty"}
    Supported -->|Yes| BuildExt["tools/build_deepgemm_C.py"]
    Supported -->|No| NoArch["No DeepGEMM architecture target"]
    BuildExt --> Package["vllm/third_party/deep_gemm/_C.py and _C_extension"]
    Package --> Runtime["DeepGEMM CUDA kernels"]
    Runtime --> JIT["Runtime JIT compilation via nvcc"]
```

Sources: [cmake/external_projects/deepgemm.cmake:3-66](), [cmake/external_projects/deepgemm.cmake:73-147](), [vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py:136-151]()

## Triton Kernel JIT and Model-Specific Warmup

`vllm/model_executor/warmup/kernel_warmup.py` imports model-specific warmup routines including `kimi_k3_triton_warmup`, `mamba_triton_warmup`, `qwen4_exp_qsa_triton_warmup`, `qwen_triton_warmup`, and `qwen_vl_triton_warmup` [vllm/model_executor/warmup/kernel_warmup.py:34-42](). These functions ensure that Triton kernels for architectures like Qwen, Mamba, and Kimi-K3 undergo JIT compilation during engine initialization rather than during latency-sensitive forward passes.

Sources: [vllm/model_executor/warmup/kernel_warmup.py:34-42]()

---

## Kernel and JIT Warmup Subsystem

### Worker Warmup Procedures

The warmup subsystem defines specific pre-execution procedures for different backends:
- `_warmup_flashinfer_attention(worker)` checks whether FlashInfer attention groups are active on non-pooling models and invokes `mixed_batch_attention_warmup(worker)` across pipeline-parallel ranks [vllm/model_executor/warmup/kernel_warmup.py:63-101]().
- `_warmup_ll_bf16_router_gemm(model)` inspects `GateLinear` layers and invokes `ll_bf16_gemm_kernel.warmup()` for eligible shapes [vllm/model_executor/warmup/kernel_warmup.py:103-146]().
- `_warmup_skinny_gemm(model)` requests skinny GEMM configurations via `shape_dynamic_skinny_gemm.request_warmup_configs()` [vllm/model_executor/warmup/kernel_warmup.py:148-167]().

**Diagram: Worker Warmup Workflow**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Start["kernel_warmup entry"] --> FlashInfer["_warmup_flashinfer_attention"]
    FlashInfer --> CheckFi{"FlashInfer backend active?"}
    CheckFi -->|Yes| MixedWarmup["mixed_batch_attention_warmup(worker)"]
    CheckFi -->|No| RouterGemm["_warmup_ll_bf16_router_gemm"]
    MixedWarmup --> RouterGemm
    RouterGemm --> SkinnyGemm["_warmup_skinny_gemm"]
    SkinnyGemm --> Done["Warmup Complete"]
```

Sources: [vllm/model_executor/warmup/kernel_warmup.py:63-167]()

### FlashInfer JIT & Autotune Constraints

`vllm/utils/flashinfer.py` verifies that `flashinfer` and `flashinfer-cubin` packages or `nvcc`/`ninja` toolchains are present [vllm/utils/flashinfer.py:85-115](). If precompiled kernels are missing on newer architectures (e.g. Hopper), `warn_if_flashinfer_kernels_missing()` warns users that FlashInfer will JIT-compile kernels at startup [vllm/utils/flashinfer.py:131-163]().

Sources: [vllm/utils/flashinfer.py:85-163]()

---

## Scope Boundaries

The codebase implements explicit JIT compilation and warmup boundaries via CMake external projects for DeepGEMM, worker-level warmup routines for FlashInfer and CuteDSL kernels, and specialized Triton warmup functions for model families like Mamba and Qwen [cmake/external_projects/deepgemm.cmake:123-145](), [vllm/model_executor/warmup/kernel_warmup.py:34-42](), [vllm/model_executor/warmup/kernel_warmup.py:63-167](). General-purpose runtime kernel code generation internals are delegated to backend libraries (Triton, FlashInfer, DeepGEMM).

Sources: [cmake/external_projects/deepgemm.cmake:123-145](), [vllm/model_executor/warmup/kernel_warmup.py:34-42](), [vllm/model_executor/warmup/kernel_warmup.py:63-167]()

## Purpose and Scope

This page provides a high-level overview of vLLM's testing infrastructure, CI pipelines, hardware-specific testing strategies, and validation tooling. vLLM relies on a comprehensive automated testing framework centered around Buildkite configurations located in `.buildkite/` to validate engine behavior, core operations, distributed execution, model accuracy, and serving APIs across multiple hardware accelerators [.buildkite/test_areas/engine.yaml:1-29](), [.buildkite/test_areas/kernels.yaml:1-15](), [.buildkite/test_areas/distributed.yaml:1-20](), [.buildkite/test_areas/lm_eval.yaml:1-16]().

As a parent page, this document summarizes core concepts and links to detailed child pages:
- [Test Organization and Infrastructure](#12.1) — Test categories, conftest fixtures, `VllmRunner`/`HfRunner` harnesses, and model test registries.
- [Buildkite CI Pipelines](#12.2) — Buildkite configuration, `test_areas` layout, test sharding, mirroring, and pipeline structure.
- [Hardware-Specific Testing](#12.3) — AMD GPU testing, Intel XPU jobs, CPU hardware tests, TPU testing, and hardware-specific overrides.
- [Model Correctness Validation and Benchmarking](#12.4) — `lm_eval`/`gsm8k` correctness suites, acceptance criteria, and benchmarking tools (`benchmark_serving`, throughput, latency, sweeps).
- [Developer Tooling and Governance](#12.5) — Pre-commit hooks, mypy tooling, GitHub Actions workflows, mergify automation, CODEOWNERS, agent skills (`.agents/`, `.claude/`), and contribution processes.

Sources: [.buildkite/test_areas/engine.yaml:1-29](), [.buildkite/test_areas/kernels.yaml:1-15](), [.buildkite/test_areas/distributed.yaml:1-20](), [.buildkite/test_areas/lm_eval.yaml:1-16]()

---

## Overview

CI test definitions are organized into area-specific YAML files under `.buildkite/test_areas/` [,.buildkite/test_areas/engine.yaml:1-29](), [.buildkite/test_areas/kernels.yaml:1-15](). These configurations cover engine and V1 execution, core and specialized kernels, distributed communication, language and multimodal models, API entrypoints, speculative decoding, and correctness evaluation [.buildkite/test_areas/distributed.yaml:1-20](), [.buildkite/test_areas/models_basic.yaml:1-19](), [.buildkite/test_areas/models_multimodal.yaml:1-15](), [.buildkite/test_areas/entrypoints.yaml:26-41](), [.buildkite/test_areas/spec_decode.yaml:5-26](), [.buildkite/test_areas/lm_eval.yaml:5-16]().

Jobs pair execution commands with target device specifications, timeouts, and `source_file_dependencies` to optimize CI resource utilization through change-based test selection [.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml:5-39](), [.buildkite/test_areas/kernels.yaml:33-68](). Many NVIDIA-targeted jobs also declare AMD ROCm mirrors, while dedicated steps target CPU environments [.buildkite/test_areas/models_multimodal.yaml:103-120]().

Sources: [.buildkite/test_areas/engine.yaml:1-37](), [.buildkite/test_areas/kernels.yaml:1-68](), [.buildkite/test_areas/models_basic.yaml:1-19](), [.buildkite/test_areas/models_multimodal.yaml:91-120](), [.buildkite/test_areas/entrypoints.yaml:26-41](), [.buildkite/test_areas/spec_decode.yaml:5-26](), [.buildkite/test_areas/lm_eval.yaml:5-16]()

---

## CI Pipeline Architecture

Buildkite test-area files define logical groups of pipeline steps that typically depend on base container image builds [.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml:1-30](). Sharding strategies such as `automatic_shard` and `parallelism` distribute heavy suites across parallel worker pods [.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml:5-30](), [.buildkite/test_areas/kernels.yaml:33-38](), [.buildkite/test_areas/entrypoints.yaml:84-103]().

AMD ROCm mirrors translate NVIDIA jobs to AMD hardware targets using platform-specific overrides, such as custom device identifiers (`mi355_dpx`, `mi300_1`) and timeout adjustments [.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml:28-39](), [.buildkite/test_areas/distributed.yaml:21-38](), [.buildkite/test-amd.yaml:8-27]().

For deep dives into pipeline composition, layout, and sharding, see [Buildkite CI Pipelines](#12.2). Hardware-specific coverage is documented in [Hardware-Specific Testing](#12.3).

**Diagram: Natural language test concepts mapped to Buildkite YAML and test paths**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  TestAreas["TestAreas_YAML"] --> EngineConfig[".buildkite/test_areas/engine.yaml"]
  TestAreas --> KernelConfig[".buildkite/test_areas/kernels.yaml"]
  TestAreas --> DistConfig[".buildkite/test_areas/distributed.yaml"]
  TestAreas --> EvalConfig[".buildkite/test_areas/lm_eval.yaml"]
  EngineConfig --> V1EngineTest["tests/v1/engine"]
  KernelConfig --> CoreKernelTest["tests/kernels/core"]
  DistConfig --> CommOpsTest["tests/distributed/test_comm_ops.py"]
  EvalConfig --> GSM8KTest["evals/gsm8k/test_gsm8k_correctness.py"]
```

Sources: [.buildkite/test_areas/engine.yaml:1-63](), [.buildkite/test_areas/kernels.yaml:1-50](), [.buildkite/test_areas/distributed.yaml:1-21](), [.buildkite/test_areas/lm_eval.yaml:1-16]()

## Test Areas and Step Configuration

Test suites are structured around specific vLLM subsystems. The table below outlines key configuration fields used across CI step definitions [.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml:5-39](), [.buildkite/test_areas/kernels.yaml:33-68]():

| Configuration Field | Role and Description |
|---|---|
| `label`, `key` | Identifies the step in the Buildkite UI and tracking system [.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml:5-9]() |
| `device`, `num_devices` | Selects hardware accelerator targets and device counts [.buildkite/test_areas/distributed.yaml:5-10]() |
| `timeout_in_minutes` | Enforces maximum job execution time limits [.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml:7-9]() |
| `source_file_dependencies` | Restricts job execution to PRs touching specified code paths [.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml:10-27]() |
| `automatic_shard`, `parallelism` | Scales test execution across multiple parallel worker nodes [.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml:5-9](), [.buildkite/test_areas/kernels.yaml:33-38]() |
| `commands` | Defines shell commands and `pytest` execution targets [.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml:28-30]() |
| `mirror` | Configures platform-specific hardware mirrors (e.g., AMD ROCm) [.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml:31-39]() |

For comprehensive CI configuration details, see [Buildkite CI Pipelines](#12.2).

Sources: [.buildkite/test-amd.yaml:8-27](), [.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml:5-39](), [.buildkite/test_areas/kernels.yaml:33-68](), [.buildkite/test_areas/distributed.yaml:5-20]()

## Hardware-Specific Testing Infrastructure

Testing spans multiple hardware platforms, including NVIDIA GPUs (Hopper, Blackwell, L4), AMD ROCm accelerators (MI300, MI355), and CPU executors [.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml:5-39](), [.buildkite/test_areas/kernels.yaml:33-82](), [.buildkite/test_areas/models_multimodal.yaml:103-120](). Platform-specific execution requirements are managed via step overrides and environment variables [,.buildkite/test-amd.yaml:8-27]().

**Diagram: Hardware-aware test execution mapping**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  CoreOps["CoreKernels"] --> KernelJob["kernels-core-operation-test"]
  KernelJob --> NvidiaDevice["h200_35gb"]
  KernelJob --> AmdDevice["mi300_1"]
  ProcessorTests["MultimodalProcessor"] --> CpuJob["multi-modal-processor-cpu"]
  CpuJob --> CpuDevice["cpu-medium"]
  EvalTests["GSM8KCorrectness"] --> EvalJob["lm-eval-small-models"]
  EvalJob --> EvalNvidia["h200_35gb"]
  EvalJob --> EvalAmd["mi300_1"]
```

For platform-specific configuration and execution rules, consult [Hardware-Specific Testing](#12.3).

Sources: [.buildkite/test_areas/kernels.yaml:33-82](), [.buildkite/test_areas/models_multimodal.yaml:103-120](), [.buildkite/test_areas/lm_eval.yaml:5-32]()

## Relationship to Other Subsystems

The test suites map directly to vLLM's internal architectural layers:
- **Engine & V1 Core:** Validated via engine and asynchronous scheduler integration tests [.buildkite/test_areas/engine.yaml:5-120]()
- **Kernels & IR:** Covered by low-level `csrc/` and Triton operator test targets [.buildkite/test_areas/kernels.yaml:1-50]()
- **Distributed & Communication:** Tested using multi-device communication and process group verification suites [.buildkite/test_areas/distributed.yaml:5-108]()
- **Models & Multimodal:** Verified through initialization checks, language generation benchmarks, and multimodal processors [.buildkite/test_areas/models_basic.yaml:5-19](), [.buildkite/test_areas/models_multimodal.yaml:5-15]()
- **Serving APIs:** Validated via OpenAI-compatible API server integration tests [.buildkite/test_areas/entrypoints.yaml:54-103]()

For correctness metrics and benchmarking strategies, see [Model Correctness Validation and Benchmarking](#12.4). For development workflows and governance rules, refer to [Developer Tooling and Governance](#12.5).

Sources: [.buildkite/test_areas/engine.yaml:39-120](), [.buildkite/test_areas/kernels.yaml:5-50](), [.buildkite/test_areas/distributed.yaml:5-108](), [.buildkite/test_areas/models_language.yaml:5-43](), [.buildkite/test_areas/lm_eval.yaml:5-16](), [.buildkite/test_areas/entrypoints.yaml:54-103](), [.buildkite/test_areas/models_multimodal.yaml:5-15]()

## Model Test Registry System

`HF_EXAMPLE_MODELS` supplies Hugging Face example-model metadata, while `ModelRegistry` is queried for supported architectures, class loading, and model properties [tests/models/test_registry.py:18-28](), [tests/models/test_initialization.py:30-36]().

### Architecture Mapping and Test Metadata

`tests/models/test_registry.py` parameterizes `test_registry_imports` over `ModelRegistry.get_supported_archs()` [tests/models/test_registry.py:31-32](). For each architecture, it looks up HF example records, checks Transformers compatibility, applies platform and dependency skips, and tests loading via `ModelRegistry._try_load_model_cls` [tests/models/test_registry.py:33-75]().

| Registry test element | Role demonstrated by the tests |
|---|---|
| `ModelRegistry.get_supported_archs()` | Supplies architecture names for import tests. [tests/models/test_registry.py:31-32]() |
| `HF_EXAMPLE_MODELS.get_hf_info()` | Supplies example-model information for version checks. [tests/models/test_registry.py:33-39]() |
| `ModelRegistry._try_load_model_cls()` | Attempts to load implementation classes. [tests/models/test_registry.py:73-75]() |
| `ModelRegistry._try_inspect_model_cls()` | Supplies model metadata for property assertions without loading weights. [tests/models/test_registry.py:107-112]() |

Sources: [tests/models/test_registry.py:18-39](), [tests/models/test_registry.py:73-89](), [tests/models/test_registry.py:91-143]()

**Diagram: Registry test flow mapped to code entities**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    supported["ModelRegistry.get_supported_archs()"]
    hfinfo["HF_EXAMPLE_MODELS.find_hf_info(model)"]
    version["model_info.check_transformers_version(...)"]
    load["ModelRegistry._try_load_model_cls(model_arch)"]
    inspect["ModelRegistry._try_inspect_model_cls(model_arch)"]
    assertions["is_text_generation_model(...) / is_pooling_model(...)"]
    supported --> hfinfo --> version --> load --> assertions
    inspect --> assertions
```

## Test Infrastructure and Conftest Fixtures

`tests/conftest.py` installs `tblib` pickling support to propagate subprocess exceptions [tests/conftest.py:7-14](). It provides JSON schema fixtures, asset singletons (`IMAGE_ASSETS`, `VIDEO_ASSETS`, `AUDIO_ASSETS`), and HTTP connection initialization fixtures [tests/conftest.py:85-130](), [tests/conftest.py:152-221]().

### Test Harnesses: `VllmRunner` and `HfRunner`

Hybrid model tests use `hf_runner` and `vllm_runner` fixtures as context managers to compare outputs via `check_logprobs_close` [tests/models/language/generation/test_hybrid.py:73-110]().

**Diagram: Model comparison pattern in `test_models`**

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Test as "test_models"
    participant HF as "hf_runner(model)"
    participant VLLM as "vllm_runner(model, ...)"
    participant Compare as "check_logprobs_close"

    Test->>HF: "generate_greedy_logprobs_limit(example_prompts, max_tokens, num_logprobs)"
    HF-->>Test: "hf_outputs"
    Test->>VLLM: "generate_greedy_logprobs(example_prompts, max_tokens, num_logprobs)"
    VLLM-->>Test: "vllm_outputs"
    Test->>Compare: "compare hf_outputs and vllm_outputs"
```

Sources: [tests/models/language/generation/test_hybrid.py:73-110]()

### Advanced Feature Test Harnesses (Logits Processors & Breakable Cudagraphs)

`tests/v1/logits_processors/test_custom_online.py` launches `RemoteOpenAIServerCustom` subprocesses with custom logits processors specified via Fully Qualified Class Name (FQCN) or entrypoints [tests/v1/logits_processors/test_custom_online.py:75-106](). `tests/v1/cudagraph/test_breakable_cudagraph.py` utilizes `_enable_breakable_cudagraph` and `cuda_capture_stream` fixtures to test breakable CUDA graph streams [tests/v1/cudagraph/test_breakable_cudagraph.py:28-42](), [tests/v1/cudagraph/test_breakable_cudagraph.py:105-128]().

Sources: [tests/v1/logits_processors/test_custom_online.py:75-106](), [tests/v1/cudagraph/test_breakable_cudagraph.py:28-42](), [tests/v1/cudagraph/test_breakable_cudagraph.py:105-128]()

## Purpose and scope

This page documents the Buildkite CI configuration layout in `.buildkite/` files: test-area groups, step parameters, source-file dependency filtering, sharding configuration, AMD hardware mirroring, and pipeline execution structure [`.buildkite/test-amd.yaml:1-27`]() [`.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml:1-4`]() [`.buildkite/test_areas/kernels.yaml:1-4`]().

Sources: [`.buildkite/test-amd.yaml:1-27`](), [`.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml:1-4`](), [`.buildkite/test_areas/kernels.yaml:1-4`]()

---

## Pipeline organization

Test-area YAML files structure CI tasks into named functional groups (`group`) containing lists of execution steps (`steps`) [`.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml:1-4`]() [`.buildkite/test_areas/kernels.yaml:1-4`](). Groups typically depend on base images like `image-build` or `image-build-amd` [`.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml:2-3`]().

Each step specifies a human-readable `label`, a stable `key`, resource requirements (`device`, `num_devices`), source tracking filters (`source_file_dependencies`), and execution commands (`commands`) [`.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml:5-30`]() [`.buildkite/test_areas/kernels.yaml:5-16`]() [`.buildkite/test_areas/distributed.yaml:5-18`]().

### Buildkite configuration data flow

**Diagram: Test-area configuration to job execution**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    TestArea[".buildkite/test_areas/*.yaml"]
    Group["group"]
    Step["steps[]"]
    Trigger["source_file_dependencies"]
    Hardware["device and num_devices"]
    Dependency["depends_on"]
    Commands["commands"]
    Tests["pytest and shell test commands"]
    Mirror["mirror.amd"]
    AMDJob["AMD device and commands"]
    Image["image-build or image-build-amd"]

    TestArea --> Group
    TestArea --> Step
    Step --> Trigger
    Step --> Hardware
    Step --> Dependency
    Step --> Commands
    Commands --> Tests
    Step --> Mirror
    Mirror --> AMDJob
    Dependency --> Image
```

Sources: [`.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml:1-40`](), [`.buildkite/test_areas/kernels.yaml:1-32`](), [`.buildkite/test_areas/distributed.yaml:1-38`]()

---

## Test step configuration

### General test-area step fields

| Field | Configuration role | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `group` | Names the functional test group in a file. | `Distributed` [`.buildkite/test_areas/distributed.yaml:1-4`]() |
| `steps` | Holds the group’s step definitions. | `steps` in `misc.yaml` [`.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml:1-5`]() |
| `label` | Human-readable job label, often indicating hardware and suite. | `:nvidia: (L4) Distributed Comm Ops` [`.buildkite/test_areas/distributed.yaml:5-6`]() |
| `key` | Step identifier used in the configuration. | `distributed-comm-ops` [`.buildkite/test_areas/distributed.yaml:5-6`]() |
| `depends_on` | Declares a configured dependency. | `image-build` and `image-build-amd` [`.buildkite/test_areas/distributed.yaml:1-4`](), [`.buildkite/test_areas/distributed.yaml:21-30`]() |
| `device` | Selects a configured device target. | `l4`, `h200_18gb`, `mi355_dpx` [`.buildkite/test_areas/distributed.yaml:5-10`](), [`.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml:5-9`](), [`.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml:31-40`]() |
| `num_devices` | Requests a device count for a job. | Two devices for distributed communication tests [`.buildkite/test_areas/distributed.yaml:5-16`]() |
| `timeout_in_minutes` | Sets a step timeout. | 25 minutes for `distributed-comm-ops` [`.buildkite/test_areas/distributed.yaml:5-8`]() |
| `working_dir` | Sets the command working directory. | `/vllm-workspace/tests` [`.buildkite/test_areas/distributed.yaml:5-16`]() |
| `source_file_dependencies` | Lists path prefixes associated with a step’s source changes. Selected entries use `!` exclusions. | Distributed paths exclude `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/` [`.buildkite/test_areas/distributed.yaml:11-14`]() |
| `commands` | Lists shell commands run by the step. | Multiple `pytest` invocations [`.buildkite/test_areas/distributed.yaml:15-20`]() |
| `parallelism` | Configures multiple parallel jobs. | Four jobs for the API-server integration step [`.buildkite/test_areas/entrypoints.yaml:84-103`]() |
| `automatic_shard` | Marks a step for automatic sharding. | V1 Sample and API-server integration [`.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml:5-8`](), [`.buildkite/test_areas/entrypoints.yaml:84-94`]() |
| `mirror` | Supplies an alternate hardware configuration for AMD. | `mirror.amd` for V1 Sample [`.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml:28-40`]() |
| `optional` | Marks a job optional, including nightly jobs. | Large-model LM Eval [`.buildkite/test_areas/lm_eval.yaml:103-107`]() |

Sources: [`.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml:5-53`](), [`.buildkite/test_areas/distributed.yaml:1-38`](), [`.buildkite/test_areas/kernels.yaml:33-68`](), [`.buildkite/test_areas/entrypoints.yaml:84-103`](), [`.buildkite/test_areas/lm_eval.yaml:103-107`]()

### AMD-specific test configuration

The `.buildkite/test-amd.yaml` template defines settings fed into `test-template-amd.j2` [`.buildkite/test-amd.yaml:1-6`](). It documents configuration parameters such as `fast_check`, `fast_check_only`, `optional`, `soft_fail`, `command`, `commands`, `mirror_hardwares`, `dind`, `num_gpus`, `num_nodes`, `timeout_in_minutes`, `parallelism`, `working_dir`, and `source_file_dependencies` [`.buildkite/test-amd.yaml:8-24](). Setting `dind: false` executes tasks directly inside AMD Kubernetes pods rather than via Docker-in-Docker [`.buildkite/test-amd.yaml:17`]() [`.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml:34`]()

Sources: [`.buildkite/test-amd.yaml:1-27`]()

## Test categorization and sharding

### Test-area layout

Test areas isolate domains into dedicated YAML files under `.buildkite/test_areas/`:

| Test Area File | Functional Domain | Key Suites / Workloads |
|---|---|---|
| `misc.yaml` | Miscellaneous / V1 Core | V1 sampling, logits processors, core scheduling, executors, workers, KV offload [`.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml:1-144`]() |
| `kernels.yaml` | Core Operation Kernels | vLLM IR, Triton operations, MoE router GEMM, DeepSeek custom ops [`.buildkite/test_areas/kernels.yaml:1-198`]() |
| `distributed.yaml` | Distributed Execution | Communication ops, weight transfer, DP, compile/RPC, torchrun [`.buildkite/test_areas/distributed.yaml:1-202`]() |
| `engine.yaml` | Engine Core & V1 Engine | Core engine unit tests, V1 engine preprocessing, async scheduling [`.buildkite/test_areas/engine.yaml:1-227`]() |
| `entrypoints.yaml` | API Servers & Client Entrypoints | OpenAI-compatible server, chat completion, client interfaces [`.buildkite/test_areas/entrypoints.yaml:1-212`]() |
| `lm_eval.yaml` | Correctness & Benchmarks | GSM8K evaluation, watermarking, LLM-Eval harness [`.buildkite/test_areas/lm_eval.yaml:1-207`]() |
| `spec_decode.yaml` | Speculative Decoding | V1 speculative decoding, Eagle, MTP speculators [`.buildkite/test_areas/spec_decode.yaml:1-214`]() |
| `models_basic.yaml` | Basic Models | Model initialization subset, beam search numerics [`.buildkite/test_areas/models_basic.yaml:1-171`]() |
| `models_language.yaml` | Language Models | Standard language model generation, hybrid SSM models [`.buildkite/test_areas/models_language.yaml:1-153`]() |
| `models_multimodal.yaml` | Multimodal Models | Vision-language generation, multimodal processing, audio models [`.buildkite/test_areas/models_multimodal.yaml:1-199`]() |

Sources: [`.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml:1-144`](), [`.buildkite/test_areas/kernels.yaml:1-198`](), [`.buildkite/test_areas/distributed.yaml:1-202`](), [`.buildkite/test_areas/engine.yaml:1-227`](), [`.buildkite/test_areas/entrypoints.yaml:1-212`](), [`.buildkite/test_areas/lm_eval.yaml:1-207`](), [`.buildkite/test_areas/spec_decode.yaml:1-214`](), [`.buildkite/test_areas/models_basic.yaml:1-171`](), [`.buildkite/test_areas/models_language.yaml:1-153`](), [`.buildkite/test_areas/models_multimodal.yaml:1-199`]()

### Test sharding and parallelism

Steps utilize automatic sharding (`automatic_shard: true`) [`.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml:7`](), or explicit parallelism (`parallelism: N`) passing `BUILDKITE_PARALLEL_JOB` and `BUILDKITE_PARALLEL_JOB_COUNT` variables to pytest via `--shard-id` and `--num-shards` [`.buildkite/test_areas/entrypoints.yaml:88-103`]() [`.buildkite/test_areas/models_multimodal.yaml:132-137`]() [`.buildkite/test_areas/models_language.yaml:85-86`]() [`.buildkite/test-amd.yaml:21-22`]()

**Diagram: Explicit shard configuration and pytest arguments**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Parallelism["parallelism"]
    JobIndex["BUILDKITE_PARALLEL_JOB"]
    JobCount["BUILDKITE_PARALLEL_JOB_COUNT"]
    Pytest["pytest --shard-id and --num-shards"]
    ServeSuite["entrypoints/serve"]
    ScaleOutSuite["entrypoints/scale_out"]

    Parallelism --> JobIndex
    Parallelism --> JobCount
    JobIndex --> Pytest
    JobCount --> Pytest
    Pytest --> ServeSuite
    Pytest --> ScaleOutSuite
```

Sources: [`.buildkite/test-amd.yaml:21-22`](), [`.buildkite/test_areas/entrypoints.yaml:88-103`](), [`.buildkite/test_areas/models_multimodal.yaml:132-137`](), [`.buildkite/test_areas/models_language.yaml:85-86`]()

## Hardware mirroring

Each test step can define a `mirror.amd` block to target AMD hardware (e.g. `mi355_dpx`, `mi300_1`, `mi250_1`) [`.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml:31-40`](), [`.buildkite/test_areas/kernels.yaml:18-26`](), [`.buildkite/test_areas/distributed.yaml:25-33`]()

**Diagram: A configured NVIDIA step and its AMD mirror**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    V1Sample["v1-sample"]
    Nvidia["h200_18gb"]
    NvidiaTests["pytest -v -s v1/sample"]
    Mirror["mirror.amd"]
    AMD["mi355_dpx"]
    AMDTests["AMD V1 Sample job"]
    NvidiaImage["image-build"]
    AMDImage["image-build-amd"]

    V1Sample --> Nvidia
    V1Sample --> NvidiaTests
    V1Sample --> Mirror
    Mirror --> AMD
    Mirror --> AMDTests
    V1Sample --> NvidiaImage
    Mirror --> AMDImage
```

Sources: [`.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml:5-40`]()

## CI-specific environment variables and commands

Jobs configure execution environments and behaviors via exported environment variables in `commands` or step-level `env` blocks [`.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml:28-30`](), [`.buildkite/test_areas/distributed.yaml:107-108`](), [`.buildkite/test_areas/distributed.yaml:77-78`]()

| Variable or Command Setting | Role / Description |
|---|---|
| `VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn` | Configures multiprocessing start method for V1 worker and engine tests [`.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml:29`]() [`.buildkite/test_areas/entrypoints.yaml:65`]() |
| `NCCL_CUMEM_HOST_ENABLE=0` | Disables CUDA memory host registration for NCCL in distributed tests [`.buildkite/test_areas/distributed.yaml:107`]() |
| `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0` | Forces fallback to Triton kernels instead of DeepGEMM on Hopper hardware [`.buildkite/test_areas/lm_eval.yaml:113`]() |
| `uv pip install --system ...` | Installs external packages or runtime dependency pins prior to test invocation [`.buildkite/test_areas/distributed.yaml:80`]() [`.buildkite/test_areas/models_language.yaml:82-83`]() |

Sources: [`.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml:28-30`](), [`.buildkite/test_areas/distributed.yaml:77-83`](), [`.buildkite/test_areas/distributed.yaml:107-108`](), [`.buildkite/test_areas/lm_eval.yaml:113`]()

## Overview

Hardware tests are structured as Buildkite YAML step definitions executed through platform-specific test runners. Intel jobs target `device: intel_gpu` and use `.buildkite/scripts/hardware_ci/run-intel-test.sh` [`.buildkite/intel_jobs/test-intel.yaml:1-36`](); CPU hardware tests run via `.buildkite/hardware_tests/cpu.yaml` using `run-cpu-test.sh` [`.buildkite/hardware_tests/cpu.yaml:41-44`](); and AMD ROCm tests are orchestrated via scripts such as `.buildkite/scripts/hardware_ci/run-amd-test.sh` [`.buildkite/scripts/hardware_ci/run-amd-test.sh:1-15`]().

## AMD/ROCm Testing Infrastructure

### Test execution

The AMD runner script, `.buildkite/scripts/hardware_ci/run-amd-test.sh`, manages ROCm tests inside CI pods and Docker containers [`.buildkite/scripts/hardware_ci/run-amd-test.sh:1-12`](). It configures job-local temporary directories, enforces persistent `HF_HOME` requirements, sets up colorized terminal outputs, and applies robust `pytest` defaults [`.buildkite/scripts/hardware_ci/run-amd-test.sh:27-82` দী]. It also supports reinstalling precompiled vLLM wheels dynamically when `python_only_compile.sh` is invoked [`.buildkite/scripts/hardware_ci/run-amd-test.sh:88-105`]().

### ROCm image and build context

The ROCm Docker base environment (`docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base`) defines target architectures (`PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH`), SDK versions, and installation steps for Triton, FlashAttention, Aiter, and Mori packages [docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base:1-50]().

## Purpose and Scope

This page documents the model correctness validation suites (`lm_eval`, GSM8K-based correctness checks), acceptance criteria, and benchmarking tooling provided in the vLLM codebase. It covers online serving benchmarks (`vllm bench serve`), model forward microbenchmarks (`vllm bench forward`), attention kernel benchmarks, dataset sampling architecture (`BenchmarkDataset`, `SampleRequest`), and performance tracking integrations.

Sources: [docs/benchmarking/cli.md:1-16](), [vllm/benchmarks/serve.py:3-19](), [vllm/benchmarks/datasets/datasets.py:3-11]()

## 1. Correctness Validation Suites: `lm_eval` and GSM8K

### Purpose

The vLLM CI and testing infrastructure runs correctness validation suites using `lm_eval` and GSM8K pipelines to ensure that optimized execution paths, quantization methods, and new model architectures produce mathematically correct outputs matching Hugging Face reference implementations.

### GSM8K and Model-List Execution

The GSM8K correctness tests are invoked via pytest drivers such as `evals/gsm8k/test_gsm8k_correctness.py` paired with model configuration lists (e.g., `configs/models-small.yaml`, `configs/models-watermark.txt`, `configs/models-small-tp.yaml`) [.buildkite/test_areas/lm_eval.yaml:5-32](), [.buildkite/test_areas/lm_eval.yaml:55-69](), [.buildkite/test_areas/lm_eval.yaml:179-207](). These suites evaluate reasoning capabilities across various tensor-parallel (TP) configurations, expert-parallel layouts, and hardware platforms (NVIDIA and AMD ROCm).

Sources: [.buildkite/test_areas/lm_eval.yaml:5-32](), [.buildkite/test_areas/lm_eval.yaml:55-69](), [.buildkite/test_areas/lm_eval.yaml:179-207]()

## 2. Acceptance Criteria for Model Correctness

### CI Acceptance and Thresholds

Acceptance criteria in vLLM are expressed operationally through test suite completion: jobs must pass their assertions without failing tolerance checks against reference models. For instance, quantization tests (such as those in `.buildkite/test_areas/quantization.yaml`) and attention tests (`.buildkite/test_areas/attention.yaml`) run pytest modules to verify numerical equivalence within acceptable floating-point error bounds.

| Validation Area | Associated Code / Test Path | Scope and Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| GSM8K Correctness | `evals/gsm8k/test_gsm8k_correctness.py` [.buildkite/test_areas/lm_eval.yaml:5-15]() | Evaluates arithmetic reasoning accuracy across models. |
| LM Eval Correctness | `test_lm_eval_correctness.py` [.buildkite/test_areas/lm_eval.yaml:106-118]() | Runs broader benchmark suites (MMLU, GSM8K, etc.) using configuration lists. |
| Quantized MoE / Fusions | `tests/quantization/test_blackwell_moe.py` [.buildkite/test_areas/quantization.yaml:87-118]() | Verifies quantized Mixture-of-Experts correctness on advanced hardware. |
| V1 Attention Backends | `tests/v1/attention/` [.buildkite/test_areas/attention.yaml:5-19]() | Validates correctness of FlashAttention, FlashInfer, MLA, and Triton attention backends. |

Sources: [.buildkite/test_areas/lm_eval.yaml:5-15](), [.buildkite/test_areas/lm_eval.yaml:106-118](), [.buildkite/test_areas/quantization.yaml:87-118](), [.buildkite/test_areas/attention.yaml:5-19]()

## 3. Benchmarking Tools Overview

### 3.1 Online Serving Benchmark: `vllm bench serve`

The online serving benchmark utility (`vllm/benchmarks/serve.py`) measures end-to-end throughput and latency against a running OpenAI-compatible vLLM server [vllm/benchmarks/serve.py:3-19](). 

Key mechanics include:
- **Server Model Discovery**: Automatically fetches served model IDs and roots via `get_first_model_from_server()` [vllm/benchmarks/serve.py:170-187]().
- **Prompt Tokenizer Alignment**: `_align_prompts_to_server_tokenizer()` probes the server's `/tokenize` and `/detokenize` endpoints to ensure local and server-side tokenization counts match, re-aligning prompts if discrepancies arise [vllm/benchmarks/serve.py:81-167]().
- **Request Dispatch**: Dispatches concurrent requests using `ASYNC_REQUEST_FUNCS` with Poisson request rates or bursty patterns [vllm/benchmarks/serve.py:45-53]().

### 3.2 Model Forward Benchmark: `vllm bench forward`

Defined in `vllm/benchmarks/forward/main.py` and documented in `docs/cli/README.md`, `vllm bench forward` bypasses the scheduler to benchmark exact-batch model forward passes as one-shot CUDA graphs [docs/cli/README.md:137-140](), [vllm/benchmarks/forward/main.py:3-14]().

- **Request Specifications**: Cases are defined as `[N*]Q[@K][c][:D]` where `Q` is query length, `K` is total KV length including query, `c` denotes chunked prefill, and `D` is draft tokens [docs/cli/README.md:137-140]().
- **Routing Fixtures**: Supports `--routing auto`, `real`, `balanced`, and `zipf` (for skewed synthetic MoE expert loads) [docs/benchmarking/cli.md:17-38](), [vllm/benchmarks/forward/main.py:68-76]().
- **Capture and Profiling**: Uses `ForwardBench` to capture execution graphs after JIT warmup, recording metrics such as `median_us`, `samples_us`, and kernel-level profiles via `--profile-dir` [docs/cli/README.md:139](), [vllm/benchmarks/forward/main.py:87-93]().

Sources: [docs/benchmarking/cli.md:17-38](), [vllm/benchmarks/serve.py:3-19](), [docs/cli/README.md:137-140](), [vllm/benchmarks/forward/main.py:3-14]()

### Serving Benchmark: Workflow Mapped to Code Entities

The following diagram illustrates the workflow of the online serving benchmark and its interaction with server endpoints and internal functions.

## 4. Benchmark Dataset Architecture

Benchmark data generation is managed via subclasses of `BenchmarkDataset` in `vllm/benchmarks/datasets/datasets.py` [vllm/benchmarks/datasets/datasets.py:3-11](), [vllm/benchmarks/datasets/datasets.py:99-102]().

- **`SampleRequest`**: Data class representing a single inference request, containing fields for `prompt`, `prompt_len`, `expected_output_len`, `multi_modal_data`, `lora_request`, `chat_messages`, and `request_overrides` [vllm/benchmarks/datasets/datasets.py:74-91]().
- **Supported Datasets**: Includes ShareGPT, ShareGPT4V/Video, BurstGPT, Random synthetic data, HuggingFace vision/audio/AIMO datasets, and custom JSONL inputs [docs/benchmarking/cli.md:62-87]().

Sources: [docs/benchmarking/cli.md:62-87](), [vllm/benchmarks/datasets/datasets.py:3-11](), [vllm/benchmarks/datasets/datasets.py:74-91](), [vllm/benchmarks/datasets/datasets.py:99-102]()

---

## 5. Sweep Tooling and Attention Benchmarks

### Attention Kernel Benchmark

Attention performance is validated using the attention kernel benchmark script located at `benchmarks/attention_benchmarks/benchmark.py` [docs/benchmarking/cli.md:46-48](). It evaluates backends such as `FLASH_ATTN` and `FLASHINFER` across various batch specifications (`--batch-specs`), returning exit codes indicating success (`0`) or configuration failure (`1`) [docs/benchmarking/cli.md:46-53]().

### Forward Microbenchmark Profiling

`vllm bench forward` includes integrated profiling via `--profile-dir` [docs/cli/README.md:139](), [vllm/benchmarks/forward/main.py:87-93](). It outputs Perfetto traces (`.trace.json.gz`) and kernel execution summaries (`.kernels.json`) which can be analyzed or compared using `python -m vllm.benchmarks.forward.profile` [docs/cli/README.md:139](), [vllm/benchmarks/forward/main.py:87-93]().

Sources: [docs/benchmarking/cli.md:46-53](), [docs/cli/README.md:139](), [vllm/benchmarks/forward/main.py:87-93]()

---

## 6. Batch Invariance and Determinism Validation

To guarantee reproducible generation and validate kernel correctness, vLLM supports deterministic execution modes. Forward benchmarks and test suites (such as `tests/benchmarks/test_forward_cli.py`) check graph determinism (`graph_deterministic`) and compare CUDA graph outputs against eager mode (`graph_vs_eager`) [tests/benchmarks/test_forward_cli.py:120-125]().

Sources: [tests/benchmarks/test_forward_cli.py:120-125]()

---

## 7. Model Comparison Framework

Model verification utilizes comparison harnesses (such as `VllmRunner` and `HfRunner`) to ensure that vLLM model implementations produce logits and generated tokens matching Hugging Face transformers references within tight numerical tolerances.

Sources: [.buildkite/test_areas/lm_eval.yaml:5-15]()

## Purpose and Scope

This page documents the developer tooling, automated quality checks, review assignments, AI agent instructions, and governance structures within the vLLM project. It covers pre-commit hooks, static analysis, GitHub Actions workflows, Mergify pull request automation, `.github/CODEOWNERS`, AI agent guidelines (`AGENTS.md`), and the project contribution and committer governance processes.

---

## Pre-commit Hooks

vLLM utilizes `pre-commit` hooks configured in [.pre-commit-config.yaml:1-172]() to maintain code quality, formatting, and consistency across Python, C++, CUDA, Markdown, shell scripts, and dependency definitions.

### Configuration and Hooks

The configuration defines global settings and individual hook repositories [.pre-commit-config.yaml:1-166]().

**Key Pre-commit Hooks:**

| Hook ID | Tool / Source | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ruff-check` & `ruff-format` | Astral Ruff [.pre-commit-config.yaml:10-15]() | Python linting, syntax checking, and auto-formatting |
| `typos` | Crate-CI typos [.pre-commit-config.yaml:16-20]() | Fast spell checking across source and documentation files |
| `clang-format` | Mirrors clang-format [.pre-commit-config.yaml:21-27]() | C++ and CUDA source code formatting |
| `markdownlint-cli2` | DavidAnson markdownlint-cli2 [.pre-commit-config.yaml:28-33]() | Markdown documentation linting (using `tools/pre_commit/.markdownlint.yaml`) [docs/contributing/README.md:93-96]() |
| `actionlint` | rhysd actionlint [.pre-commit-config.yaml:34-37]() | GitHub Actions workflow validation |
| `shellcheck` | shellcheck-py [.pre-commit-config.yaml:38-42]() | Shell script analysis (using `tools/pre_commit/.shellcheckrc`) [docs/contributing/README.md:93-95]() |
| `pip-compile` | Astral uv [.pre-commit-config.yaml:43-161]() | Requirement synchronization and hash generation for CUDA, ROCm, XPU, CPU, and docs |

Developers install and invoke pre-commit locally via [docs/contributing/README.md:86-104]():
```bash
uv pip install pre-commit>=4.5.1
pre-commit install
pre-commit run --all-files
```

Sources:
- [.pre-commit-config.yaml:1-172]()
- [docs/contributing/README.md:82-105]()

## Mypy Tooling and Static Analysis

Static type checking via `mypy` is integrated into pre-commit workflows. Global type checking rules and module-level overrides are defined in `pyproject.toml`.

### Implementation and Data Flow

To handle large codebases efficiently without import errors or excessive latency, vLLM configures strict checking rules (`check_untyped_defs = true`) while relaxing specific error codes for test suites (`tests.*`).

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["ChangedFilesInput"] --> B["group_files(changed_files)"];
    B --> C{"SilentGroupPatternMatch"};
    C -- "Yes" --> D["DefaultGroup[follow_imports=None]"];
    C -- "No" --> E{"SeparateGroupPatternMatch"};
    E -- "Yes" --> F["SeparateGroup[follow_imports='skip']"];
    E -- "No" --> G["DefaultGroup[follow_imports=None]"];
    D --> H["FileGroupsDict"];
    F --> H;
    G --> H;
    H --> I["main()"];
    I --> J["mypy(targets, python_version, follow_imports)"];
    J --> K["subprocess.run(['mypy', '--python-version', ...] + targets)"];
```
*Figure 1: Mypy file grouping and execution flow bridge from natural language requirements to `pyproject.toml` configurations and type-checking runners.*

Sources:
- [pyproject.toml:115-125]()
- [.github/workflows/pre-commit.yml:58]()

## GitHub Actions Workflows and CI Automation

vLLM relies on GitHub Actions workflows for continuous integration, issue triage, and build orchestration.

### Key Workflows

- **`pre-commit.yml`**: Runs pre-commit hooks on pull requests. It includes a `pre-run-check` job that validates PR authorship, verified labels, or a minimum threshold of 4 merged pull requests before triggering resource-intensive hooks [.github/workflows/pre-commit.yml:18-46]().
- **`issue_autolabel.yml`**: Automatically analyzes issue titles and bodies using keywords, substrings, and regular expressions via `actions/github-script` to assign triage labels (`rocm`, `cpu`, `kimi`, `quantization`, `intel-gpu`, `deepseek`, etc.) [.github/workflows/issue_autolabel.yml:1-110]().
- **`run-ci-command.yml`**: Authorizes and runs CI commands from PR comments [.github/workflows/run-ci-command.yml:1-54]().

### CI Command Automation (`run_ci_command.py`)

Authorized maintainers can trigger Buildkite CI pipelines using PR comment commands (such as `/ci run`). The automation is managed by `.github/workflows/scripts/run_ci_command.py` [docs/contributing/README.md:1-167]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["CommentEvent(/ci run)"] --> B["parse_command(comment_body)"];
    B --> C["GitHubClient.get_permission(actor)"];
    C --> D{"has_trusted_approval or TrustedPermission"};
    D -- "Yes" --> E["BuildkiteClient.create_build(payload)"];
    D -- "No" --> F["RejectCommand"];
    E --> G["Buildkite API Trigger Build"];
    F --> H["LogUnauthorized"];
```
*Figure 2: CI command authorization and dispatch flow bridging `.github/workflows/scripts/run_ci_command.py` classes `GitHubClient` and `BuildkiteClient`.*

Sources:
- [.github/workflows/pre-commit.yml:1-66]()
- [.github/workflows/issue_autolabel.yml:1-110]()
- [.github/workflows/scripts/run_ci_command.py:1-216]()
- [.github/workflows/run-ci-command.yml:1-54]()
