## Agent Skills and AI Contribution Guidelines

To maintain code quality when AI assistants contribute to vLLM, strict policies and agent instructions are defined in `AGENTS.md` and supported by agent skills [.agents/skills/pr-checklist/SKILL.md]().

### Core Policies

- **Duplicate-work checks**: Agents and contributors must verify existing issues and open pull requests before proposing new changes [AGENTS.md:8-16]().
- **No low-value busywork**: One-off PRs for tiny edits or isolated style tweaks are prohibited unless bundled with substantive work [AGENTS.md:21-24]().
- **Accountability**: Pure code-agent PRs are disallowed. A human submitter must review every line, run relevant tests, and include evaluation results for performance or model-affecting changes [AGENTS.md:25-33]().
- **Fail-closed behavior**: If work is duplicative or trivial, contributors must abort [AGENTS.md:39-41]().
- **Pr-checklist Skill**: Before opening a PR or requesting re-review, agents must execute the `.agents/skills/pr-checklist/SKILL.md` validation workflow [AGENTS.md:37]().

Sources:
- [AGENTS.md:1-163]()
- [.agents/skills/pr-checklist/SKILL.md:1-50]()

---

## Mergify Automation

Pull request automation is governed by `.github/mergify.yml` [.github/mergify.yml:1-228]().

### Key Rules

- **Documentation Labeling**: Automatically applies the `documentation` label and comments ReadTheDocs preview links on PRs modifying `docs/` or `examples/` [.github/mergify.yml:2-16]().
- **Recipe Labeling**: Automatically applies the `recipe` label and deployment preview links on PRs modifying `recipes/` [.github/mergify.yml:17-29]().
- **Pre-commit Failure Notifications**: Comments helpful instructions on PRs when the `pre-commit` check fails [.github/mergify.yml:30-54]().
- **DCO Failure Notifications**: Comments instructions when the DCO check fails [.github/mergify.yml:55-65]().
- **Component Labeling**: Automatically applies component and model labels (`ci/build`, `cohere`, `deepseek`, `frontend`, `pooling`, `rust`, `llama`, `multi-modality`, `mistral`, `new-model`) based on modified file paths or PR titles [.github/mergify.yml:66-228]().

Sources:
- [.github/mergify.yml:1-228]()

## Contribution and Governance Process

The vLLM contribution and governance model is detailed in community documentation and committer registries [docs/contributing/README.md:1-167](), [docs/governance/committers.md:1-108]().

### Governance Roles

- **Committers**: Individuals with write access responsible for reviewing, approving, and merging pull requests across core areas [docs/governance/committers.md:1-5](). Active committers include project leads [@WoosukKwon](https://github.com/WoosukKwon), [@youkaichao](https://github.com/youkaichao), and [@simon-mo](https://github.com/simon-mo), alongside specialized maintainers covering engine core, compilation, quantization, distributed execution, and hardware integrations [docs/governance/committers.md:7-70]().
- **Area Owners**: Designated domain experts who act as primary reviewers for specific subsystems (e.g., Scheduler, KV Cache Manager, AsyncLLM, ModelRunner/Executor/Worker) [docs/governance/committers.md:94-108]().

Sources:
- [docs/contributing/README.md:1-167]()
- [docs/governance/committers.md:1-108]()

This page defines codebase-specific terms, jargon, abbreviations, and domain concepts essential for onboarding engineers working on vLLM. It bridges high-level architectural concepts with concrete code entities, files, and classes across the repository.

---

## A

### Attention Backend
The specific implementation of the attention mechanism (e.g., FlashAttention, FlashInfer, Triton, or custom ROCm AITER/MLA kernels). vLLM selects an attention backend based on hardware platform, model architecture, and optimization configuration.

- **Implementation**: Managed via `AttentionBackend` and metadata builders such as `CommonAttentionMetadata` [vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py:123-130]().
- **Registry**: Backends are selected through the `AttentionBackendEnum` mapping [vllm/config/model.py:55-55]().
- **Integration**: Dispatches underlying hardware-accelerated attention operations during model execution.

Sources: [vllm/config/model.py:55-55](), [vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py:123-130]()

---

## B

### BlockPool
The physical memory manager responsible for allocating, recycling, and tracking fixed-size Key-Value (KV) cache blocks across devices (GPU, CPU offload tiers, or disk).

- **Implementation**: Backed by `KVCacheManager` and core scheduler integrations [vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py:40-40]().
- **Block Representation**: Individual memory segments are tracked via cache block structures and hash indices [vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py:42-42]().

Sources: [vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py:40-42]()

---

## C

### CompilationConfig
Configuration structure governing PyTorch's `torch.compile` (Dynamo + Inductor) pipeline, operator fusion passes, and CUDA graph capture scopes.

- **Definition**: Defined in `CompilationConfig` [vllm/config/vllm.py:35-37]().
- **Optimization Levels**: Controlled via `OptimizationLevel` (ranging from `O0` for no compilation/instant startup to `O2`/`O3` for full piecewise and complete CUDA graph capture) [vllm/config/vllm.py:158-171]().

Sources: [vllm/config/vllm.py:35-37](), [vllm/config/vllm.py:158-171]()

### CUDA Graph
An optimization technique that records sequences of CUDA kernel launches on the host and replays them with minimal CPU overhead during token decoding.

- **Modes**: Governed by `CUDAGraphMode` supporting execution semantics [vllm/config/vllm.py:38-38]().
- **Manager**: Coordinated via compilation and execution utilities handling batch descriptors and memory pools [vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py:114-119]().

Sources: [vllm/config/vllm.py:38-38](), [vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py:114-119]()

---

## D

### DSpark
A speculative decoding method specifically designed for Qwen3-Omni models. It utilizes a standalone draft checkpoint with a particular architecture (`Qwen3OmniDSparkModel`) and requires `num_speculative_tokens` to match the `block_size` trained into the draft model.

- **Validation**: `_validate_qwen3_omni_dspark` ensures the target model is a Qwen3-Omni variant and the draft model adheres to the DSpark contract [tests/test_config.py:51-51]().
- **Configuration**: `SpeculativeConfig` defines `DSparkModelTypes` and `SpeculativeMethod` to enable this feature [vllm/config/speculative.py:81-93]().

Sources: [tests/test_config.py:51-51](), [vllm/config/speculative.py:81-93]()

---

## E

### EngineCore
The core asynchronous execution orchestrator in vLLM's V1 engine architecture. It manages request queues, scheduling rounds, block allocation, and coordinates model runners.

- **Scheduler Integration**: Works tightly with `Scheduler` to admit, schedule, and preempt requests [vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py:86-100]().
- **Request Lifecycle**: Processes request state transitions from waiting to running and finished [tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py:62-62]().

Sources: [vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py:86-100](), [tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py:62-62]()

### EPLB (Expert Placement Load Balancing)
A specialized load-balancing subsystem for Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models that redistributes experts across data-parallel ranks to prevent computational hot-spotting.

- **Controller**: Managed via `EPLBController` and state structures within worker execution loops [vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py:125-125]().

Sources: [vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py:125-125]()

---

## F

### FusedMoE
An optimized implementation of Mixture-of-Experts layers that fuses the router dispatch logic and expert GEMM operations into high-performance custom kernels.

- **Integration**: Invoked via model definition layers and configuration options [vllm/engine/arg_utils.py:87-87]().

Sources: [vllm/engine/arg_utils.py:87-87]()

---

## K

### KV Cache Manager
The subsystem coordinating KV cache layout, allocation strategies, prefix caching hashing, and block tables.

- **Manager**: Implemented through `KVCacheManager` [vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py:40-40]().
- **Utilities**: Employs block hash indexing and block state management [vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py:40-42]().

Sources: [vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py:40-42]()

---

## M

### MLA (Multi-Latent Attention)
An attention architecture used in models like DeepSeek-V3/V4 that compresses Key-Value representations into lower-dimensional latent vectors to drastically reduce memory footprint and bandwidth during prefill and decode.

- **Metadata & Backends**: Supported by specialized attention metadata builders and flashinfer/sparse MLA backends [vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py:123-130]().

Sources: [vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py:123-130]()

### ModelConfig
The core configuration container specifying model weights, tokenizer settings, runner types, and architecture flags.

- **Definition**: Encapsulated by `ModelConfig` [vllm/config/model.py:152-154]().
- **Model Registry**: `_TEXT_GENERATION_MODELS` maps Hugging Face model architecture names to their vLLM implementations [vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py:73-75]().
- **Transformers Backend**: Allows using models implemented in Hugging Face Transformers directly, configurable via `model_impl="transformers"` [docs/models/supported_models.md:43-46]().

Sources: [vllm/config/model.py:152-154](), [vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py:73-75](), [docs/models/supported_models.md:43-46]()

---

## O

### OptimizationLevel
An enumeration defining different levels of optimization applied to the vLLM engine, primarily affecting compilation and CUDA graph usage.

- **Levels**:
    - `O0`: No optimization, immediate startup [vllm/config/vllm.py:160-163]().
    - `O1`: Quick optimizations, Dynamo+Inductor compilation, piecewise CUDA graphs [vllm/config/vllm.py:164-166]().
    - `O2`: Full optimizations, includes `O1` plus full and piecewise CUDA graphs [vllm/config/vllm.py:167-168]().
    - `O3`: Currently same as `O2` [vllm/config/vllm.py:169-170]().
- **Definition**: `OptimizationLevel` [vllm/config/vllm.py:158-159]().

Sources: [vllm/config/vllm.py:158-171]()

---

## P

### PerformanceMode
A literal type defining high-level performance profiles for the vLLM engine.

- **Modes**:
    - `"balanced"`: A general-purpose mode.
    - `"interactivity"`: Prioritizes low latency for interactive use cases.
    - `"throughput"`: Optimizes for maximum token generation rate.
- **Definition**: `PerformanceMode` [vllm/config/vllm.py:173-173]().

Sources: [vllm/config/vllm.py:173-173]()

---

## S

### Scheduler
The core component responsible for managing the lifecycle of requests, allocating KV cache blocks, and determining which requests run in each iteration.

- **Initialization**: `Scheduler` is initialized with configuration objects like `VllmConfig`, `KVCacheConfig`, and `StructuredOutputManager` [vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py:86-97]().
- **Scheduling Logic**: Implements policies for preemption, token budget management, and handling multimodal inputs [vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py:130-161]().

Sources: [vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py:86-97](), [vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py:130-161]()

### Speculative Decoding
A technique to accelerate LLM inference by using a smaller, faster draft model to predict a sequence of tokens, which are then verified by the larger target model.

- **Configuration**: `SpeculativeConfig` defines parameters such as the method (`ngram`, `draft_model`, `dspark`, `eagle`, etc.), number of speculative tokens, and rejection sampling strategy [vllm/config/speculative.py:85-93]().

Sources: [vllm/config/speculative.py:85-93]()

### KV Cache Architecture
Relating logical caching concepts to the physical block pool and management classes.

```mermaid

        PhysicalMem["PhysicalGPUBlocks"]
    end

    subgraph "CodeEntities"
        CacheCfg["CacheConfig (vllm/config/cache.py)"]

    end

    CacheCfg -->|"Configures"| Mgr
    Mgr -->|"Allocates"| Block
    LogicalCache -.-> Mgr
    PhysicalMem -.-> Block
```

## Technical Terms Table

| Term | Definition | Code Pointer |
|---|---|---|
| **TP (Tensor Parallelism)** | Sharding weights across multiple devices horizontally. | `ParallelConfig` [vllm/config/vllm.py:59-59]() |
| **PP (Pipeline Parallelism)** | Partitioning layers sequentially across devices. | `ParallelConfig` [vllm/config/vllm.py:59-59]() |
| **VllmConfig** | Root configuration object unifying all sub-configs. | `VllmConfig` [vllm/config/vllm.py:34-34]() |
| **CompilationMode** | Strategy for `torch.compile` integration (`NONE`, `VLLM_COMPILE`, etc.). | `CompilationMode` [vllm/config/compilation.py:37-37]() |
| **CUDAGraphMode** | Granularity of CUDA graph capture (`NONE`, `PIECEWISE`, `FULL`). | `CUDAGraphMode` [vllm/config/compilation.py:38-38]() |
| **Scheduler** | Core token scheduler managing admission and batches. | `Scheduler` [vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py:86-86]() |
| **GPUModelRunner** | Coordinates execution pipeline, attention, and sampling on GPU. | `GPUModelRunner` [vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py:123-130]() |
